### [`v83.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/releases/tag/v83.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/compare/v82.0.0...v83.0.0)

I don't recall ever having this many breaking API changes in a single release, and the last release was only 3 weeks ago!

A special heart-felt thanks goes to [@​merchantmoh-debug](https://redirect.github.com/merchantmoh-debug), [@​Not-Dhananjay-Mishra](https://redirect.github.com/Not-Dhananjay-Mishra), and [@​alexandear](https://redirect.github.com/alexandear) for the addition of a long-requested feature to this repo:

- native auto-generated iterators for all `List*` methods that support pagination (change your call from `List*` to `List*Iter` and make sure to use a rate-limiting transport or you will quickly exhaust your quotas!)

A second set of heart-felt thanks go to [@​stevehipwell](https://redirect.github.com/stevehipwell) for setting up our REVIEWERS file and to our amazing volunteer reviewers:

- [@​stevehipwell](https://redirect.github.com/stevehipwell)
- [@​alexandear](https://redirect.github.com/alexandear)
- [@​zyfy29](https://redirect.github.com/zyfy29)
- [@​Not-Dhananjay-Mishra](https://redirect.github.com/Not-Dhananjay-Mishra)

who have reduced our code-review wait times from days (*sometimes weeks*) down to literally ***hours*** and thereby enable rapid responses to bug fixes and attempts to stay up-to-date with the ever-evolving GitHub v3 API.

This release contains the following breaking API changes:

- fix!: Divide `PackageGetAllVersions` into two separate methods `ListPackageVersions` and `ListUserPackageVersions` ([#​4014](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/4014))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `PackageGetAllVersions` is now divided into `ListPackageVersions` and `ListUserPackageVersions`.
- fix!: Remove unsupported pagination from `ListAutolinks` ([#​4012](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/4012))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `opts *ListOptions` is removed from `RepositoriesService.ListAutoLinks`.
- fix!: Remove `ListOptions` from `PullRequestsService.ListReviewers` ([#​4009](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/4009))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `PullRequestsService.ListReviewers` no longer has `opts *ListOptions`.
- fix!: Change `PremiumRequestUsageItem` quantities to `float64` ([#​4002](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/4002))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `PremiumRequestUsageItem` numeric fields are now `float64`.
- fix!: Add `ListOptions` to `ListDeploymentBranchPolicies` and `ListCustomDeploymentRuleIntegrations` ([#​3988](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3988))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `RepositoriesService.ListDeploymentBranchPolicies` and `RepositoriesService.ListCustomDeploymentRuleIntegrations` now accept `ListOptions`.
- fix!: Pass `url` struct tags by value instead of by reference ([#​3991](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3991))
  BREAKING CHANGE: Many `*Options` structs now pass `omitempty` URL struct fields by value instead of by reference.
- fix!: Fix pagination support for `IssuesService` list methods ([#​3984](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3984))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `ListCursorOptions` is removed from `IssueListOptions`.
- fix!: Add field `PerPage` to `OrganizationsListOptions` ([#​3986](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3986))

- fix!: Add `ListLicensesOptions` to `LicensesService.List` ([#​3981](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3981))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `LicensesService.List` now accepts `ListLicensesOptions` for pagination.
- fix!: Change `SCIMEnterpriseAttributeOperation.Value` from `*string` to `any` ([#​3971](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3971))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `SCIMEnterpriseAttributeOperation.Value` is changed from `*string` to `any`.
- feat!: Add `ListOptions` to `RepositoriesService.ListAllTopics` ([#​3978](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3978))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `RepositoriesService.ListAllTopics` now accepts `ListOptions` for pagination.
- fix!: Replace `UserListOptions.ListOptions` with `UserListOptions.PerPage` ([#​3977](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3977))
  BREAKING CHANGE: Replaces `UserListOptions.ListOptions` with `UserListOptions.PerPage` which also removes `UsersService.ListAllIter`.
- fix!: `CreateHostedRunnerRequest`, `UpdateHostedRunnerRequest` instead of `HostedRunnerRequest` ([#​3973](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3973))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `ActionsService.CreateHostedRunner` and `EnterpriseService.CreateHostedRunner` now accept `CreateHostedRunnerRequest`; `ActionsService.UpdateHostedRunner` and `EnterpriseService.UpdateHostedRunner` now accept `UpdateHostedRunnerRequest`.
- refactor!: Use `RepositoryPermissions` struct for `User.Permissions` ([#​3963](https://redirect.github.com/google/go-github/issues/3963))
  BREAKING CHANGE: `User.Permissions` is now `*RepositoryPermissions` instead of `map[string]bool`.

items.title: fix(ci): eliminate pull_request_target ACE in check-registry-diff
items.body:
## Description

Replaces the vulnerable `registry-diff` job in `check-registry-diff.yaml` with a safe two-workflow artifact bridge pattern.

**The vulnerability**: The `registry-diff` job triggered on `pull_request_target` (base repo privileges, `pull-requests: write` token) and explicitly checked out fork code with `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}`, then executed `make weaver-install` and `make semantic-conventions/diff` from the attacker's Makefile. Any GitHub user could trigger this by opening a fork PR touching `pkg/instrumentation/**/semconv/**` or `.semconv-version`, achieving arbitrary code execution and GITHUB_TOKEN exfiltration for PR comment manipulation.

This is the same class of vulnerability exploited by the HackerBot-CLAW campaign against open source GitHub Actions workflows.

## Motivation

Closes the attack surface by splitting the job across a trust boundary:

- **`generate-registry-diff.yaml`** — runs on `pull_request` (fork PRs get a read-only sandbox token). Generates the diff from PR code, saves `pr-number.txt` + `semconv-version.txt` + diff markdown as artifacts. No write access.
- **`comment-registry-diff.yaml`** — runs on `workflow_run` (trusted base-repo context). Downloads the artifact, validates the PR number against `^[0-9]+$` and version against `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`, then posts the PR comment. Never executes any fork code.
- **`check-registry-diff.yaml`** — `pull_request_target` trigger, `pull-requests: write` permission, `env:` block, and the entire `registry-diff` job removed. The `registry-check` job is untouched.

Fixes #<!-- issue number -->

items.title: fix(test): missing go.sum entries in test apps cause integration test failure locally
items.body:
## Description

`make test-integration` fails locally with `TestGRPCClient` due to missing `go.sum` entries in `test/apps/grpcclient` and `test/apps/grpcserver`.

```
failed to run build plan:
../../../../../go/pkg/mod/google.golang.org/grpc@v1.78.0/internal/tcp_keepalive_unix.go:27:2:
missing go.sum entry for module providing package golang.org/x/sys/unix
(imported by google.golang.org/grpc/internal); to add:
    go get google.golang.org/grpc/internal@v1.78.0
```

## Root cause

The `go.sum` files in `test/apps/grpcclient` and `test/apps/grpcserver` have been incomplete since they were first introduced in #274. They include the hash for `golang.org/x/sys v0.39.0` but are missing the hash for the `golang.org/x/sys/unix` subpackage, which is transitively required by `google.golang.org/grpc@v1.78.0`. This suggests `go mod tidy` was not run (or not run completely) before committing.

## Why CI may still pass

CI runners likely have a warm Go module cache from prior workflow runs, which already contains the required module hashes. This allows the build to succeed without consulting the `go.sum` file for those specific entries. On a fresh clone with a clean module cache, Go strictly enforces that every transitive dependency has a matching `go.sum` entry, causing the failure.

## Fix

Run `go mod tidy` in the affected test app directories:

```sh
cd test/apps/grpcclient && go mod tidy
cd test/apps/grpcserver && go mod tidy
```

It may also be worth auditing all `test/apps/*/go.sum` files for similar staleness, and considering adding a CI step or Makefile target that verifies `go mod tidy` produces no diff across all modules.

items.title: Add pos field to InstRawRule forcustomizable injection position
items.body:
**1. Background**

Currently, an `InstRawRule` is defined with the following structure:

```yaml
raw_helloworld:
  target: main
  func: Example
  raw: |
    go func(){
      h := sha256.New()
      h.Write([]byte("RawCode"))
      fmt.Printf("RawCode: %x\n", h.Sum(nil))
    }()
  imports:
    fmt: "fmt"
    sha256: "crypto/sha256"
```

This configuration injects the code snippet from the `raw` field at the very beginning (the entry point) of the target function, such as `main.Example()`. The injection position is not customizable.

**2. Proposal**

I propose introducing a new optional field named `pos`. This field will allow users to specify a precise injection point within the function body using a regular expression.

When the `pos` field is present, the instrumenter will search for the first line in the function that matches the regex and inject the code snippet **before** that line. If `pos` is omitted, the behavior defaults to injecting at the function's entry point, preserving backward compatibility.

**3. Example Usage**

Consider the following target function:

```go
func Example(){
  a()
  b()
  c()
}
```

To inject code before the call to `b()`, the configuration would be:

```yaml
my_rule:
  target: main
  func: Example
  pos: "b\\(\\)" # Inject before the line matching b()
  raw: |
    // ... your code snippet ...
```

Similarly, `pos: "a\\(\\)"` would inject the code before `a()`.

<summary>actions/download-artifact (actions/download-artifact)</summary>

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v8.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7.0.0...v8.0.0)

##### v8 - What's new

##### Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in `actions/upload-artifact`, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the `Content-Type` header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new `skip-decompress` parameter to `false`.

##### Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the `digest-mismatch` parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to `error` which will fail the workflow run.

##### ESM

To support new versions of the @​actions/\* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

##### What's Changed

- Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by [@​danwkennedy](https://redirect.github.com/danwkennedy) in [#​460](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/460)

items.title: Automatically detect imports in hook code
items.body:
PR #283 allows us to import arbitrary packages in our hook code using the imports directive, like so:

```yaml
hook_with_imports:
  target: main
  func: Example
  before: MyHookBefore
  path: "github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/instrumentation/helloworld"
  imports:
    log: "log"        # Additional import needed by the hook
    _: "unsafe"       # Blank import if needed
```

I propose that we add a new capability to automatically analyze the dependencies of the MyHookBefore file. This would eliminate the need to manually add the imports field, which is a rather brittle and tedious approach.

items.title: nit: Consider `fasttemplate` as a replacement for `text/template`
items.body:
nit: Consider [`fasttemplate`](https://github.com/valyala/fasttemplate) as a replacement for `text/template` here. For single-variable substitution (`{{ . }}` → a string), `fasttemplate` is up to 10x faster because it avoids the full template engine parse/execute overhead. Since `CompileExpression` is called once per matched call site during compilation, the impact is minor today, but it would simplify the implementation — `fasttemplate` substitution is a single `ExecuteString` call with no need for the `_.PLACEHOLDER_0` sentinel pattern.

_Originally posted by @kakkoyun in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pull/279#discussion_r2910898932_

items.title: fix(instrument): clone args slice before mutation in stripCompleteFlag
items.body:
## Summary

`stripCompleteFlag` in `toolexec.go` modified the caller-supplied `args` slice
in-place by appending to it after a `slices.Delete`. Because `slices.Delete`
can shift elements within the same backing array, subsequent iterations or
callers could observe a corrupted view of the original slice.

- Add `slices.Clone` before the `append`/delete loop so all mutations happen on
  an owned copy, leaving the input unchanged.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test -count=1 -race ./tool/...` passes
- [ ] `golangci-lint run` passes
items.author: kakkoyun

items.title: fix(instrumentation): replace unsafe string/byte conversions in Redis hooks
items.body:
## Summary

The Redis v9 hook used `unsafe.Pointer` to reinterpret a `[]byte` as a `string` and vice versa, bypassing Go's memory model. While this pattern can work, it is undefined behaviour per the Go spec and breaks under the race detector and future GC improvements.

- Replace `*(*string)(unsafe.Pointer(&b))` with `string(b)`.
- Replace `*(*[]byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&s))` with `[]byte(s)`.
- Remove the now-unused `unsafe` import.

The safe conversions allocate a copy; for hook code this is acceptable and the clarity and correctness benefit outweighs the minor cost.

**Behavioral change**: `ProcessHook` now propagates `redis.Nil` errors unchanged instead of suppressing them, allowing callers to distinguish between actual errors and cache misses. `ProcessPipelineHook` applies the same treatment for pipeline commands.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test -count=1 -race ./pkg/instrumentation/redis/...` passes
- [ ] `golangci-lint run` passes (no `gosec` warnings)
items.author: kakkoyun

items.title: fix(setup): use cancellation context from errgroup in match.go
items.body:
## Summary

`errgroup.WithContext` returns a derived context that is cancelled when
the first goroutine in the group returns an error. The previous code
discarded that context and continued to pass the original parent context
to downstream calls, so cooperative cancellation never fired on error.

- Thread the `ctx` returned by `errgroup.WithContext` through to the
  goroutines it manages.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test -count=1 -race ./tool/...` passes
- [ ] `golangci-lint run` passes

items.title: test(pkg/instrumentation): improve test practices
items.body:
## Summary

Several test files in `pkg/instrumentation/` had minor but meaningful issues:

- Helper functions missing `t.Helper()`, causing failure lines to point
  at the helper body instead of the call site.
- `defer tp.Shutdown(...)` used at test function level — defers run when
  the enclosing function returns, not when a subtest completes, leaving
  the provider alive across subtests and causing interference.
- Replaced `defer tp.Shutdown` with `t.Cleanup(func() { _ = tp.Shutdown(...) })`
  so cleanup is scoped to the subtest.

items.title: fix(instrumentation): fix concurrency issues in shared setup
items.body:
## Summary

`pkg/instrumentation/shared/setup.go` had two concurrency defects:

1. **Local-error bug in `sync.Once.Do`**: errors assigned inside `Do`'s
   closure to a local variable were invisible to callers after the first
   invocation because `sync.Once` caches nothing — only the execution.
   Replaced with `sync.OnceValue` (Go 1.21), which caches the return
   value and returns it on every subsequent call.

2. **Goroutine leak in `setupSignalHandler`**: the goroutine blocked
   forever on a channel that was never closed. Added context-based
   cancellation so the goroutine exits cleanly when the application shuts
   down.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test -count=1 -race ./pkg/instrumentation/shared/...` passes
- [ ] `golangci-lint run` passes

## Why now

Identified as part of a pre-existing-issues audit of the `main` branch.

## Summary

Storing `context.Context` in a struct is a Go anti-pattern
(https://pkg.go.dev/context#pkg-overview): contexts are request-scoped
and should flow through call chains as the first function parameter.

- Remove the `ctx` field from the instrumentation struct in
  `tool/internal/instrument/toolexec.go`.
- Pass `ctx` explicitly to each method that needs it.

items.title: refactor: modernize Go idioms (interface{} → any, slices.Sort)
items.body:
## Summary

Go 1.18 introduced `any` as a built-in alias for `interface{}`. Using
`any` is now the idiomatic spelling; the old form is still valid but
considered dated.

- Replace all `interface{}` occurrences with `any` across `pkg/`,
  `tool/`, and `demo/` sources.
- Update `ast.IsInterfaceType()` to recognise both `*dst.InterfaceType`
  and `*dst.Ident{Name:"any"}` so trampoline generation handles hook
  parameters written with either spelling.
- Extend the sentinel check in `trampoline.go` for both `"interface{}"`
  and `"any"` so the pointer-to-interface guard fires for hooks that use
  the modern alias.
- Regenerate all golden test files via `make test-unit/update-golden`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test -count=1 -race ./tool/...` passes
- [ ] `go test -count=1 -race ./pkg/...` (per module) passes
- [ ] `golangci-lint run` passes

## Why now

items.title: chore(ci): add consistency checks for api.tmpl sync and golden files
items.body:
## Summary

Two new checks prevent classes of drift that have caused test failures
in the past:

**`check-api-sync`** — verifies that `tool/internal/instrument/api.tmpl`
is byte-for-byte identical to `pkg/inst/context.go`. The Makefile keeps
them in sync via `cp` during `make build`, but direct edits to `api.tmpl`
are silently overwritten on the next build. A CI check makes the contract
explicit and catches drift immediately.

**`check-golden-files`** — regenerates the testdata golden files and
asserts `git diff` is empty. The existing unit tests already fail when
golden files are stale, but the error message is cryptic. This check
surfaces a clear "golden files are stale — run `make test-unit/update-golden`"
message as a distinct CI step.

Both checks are also available as Makefile targets for local use:
```
make check-api-sync
make check-golden-files
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `make check-api-sync` passes locally
- [ ] CI `check-consistency` workflow runs on PRs touching Go sources
- [ ] Intentionally mismatching `api.tmpl` and `pkg/inst/context.go`
  causes `check-api-sync` to fail with a useful diff

items.title: On-going performance benchmarking (overhead vs. vanilla Go)
items.body:
Contributing to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/261

CI/CD: On-going performance benchmarking (overhead vs. vanilla Go)

---

Proposal: add a CI benchmark that tracks compile times for our demo apps over time.
	•	Run in a clean/isolated environment (pinned Go version, consistent machine/runner).
	•	Measure compile time for the same program using:
	1.	plain go toolchain (baseline)
	2.	otelc (instrumented)
	•	Execute each benchmark N times (we can use Go’s native benchmarking harness to reduce noise).
	•	Store results somewhere persistent (details TBD).
	•	Analyze trends over time and define a regression threshold.

Automation idea: a GitHub Action evaluates the latest run vs. historical baseline:
	•	If there’s a statistically significant regression: automatically open (or update) an issue and block the next release until it’s triaged.
	•	If the regression is expected (known change): document it and close/annotate the alert.

- `go.mod` / `go.sum` / `go.work` / `go.work.sum` — restored from `.otel-build/backup/` if backups exist

The cleanup is **idempotent** and **best-effort**: individual step failures are logged as warnings and do not abort the rest of the cleanup.

Also refactors `GoBuild()` to reuse `Cleanup()` instead of an inline defer block, eliminating duplication.

## Motivation

The setup and build phases create temporary files and modify `go.mod`/`go.sum`. Previously, cleanup only happened as a `defer` inside `GoBuild()`. If a build failed mid-way, or if `otel setup` was run independently, these artifacts were left behind with no way to clean them up short of manual deletion.

The UX design doc (`docs/ux-design.md`, "Clean-Room Usage" section) explicitly describes this use case: users who want to apply compile-time instrumentation without any persistent modifications to the codebase.

Fixes #96

items.title: fix(tool): restore modified files when build is interrupted
items.body:
## Description

Wraps the root context with `signal.NotifyContext` so that `SIGINT` (Ctrl-C) and `SIGTERM` cancel the context rather than terminating the process immediately. Adds `defer stop()` to release the signal handler when the program exits normally.

```go
ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
defer stop()
```

## Motivation

When a user interrupts `otelc go build` mid-run, the process was killed abruptly, leaving source files in a modified/partially-instrumented state. The cleanup logic (restore backups, remove generated files) lived inside a `defer` in `GoBuild`, so it would run correctly on a normal return — but never ran on an abrupt signal-kill.

`signal.NotifyContext` is the idiomatic Go solution: the signal cancels the context, `exec.CommandContext` kills subprocesses, `GoBuild` returns with a context error, and the existing `defer` restores files. No change to the cleanup logic itself is required.

Fixes #228

items.title: feat(tool): named declaration join point
items.body:
## Description

This PR adds a new `declaration_of` join point that allows instrumentation rules to target **named top-level declarations** (variables, constants, functions, and types) in a package, and apply actions such as assigning a new value to a `var` or `const`.

- Introduces `InstDeclRule` with the `declaration_of` YAML key as the new join point
- Adds `value` advice for replacing the initializer of a matched `var` or `const`
- Adds `FindVarDecl`, `FindConstDecl`, `FindTypeDecl`, and `FindNamedDecl` to the AST utilities, refactoring the existing `FindStructDecl` on top of them
- Includes golden tests covering the `assign_value` use case

### Rule Format Example

```yaml
assign_default_transport:
  target: net/http
  kind: var
  identifier: DefaultTransport
  value: |
    &http.Transport{MaxIdleConns: 100}
  imports:
    http: "net/http"
```

`identifier` is the name of the top-level symbol to match. `kind` optionally constrains the kind (`func`, `var`, `const`, `type`, or empty to match any).

### Implementation Details

- **`tool/internal/rule/decl_rule.go`** — defines `InstDeclRule`, loading/validation logic, and the set of valid `kind` values. Validation rejects `value` when `kind` is `func` or `type`, as those kinds have no initializer to replace.
- **`tool/internal/ast/shared.go`** — adds `FindVarDecl`, `FindConstDecl`, `FindTypeDecl`, and `FindNamedDecl`. `FindStructDecl` is preserved for backwards compatibility and now delegates to `FindTypeDecl`.
- **`tool/internal/instrument/apply_decl.go`** — implements `applyDeclRule`: resolves the declaration with `FindNamedDecl`, parses the `value` expression by wrapping it in a temporary `var` declaration, then replaces the `ValueSpec.Values` slice in the matched node. Imports declared in the rule are injected as with other rule types.
- **`tool/internal/setup/match.go`** — wires `InstDeclRule` into the rule-matching pipeline.

### Design Philosophy

The declaration join point complements existing function-hook and struct-field rules. Where those rules target function bodies or struct layouts, `declaration_of` targets the initialization state of package-level symbols—useful for overriding default values in third-party packages (e.g., replacing a default HTTP transport, toggling a package-level flag, or substituting a registered implementation) without modifying the package source.

## Motivation

Implements OP3.2 from #277.

items.title: feat(tool): value declaration join point
items.body:
## Description

Adds the **`value_declaration` join point** (OP3.3 from #277), which targets package-level `var` and `const` declarations by their *declared type* rather than by name.

This complements the `declaration` join point from the parent branch: where `declaration_of` pins a specific named declaration, `value_declaration` targets all declarations of a given type across the package — useful for overriding feature flags, replacing interface implementations, or injecting defaults wherever a particular type is declared.

Assisted-By: `claude-sonnet-4-6`

### What's included

- **New rule type: `value_declaration`** (`rule/value_decl_rule.go`) — matches all package-level `var`/`const` declarations whose annotated type matches a given type expression and replaces their initializer with `assign_value`. Supports built-in types (`bool`, `string`), fully-qualified types (`net/http.Client`), and pointer types (`*net/http.Request`). The type string is parsed into components (pointer flag, import path, identifier) once at construction time.

- **Type matching** (`instrument/apply_value_decl.go`) — `matchesType` handles pointer wrapping, qualified selectors, and plain identifiers. Import alias resolution reuses `collectImportAliases` and is skipped entirely for built-in types (no import path to resolve).

- **`matchesQualifiedSelector`** (`apply_call_helpers.go`) — the `pkg.Name` selector-resolution logic (`ident.Path` first, then alias map fallback) was duplicated between `matchesCallRule` and the new `matchesType`. It is extracted into a shared helper used by both.

- **Retroactive test coverage for `declaration_of`** — `decl_rule_test.go` and `apply_decl_test.go` were missing from the parent branch and are added here, covering rule construction/validation and the `applyDeclRule` apply function.

- **Setup integration** — `preciseMatching` registers `InstValueDeclRule` unconditionally for all source files in a matched package (type resolution requires import aliases, which are only available at instrumentation time); files with no matching declarations are a silent no-op.

- **Improved `FindNamedDecl` documentation** — the docstring now spells out the non-uniform concrete return type per `kind` value (`*dst.FuncDecl` / `*dst.ValueSpec` / `*dst.GenDecl`), avoiding future type-assertion surprises.

- **Golden test** (`testdata/golden/value-decl-rule/`) and unit tests (`value_decl_rule_test.go`, `apply_value_decl_test.go`).

### Rule format

```yaml
override_feature_flags:
  target: mypackage
  value_declaration: "bool"        # built-in type
  assign_value: "true"

replace_transport:
  target: net/http
  value_declaration: "*net/http.Transport"   # pointer to qualified type
  assign_value: "&http.Transport{MaxIdleConns: 100}"
  imports:
    http: "net/http"
```

### Rule fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value_declaration` | string | yes | Type expression: `bool`, `pkg/path.Type`, `*pkg/path.Type` |
| `assign_value` | string | yes | Go expression assigned to every matched declaration |
| `imports` | map[string]string | no | Extra imports needed by the injected expression |

### Limitations

- Only declarations with an **explicit type annotation** are matched — untyped declarations such as `const x = true` are skipped by design.
- `assign_value` for multi-name specs (`var a, b T = ...`) assigns the same expression (cloned) to every name in the spec.

## Motivation

Implements OP3.3 from #277. Builds on the `declaration_of` join point from the parent branch.

Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.79.3

Security

  • server: fix an authorization bypass where malformed :path headers (missing the leading slash) could bypass path-based restricted "deny" rules in interceptors like grpc/authz. Any request with a non-canonical path is now immediately rejected with an Unimplemented error. (#8981)

Release 1.79.2

  • stats: Prevent redundant error logging in health/ORCA producers by skipping stats/tracing processing when no stats handler is configured. (grpc/grpc-go#8874)

Release 1.79.1

Release 1.79.0

API Changes

  • mem: Add experimental API SetDefaultBufferPool to change the default buffer pool. (#8806)
    • Special Thanks: @​vanja-p
  • experimental/stats: Update MetricsRecorder to require embedding the new UnimplementedMetricsRecorder (a no-op struct) in all implementations for forward compatibility. (#8780)

Behavior Changes

  • balancer/weightedtarget: Remove handling of Addresses and only handle Endpoints in resolver updates. (#8841)

New Features

  • experimental/stats: Add support for asynchronous gauge metrics through the new AsyncMetricReporter and RegisterAsyncReporter APIs. (#8780)
  • pickfirst: Add support for weighted random shuffling of endpoints, as described in gRFC A113.
    • This is enabled by default, and can be turned off using the environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_PF_WEIGHTED_SHUFFLING. (#8864)

items.title: feat(tool): metaprogramming annotations (magical comments; directives)
items.body:
## Description

Adds a new **Directive Rule** — a join point that matches AST nodes annotated with magic comments (e.g., `//dd:span span.name:"my operation"`). This is a **pure filter** with no advice: it matches during the setup phase but performs no AST transformation during instrumentation. It becomes useful when `all-of` combinators land, allowing directive annotations to be combined with other join points.

### What's included

- **New rule type: `directive`** — matches source files containing a `//directive` comment. The directive name is specified without the `//` prefix. Validation rejects empty directives, directives with spaces, and directives that start with `//`.

- **Directive matching** (`matchDirective`) — validates that the comment is a line comment (not block), has no space after `//`, matches the full directive name (not a prefix), and requires whitespace after the name if arguments follow. Ports the matching semantics from Orchestrion's `directive.matches`.

- **Argument parsing** (`ParseDirectiveArgs`, `scanArgs`, `tokenize`) — parses `key:value` arguments from directive comments. Values may be Go double-quoted strings (handled via `strconv.Unquote`). Single quotes and malformed input are rejected. This infrastructure is ready for use when combinators wire directive args into the instrument phase.

- **Setup integration** — `createRuleFromFields` dispatches on the `directive` YAML key. `preciseMatching` uses a lazy-loaded `os.ReadFile` + `bytes.Contains` pre-filter (since `ParseFileFast` skips comments, the raw bytes are needed).

- **Instrument phase** — directive rules are intentionally **excluded from `groupRules`** to avoid a wasted parse+write cycle for files that only have directive rules (no AST transformation to apply).

- **Tests** — unit tests for matching (10 cases), arg parsing (9 cases), directive args (3 cases), rule validation (5 cases), rule factory (2 cases), `TestGroupRules` exclusion, and a golden integration test.

### Rule format

```yaml
my_directive_rule:
  target: main
  directive: "otelc:span"
```

### Rule fields

| Field       | Type   | Required | Description |
|-------------|--------|----------|-------------|
| `directive` | string | yes      | Directive name to match (without `//`) |

### Design decisions

- **Pure filter, no advice** — no `before`/`after`/`assign_value` fields. The rule only participates in setup-phase matching.
- **`bytes.Contains` pre-filter** — a loose but fast check on raw file bytes. False positives (e.g., the directive appearing inside a string literal) are acceptable because the precise `matchDirective` function will be used for real matching when combinators land.
- **Excluded from `groupRules`** — since `applyDirectiveRule` would be a no-op, directive rules don't enter the instrument phase's file-processing loop, avoiding unnecessary AST parse+write cycles.

## Motivation

Implements the Orchestrion-equivalent `directive` join point for compile-time instrumentation. This is a prerequisite for the `all-of` combinator feature, which will allow rules like "instrument functions annotated with `//dd:span`" by combining directive matching with function join points.

Design follows feedback on Orchestrion PR https://github.com/DataDog/orchestrion/pull/665 regarding Go double-quoted string support for directive argument values.

items.body:
## Description

Adopts the 2-tier \`where\`/\`do\` rule schema agreed in the design discussion on this PR. This is branch 0 of the OP4 stack (#381–#386).

Top-level \`target\` + \`version\` scope the package. \`where\` carries all non-package selectors (point selectors + \`where.file\` for file-level predicates; implicit \`all-of\` at the top, with \`one-of\`/\`not\` as named sub-groups). \`do\` carries modifiers, and the modifier name in \`do\` declares the rule type.

**What is in this branch:**

- \`func\`, \`recv\` (file-level via \`where.file\`), \`struct\` leaf filters implemented
- \`all-of\`, \`one-of\`, \`not\` combinators and \`has_directive\` are schema-present but return descriptive errors at runtime (wired up in follow-up PRs #381–#386)
- \`normalize\` layer translating structured \`where\`/\`do\` form to the internal flat fields that \`createRuleFromFields\` consumes
- Golden fixtures migrated to canonical 2-tier form
- [ADR-0003](docs/adr/0003-structured-rule-schema.md) records the decision in Nygard form (Status/Context/Decision/Consequences)
- [docs/rules.md](docs/rules.md) contains the full field reference, valid/invalid shape examples, and flat→structured migration guide

**Deferred items (not in this PR):**

- Target globbing — \`rulesByTarget\` remains exact-match; glob on \`target\` tracked as a follow-up
- \`is_test\` / \`test_main\` filters — reserved for a follow-up PR
- \`defaults:\` section sugar — deferred to a future iteration
- \`import_path\` / \`package_name\` filters — dropped from the stack; single \`*\` on \`target\` deferred

Fixes #346 (partial — branch 0 of the stack)

### gRPC-Go has an authorization bypass via missing leading slash in :path
[CVE-2026-33186](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33186) / [GHSA-p77j-4mvh-x3m3](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-p77j-4mvh-x3m3)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact
_What kind of vulnerability is it? Who is impacted?_

It is an **Authorization Bypass** resulting from **Improper Input Validation** of the HTTP/2 `:path` pseudo-header.

The gRPC-Go server was too lenient in its routing logic, accepting requests where the `:path` omitted the mandatory leading slash (e.g., `Service/Method` instead of `/Service/Method`). While the server successfully routed these requests to the correct handler, authorization interceptors (including the official `grpc/authz` package) evaluated the raw, non-canonical path string. Consequently, "deny" rules defined using canonical paths (starting with `/`) failed to match the incoming request, allowing it to bypass the policy if a fallback "allow" rule was present.

**Who is impacted?**
This affects gRPC-Go servers that meet both of the following criteria:
1. They use path-based authorization interceptors, such as the official RBAC implementation in `google.golang.org/grpc/authz` or custom interceptors relying on `info.FullMethod` or `grpc.Method(ctx)`.
2. Their security policy contains specific "deny" rules for canonical paths but allows other requests by default (a fallback "allow" rule).

The vulnerability is exploitable by an attacker who can send raw HTTP/2 frames with malformed `:path` headers directly to the gRPC server.

##### Patches
_Has the problem been patched? What versions should users upgrade to?_

Yes, the issue has been patched. The fix ensures that any request with a `:path` that does not start with a leading slash is immediately rejected with a `codes.Unimplemented` error, preventing it from reaching authorization interceptors or handlers with a non-canonical path string.

Users should upgrade to the following versions (or newer):
* **v1.79.3**
* The latest **master** branch.

It is recommended that all users employing path-based authorization (especially `grpc/authz`) upgrade as soon as the patch is available in a tagged release.

##### Workarounds
_Is there a way for users to fix or remediate the vulnerability without upgrading?_

While upgrading is the most secure and recommended path, users can mitigate the vulnerability using one of the following methods:

##### 1. Use a Validating Interceptor (Recommended Mitigation)
Add an "outermost" interceptor to your server that validates the path before any other authorization logic runs:

```go
func pathValidationInterceptor(ctx context.Context, req any, info *grpc.UnaryServerInfo, handler grpc.UnaryHandler) (any, error) {
    if info.FullMethod == "" || info.FullMethod[0] != '/' {
        return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unimplemented, "malformed method name")
    }   
    return handler(ctx, req)
}

// Ensure this is the FIRST interceptor in your chain
s := grpc.NewServer(
    grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor(pathValidationInterceptor, authzInterceptor),
)
```

##### 2. Infrastructure-Level Normalization
If your gRPC server is behind a reverse proxy or load balancer (such as Envoy, NGINX, or an L7 Cloud Load Balancer), ensure it is configured to enforce strict HTTP/2 compliance for pseudo-headers and reject or normalize requests where the `:path` header does not start with a leading slash.

##### 3. Policy Hardening
Switch to a "default deny" posture in your authorization policies (explicitly listing all allowed paths and denying everything else) to reduce the risk of bypasses via malformed inputs.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 9.1 / 10 (Critical)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p77j-4mvh-x3m3](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-p77j-4mvh-x3m3)

items.title: feat(tool): add join point filter interface
items.body:
## Description

Introduces the `Filter` interface and `where` clause foundation for join point composition ([#346](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/346)).

The `where` clause is optional — all existing rules continue to work unchanged. Two leaf filters are implemented: `FuncFilter` (function name + receiver) and `StructFilter` (struct name). Combinators (`all-of`, `one-of`, `not`) and additional leaf types (`import_path`, `package_name`, `test_main`, `directive`) are stubbed with descriptive errors, ready for branches 1-6 of OP4.

Architecture decisions are documented in ADR-0003 and ADR-0004.

> **Note:** This is a draft. It is the base branch of a stack; subsequent branches (combinators, glob filtering, package/test filters) will stack on top of this one.

## Motivation

Flat rules can express only a single predicate. There is currently no way to compose conditions — for example, "instrument functions annotated with `//otelc:span`" — or filter on package-level properties such as import path patterns.

Fixes #346 (partial — this is branch 0 of 6)

items.title: feat(tool): function or method with specific signature filter for `InstFuncRule`
items.body:
## Description

Extends `InstFuncRule` with five optional signature sub-filters that narrow function matching beyond name and receiver type:

| YAML field | Semantics |
|---|---|
| `signature` | Exact match on parameter and result types (field-list order) |
| `signature_contains` | OR-match: any listed arg type found in params **or** any listed return type found in results |
| `result_implements` | Any return type exactly matches the named type |
| `final_result_implements` | Only the last return type matches the named type |
| `argument_implements` | Any parameter type exactly matches the named type |

All filters are optional; when none are set the rule behaves exactly as before. All specified filters must match (AND logic).

Example rule:

```yaml
my_rule:
  target: example.com/pkg
  func: Open
  signature:
    args: [string]
    returns: ["*os.File", error]
  before: OnOpen
  path: example.com/hooks
```

Type-name matching is structural (DST-level, no type checker). For the `*_implements` filters this means an exact type-name match rather than full interface-satisfaction checking — matching Orchestrion's fast-path behaviour.

**New files:**
- `tool/internal/ast/typename.go` — private type-name parser + `parsedTypeName.matches` + `fieldListContainsType`
- `tool/internal/ast/typename_test.go` — unit tests for type-name parsing and field matching
- `tool/internal/ast/funcmatch_test.go` — unit tests for `FuncDeclMatchesFilters` (all five filters, combined AND logic, edge cases)
- `tool/internal/rule/func_rule_test.go` — YAML unmarshal tests for the new fields
- `tool/internal/instrument/testdata/golden/func-signature/` — golden integration test matching `Func1(string, int) (float32, error)` by exact signature

## Motivation

Instrumentation rules targeting overloaded-by-signature patterns (common in middleware, handler registration, and interface adapter code) currently require unique function names. The new sub-filters allow a rule to target a specific function variant without relying solely on its name.

Implements OP3.5 from #277.

Release 1.79.3

Security

  • server: fix an authorization bypass where malformed :path headers (missing the leading slash) could bypass path-based restricted "deny" rules in interceptors like grpc/authz. Any request with a non-canonical path is now immediately rejected with an Unimplemented error. (#8981)

  • mem: Add experimental API SetDefaultBufferPool to change the default buffer pool. (#8806)
    • Special Thanks: @​vanja-p
  • experimental/stats: Update MetricsRecorder to require embedding the new UnimplementedMetricsRecorder (a no-op struct) in all implementations for forward compatibility. (#8780)

Behavior Changes

  • balancer/weightedtarget: Remove handling of Addresses and only handle Endpoints in resolver updates. (#8841)

  • experimental/stats: Add support for asynchronous gauge metrics through the new AsyncMetricReporter and RegisterAsyncReporter APIs. (#8780)

items.title: feat(tool): add built-in pprof profiling support
items.body:
## Why

Closes #389.

`otelc` spawns one `otelc toolexec` process per package during a build.
To measure and compare instrumentation overhead across runs, we need CPU,
heap, and trace profiles from **all** processes — not just the parent.
This PR adds that capability with zero changes to the build pipeline.

## What

Three new hidden root flags (also settable via env vars):

| Flag | Env var | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `--profile-path=<dir>` | `OTELC_PROFILE_PATH` | Directory for output files |
| `--profile=cpu\|heap\|trace` | `OTELC_ENABLED_PROFILES` | Profile types (repeatable) |
| `--profile-summary` | `OTELC_PROFILE_SUMMARY` | Merge per-PID files after build |

Each process writes PID-stamped files (`otelc-cpu-<PID>.pprof`, etc.) so
parallel toolexec invocations never collide. Env vars are set in the
`Before` hook so `os.Environ()` in `BuildWithToolexec` propagates them to
child processes automatically — no changes to the build pipeline needed.

`--profile-summary` merges all per-PID files into one file per type using
`go tool pprof -proto`, then removes the individual files.

### Usage

```bash
# Collect CPU + heap profiles across all processes
otelc --profile-path=./profiles --profile=cpu --profile=heap go build ./...

# Merge into two summary files
otelc --profile-path=./profiles --profile=cpu --profile=heap \
      --profile-summary go build ./...

# Compare two builds
go tool pprof -http=:8080 -diff_base=baseline/otelc-cpu.pprof modified/otelc-cpu.pprof
```

See `docs/profiling.md` for full documentation including merge and diff workflows.

## Changes

- `tool/internal/profile/profile.go` — new package: `Session`, `Start`, `Stop`, `StartFromEnv`, `Merge`, `ParseTypes`
- `tool/internal/profile/profile_test.go` — 10 unit tests (all pass with `-race`)
- `tool/cmd/profiling.go` — CLI glue: `initProfiling` / `stopProfiling` hooks
- `tool/cmd/main.go` — 3 hidden flags, composed `Before`/`After` hooks; fix wrong path in log error message
- `tool/internal/ast/directive.go` — suppress pre-existing `revive` `unhandled-error` on `strings.Builder.WriteRune` (never errors by contract)
- `docs/profiling.md` — user-facing documentation
- `go.mod` — promote `google/go-cmp` from indirect to direct dependency

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./tool/...` — clean
- [x] `go test -race -count=1 ./tool/...` — all pass
- [x] `make format` — no drift
- [x] `make lint` — 0 issues

items.title: refactor(tool): structured rule schema with where/do grouping
items.body:
## Description

Introduce explicit `where` (selectors) and `do` (modifiers) blocks in rule YAML files, replacing the previous flat field layout where matcher and modifier fields were mixed at the same level.

**Before:**
```yaml
server_hook:
  target: net/http
  func: ServeHTTP
  recv: serverHandler
  before: BeforeServeHTTP
  after: AfterServeHTTP
  path: "github.com/.../server"
```

**After:**
```yaml
server_hook:
  where:
    target: net/http
    func: ServeHTTP
    recv: serverHandler
  do:
    inject_hooks:
      before: BeforeServeHTTP
      after: AfterServeHTTP
      path: "github.com/.../server"
```

The modifier name inside `do` determines the rule type: `inject_hooks`, `inject_code`, `add_struct_fields`, `add_file`, `wrap_call`, `expand_directive`, `assign_value`.

A `normalizeRule()` function at the YAML parsing boundary translates the new format to the internal flat representation — rule structs, constructors, validation, and JSON serialization are unchanged.

## Motivation

Rules have two concerns — **what to match** and **what to do** — but they were expressed as a flat bag of fields. Scanability suffers: it takes effort to tell selectors from modifiers without knowing the rule type. The new schema makes intent visible at a glance and gives future modifier types (`prepend_statements`, `modify_body`, etc.) a natural place to live.

ADR: `docs/adr/0003-structured-rule-schema.md`

---

- [x] Code formatted: `make format`

## Description

`GoBuild()` no longer removes `.otelc-build/` after the build completes.
Backed-up files (`go.mod`, `go.sum`, etc.) are still restored and generated
runtime files are still removed, but the working directory is preserved so
users can inspect intermediate build artifacts for debugging.

The backup restoration logic is extracted into a `restoreBackups()` helper,
which `Cleanup()` calls internally — no behavior change for `otelc cleanup`.

## Motivation

Keeping `.otelc-build/` after a build makes it easier to debug instrumentation
issues by inspecting matched rules, extracted packages, and the go build cache.
Users can still run `otelc cleanup` to remove it explicitly.

Fixes #393

items.title: feat(tool): add --stats flag for toolexec timing
items.body:
## Description

Adds a hidden `--stats` flag (and `OTELC_STATS` env var) that logs wall-clock duration for every toolexec command invocation. When enabled, each compile/link/asm call emits a structured log entry:

```
tool=compile package=github.com/foo/bar duration=123.4ms duration_ms=123
```

**Changes:**
- `tool/util/shared.go` — `EnvOtelcStats = "OTELC_STATS"` constant, shared between `cmd` and `internal/instrument` to avoid import cycles
- `tool/cmd/stats.go` — new: `initStats` Before-hook reads `--stats` flag and sets the env var
- `tool/cmd/main.go` — hidden `--stats` flag with `Sources: cli.EnvVars(util.EnvOtelcStats)`; `initStats` chained after `initProfiling`
- `tool/internal/instrument/toolexec.go` — wraps `util.RunCmd` with `time.Now()`/`time.Since()` when `OTELC_STATS` is set; logs tool, package, duration

## Motivation

Needed for benchmarking otelc against Orchestrion. Per-tool timing identifies which compilation phases are slowest and where instrumentation overhead concentrates.

`OTELC_STATS` propagates to child toolexec processes automatically via `os.Environ()` in `BuildWithToolexec` — the same pattern used by `OTELC_PROFILE_PATH`.

Fixes #389

items.title: feat(tool): wrap_expression advice for function_call and identifier rules
items.body:
## Description

A `wrap_expression` advice operator that wraps an existing expression using a Go template, where `{{ . }}` is substituted with the original expression.

- **`identifier` rule** (`InstDeclRule`): new optional `wrap_expression` field (mutually exclusive with `value`). Wraps the existing initializer of a matched `var` or `const` declaration. Returns an actionable error if the declaration has no initializer.
- **`function_call` rule** (`InstCallRule`): removes the `*CallExpr` output constraint from the template — the wrapped expression may now be any `dst.Expr` type, not only a call expression. Rewrites `applyCallRule` to use a two-pass approach (`dst.Inspect` to collect + pre-compute, `dstutil.Apply`+`cursor.Replace` to apply) that safely replaces nodes without re-matching the original pointer inside its own wrapper.
- **`WrapExpressionAdvice`** struct added to `rule/base.go` so future rule types (e.g. `value_declaration`) can embed it without duplication.

## Example

```yaml
# Wrap the existing http.DefaultTransport with an OTel instrumented version
wrap_default_transport:
  target: net/http
  kind: var
  identifier: DefaultTransport
  wrap_expression:
    template: "otelhttp.NewTransport({{ . }})"
  imports:
    otelhttp: "go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp"
```

## Motivation

Implements OP5.3 from #347

items.title: feat(tool): append_args advice for function_call join point
items.body:
## Description

Adds `append_args` as a new advice operator on the `function_call` join point. Rules can now inject additional Go expressions as arguments to matched call sites without needing a `template` wrapper.

- **Non-ellipsis calls**: new expressions are appended directly to `call.Args`.
- **Ellipsis calls** (`f(a, opts...)`): an IIFE wrapper is generated so the spread semantics are preserved. `variadic_type` must be set when the matched call uses `...`.
- `template` and `append_args` are independent and composable: when both are set, args are appended first, then the call is wrapped.

## YAML shape

```yaml
# Non-ellipsis
add_otel_grpc_interceptors:
  target: myapp
  function_call: google.golang.org/grpc.NewClient
  append_args:
    - "grpc.WithUnaryInterceptor(otelgrpc.UnaryClientInterceptor())"
    - "grpc.WithStreamInterceptor(otelgrpc.StreamClientInterceptor())"
  imports:
    grpc: "google.golang.org/grpc"
    otelgrpc: "go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/google.golang.org/grpc/otelgrpc"

# Ellipsis — variadic_type required
add_otel_grpc_dial_interceptors:
  target: myapp
  function_call: google.golang.org/grpc.Dial
  append_args:
    - "grpc.WithUnaryInterceptor(otelgrpc.UnaryClientInterceptor())"
  variadic_type: "grpc.DialOption"
  imports:
    grpc: "google.golang.org/grpc"
    otelgrpc: "go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/google.golang.org/grpc/otelgrpc"
```


## Motivation

Implements OP5.4 from #347.

items.title: Add test capability to check if current hook satisfies latest SDK version
items.body:
As discussed in the slack, maintaining fixed version ranges for instrumented libraries (e.g., `version: v1.2.3, v1.7.0)` is a manual and potentially unscalable process. To ensure our instrumentation remains compatible with new library releases without constant manual intervention, we propose implementing a new automated test.

#### **Proposed Solution**

We should introduce a new CI test, tentatively named **`FetchingLatestVersion`**, which will allow us to use open-ended version ranges (e.g., `version: v1.2.3` only) with confidence.

#### **Expected Behavior**

1.  The test should run as part of the CI pipeline.
2.  For a given instrumented library, it should automatically fetch its **latest stable version** from its registry
3.  It will then run the corresponding integration/instrumentation tests against this latest version.
4.  **If the tests pass:** The build is successful. This confirms our assumption of forward compatibility.
5.  **If the tests fail**: The build must fail. This serves as an immediate alert to maintainers about a breaking change. In this scenario, the maintainer will need to split the instrumentation rule
    1. The existing rule's version range will be capped to define an upper bound (e.g., changing [v1.2.3,) to [v1.2.3, v4.5.6)).
    2. A new rule will be created for the new and subsequent versions (e.g., [v4.5.6,)).
    3. This new rule will require its own instrumentation implementation to handle the breaking changes.

#### **Benefits**

*   **Reduces Maintenance Burden:** Automates the process of verifying compatibility with new releases.
*   **Proactive Failure Detection:** Allows us to discover breaking changes immediately, rather than waiting for user reports.
*   **Increases Confidence:** Provides continuous assurance that our instrumentation works with the latest dependencies.

This feature is a critical testing capability for the long-term health of the project. This issue is to track its implementation and is open for community contribution.

items.title: Golden test should include its own dedicated source and hook functions
items.body:
At the moment, all golden tests depend on the shared source.go and hook.go:
```
.
├── golden
│   ├── after-only
│   │   ├── after_only.main.go.golden
│   │   ├── after_only.otelc.globals.go.golden
│   │   └── rules.yml
│   ├── before-only
│   │   ├── before_only.main.go.golden
│   │   ├── before_only.otelc.globals.go.golden
│   │   └── rules.yml
...
│   └── underscore-syntax
│       ├── rules.yml
│       ├── underscore_syntax.main.go.golden
│       └── underscore_syntax.otelc.globals.go.golden
├── hook.go
├── newfile.go
└── source.go
```
As a result, whenever a new test case is added and source.go is modified, the golden files for all test cases need to be updated as well.

I propose that each test case should have its own hook.go and source.go:
```
.
├── golden
│   ├── after-only
│   │   ├── after_only.main.go.golden
│   │   ├── after_only.otelc.globals.go.golden
│   │   ├── source.go
│   │   ├── hook.go
│   │   └── rules.yml
│   ├── before-only
│   │   ├── before_only.main.go.golden
│   │   ├── before_only.otelc.globals.go.golden
│   │   ├── source.go
│   │   ├── hook.go
│   │   └── rules.yml
...
│   └── underscore-syntax
│       ├── rules.yml
│       ├── hook.go
│       ├── source.go
│       ├── underscore_syntax.main.go.golden
│       └── underscore_syntax.otelc.globals.go.golden

```

### opentelemetry-go: BSD kenv command not using absolute path enables PATH hijacking
[CVE-2026-39883](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-39883) / [GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The fix for GHSA-9h8m-3fm2-qjrq (CVE-2026-24051) changed the Darwin `ioreg` command to use an absolute path but left the BSD `kenv` command using a bare name, allowing the same PATH hijacking attack on BSD and Solaris platforms.

##### Root Cause

`sdk/resource/host_id.go` line 42:

    if result, err := r.execCommand("kenv", "-q", "smbios.system.uuid"); err == nil {

Compare with the fixed Darwin path at line 58:

    result, err := r.execCommand("/usr/sbin/ioreg", "-rd1", "-c", "IOPlatformExpertDevice")

The `execCommand` helper at `sdk/resource/host_id_exec.go` uses `exec.Command(name, arg...)` which searches `$PATH` when the command name contains no path separator.

Affected platforms (per build tag in `host_id_bsd.go:4`): DragonFly BSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, Solaris.

The `kenv` path is reached when `/etc/hostid` does not exist (line 38-40), which is common on FreeBSD systems.

##### Attack

1. Attacker has local access to a system running a Go application that imports `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk`
2. Attacker places a malicious `kenv` binary earlier in `$PATH`
3. Application initializes OpenTelemetry resource detection at startup
4. `hostIDReaderBSD.read()` calls `exec.Command("kenv", ...)` which resolves to the malicious binary
5. Arbitrary code executes in the context of the application

Same attack vector and impact as CVE-2026-24051.

##### Suggested Fix

Use the absolute path:

    if result, err := r.execCommand("/bin/kenv", "-q", "smbios.system.uuid"); err == nil {

On FreeBSD, `kenv` is located at `/bin/kenv`.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.3 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### [`v1.42.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.42.0): /v0.64.0/v0.18.0/v0.0.16

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/compare/v1.41.0...v1.42.0)

##### Added

- Add `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.40.0` package.
  The package contains semantic conventions from the `v1.40.0` version of the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions.
  See the [migration documentation](./semconv/v1.40.0/MIGRATION.md) for information on how to upgrade from `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.39.0`. ([#​7985](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7985))
- Add `Err` and `SetErr` on `Record` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` to attach an error and set record exception attributes in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log/sdk`. ([#​7924](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7924))

##### Changed

- `TracerProvider.ForceFlush` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` joins errors together and continues iteration through SpanProcessors as opposed to returning the first encountered error without attempting exports on subsequent SpanProcessors. ([#​7856](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7856))

##### Fixed

- Fix missing `request.GetBody` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp` to correctly handle HTTP2 GOAWAY frame. ([#​7931](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7931))
- Fix semconv v1.39.0 generated metric helpers skipping required attributes when extra attributes were empty. ([#​7964](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7964))
- Preserve W3C TraceFlags bitmask (including the random Trace ID flag) during trace context extraction and injection in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation`. ([#​7834](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7834))

##### Removed

- Drop support for \[Go 1.24]. ([#​7984](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7984))

Sourced from go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp's changelog.

[1.43.0/0.65.0/0.19.0] 2026-04-02

Added

  • Add IsRandom and WithRandom on TraceFlags, and IsRandom on SpanContext in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace for W3C Trace Context Level 2 Random Trace ID Flag support. (#8012)
  • Add service detection with WithService in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource. (#7642)
  • Add DefaultWithContext and EnvironmentWithContext in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource to support plumbing context.Context through default and environment detectors. (#8051)
  • Support attributes with empty value (attribute.EMPTY) in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc. (#8038)
  • Support attributes with empty value (attribute.EMPTY) in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetricgrpc. (#8038)
  • Support attributes with empty value (attribute.EMPTY) in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc. (#8038)
  • Support attributes with empty value (attribute.EMPTY) in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp. (#8038)
  • Support attributes with empty value (attribute.EMPTY) in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp. (#8038)
  • Support attributes with empty value (attribute.EMPTY) in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp. (#8038)
  • Support attributes with empty value (attribute.EMPTY) in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/metricdata/metricdatatest. (#8038)
  • Add support for per-series start time tracking for cumulative metrics in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric. Set OTEL_GO_X_PER_SERIES_START_TIMESTAMPS=true to enable. (#8060)
  • Add WithCardinalityLimitSelector for metric reader for configuring cardinality limits specific to the instrument kind. (#7855)

Changed

  • Introduce the EMPTY Type in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute to reflect that an empty value is now a valid value, with INVALID remaining as a deprecated alias of EMPTY. (#8038)
  • Improve slice handling in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute to optimize short slice values with fixed-size fast paths. (#8039)
  • Improve performance of span metric recording in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace by returning early if self-observability is not enabled. (#8067)
  • Improve formatting of metric data diffs in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/metricdata/metricdatatest. (#8073)

Deprecated

  • Deprecate INVALID in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute. Use EMPTY instead. (#8038)

Fixed

  • Return spec-compliant TraceIdRatioBased description. This is a breaking behavioral change, but it is necessary to make the implementation spec-compliant. (#8027)
  • Fix a race condition in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric where the lastvalue aggregation could collect the value 0 even when no zero-value measurements were recorded. (#8056)
  • Limit HTTP response body to 4 MiB in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp to mitigate excessive memory usage caused by a misconfigured or malicious server. Responses exceeding the limit are treated as non-retryable errors. (#8108)
  • Limit HTTP response body to 4 MiB in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp to mitigate excessive memory usage caused by a misconfigured or malicious server. Responses exceeding the limit are treated as non-retryable errors. (#8108)
  • Limit HTTP response body to 4 MiB in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp to mitigate excessive memory usage caused by a misconfigured or malicious server. Responses exceeding the limit are treated as non-retryable errors. (#8108)
  • WithHostID detector in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource to use full path for kenv command on BSD. (#8113)
  • Fix missing request.GetBody in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp to correctly handle HTTP2 GOAWAY frame. (#8096)

[1.42.0/0.64.0/0.18.0/0.0.16] 2026-03-06

Added

  • Add go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.40.0 package. The package contains semantic conventions from the v1.40.0 version of the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions. See the migration documentation for information on how to upgrade from go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.39.0. (#7985)

items.title: feat(test): add bench tests
items.body:
Contributing to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/351

Current bench tests compare `go vs otelc` compile times under 3 different scenarios:
- `baseline`: just fmt
- `multi`: currently all available rules instrumented
- `largeidle`: a good amount of dependencies not instrumented

I'm open to discussing other scenarios.

The good thing about `go vs otelc` is that we don't care too much about historical perf evolution, which means we also don't care about the runners (which usually you end up needing dedicated or baremetal runners, etc.). So no need to push the adoption of tools like https://github.com/marketplace/actions/continuous-benchmark. With just some basic tricks (documented in `benchmarking.md`), we can obtain good enough results for `go vs otelc` comparison. I've experienced around ~<5% deviation between runs.

I let a 50% of extra overhead as an initial value, although we should define and document clearly our "SLOs".

Current results example:

```
2026/04/09 14:54:46 scenario=baseline      plain=3.443s (±0.007)  otelc=4.366s (±0.006)  overhead=+26.8%
2026/04/09 14:57:22 scenario=largeidle     plain=12.205s (±0.027)  otelc=13.625s (±0.002)  overhead=+11.6%
2026/04/09 15:01:13 scenario=multi         plain=14.900s (±0.076)  otelc=23.471s (±0.089)  overhead=+57.5%
```

items.title: feat(instrumentation): Add k8s-client-go informers instrumentation
items.body:
Implements k8s-client-go informers auto instrumentation to automatically emit traces from informer handlers.

Follows [K8S semconv](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/resource/k8s/) with some additional keys:
- k8s.object.uid (for generic/unknown objects)
- k8s.object.name (for generic/unknown objects)
- k8s.object.api_version
- k8s.object.kind

- k8s.objects.count
- k8s.objects.is_in_initial_list

Inspired by: https://github.com/alibaba/loongsuite-go-agent/tree/main/pkg/rules/k8s-client-go

Fixes #462

items.title: fix(instrumentation): prevent reentrant OTel SDK initialization
items.body:
When a project depends on golang.google.org/grpc and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL is set to grpc, initializing the exporters (autoexport.NewSpanExporter/NewMetricReader) inside initInstrumentation/SetupOTelSDK calls grpc.NewClient.

This invokes BeforeNewClient gRPC instrumentation hook which calls initInstrumentation/SetupOTelSDK again. Since initInstrumentation/SetupOTelSDK use sync.Once, this recursive call causes a deadlock.

### OpenTelemetry-Go: multi-value `baggage` header extraction causes excessive allocations (remote dos amplification)
[CVE-2026-29181](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-29181) / [GHSA-mh2q-q3fh-2475](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-mh2q-q3fh-2475)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
multi-value `baggage:` header extraction parses each header field-value independently and aggregates members across values. this allows an attacker to amplify cpu and allocations by sending many `baggage:` header lines, even when each individual value is within the 8192-byte per-value parse limit.

##### severity

HIGH (availability / remote request amplification)

##### relevant links

- repository: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go
- pinned callsite: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/1ee4a4126dbdd1bc79e9fae072fa488beffac52a/propagation/baggage.go#L58

##### vulnerability details

**pins:** open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go@1ee4a4126dbdd1bc79e9fae072fa488beffac52a
**as-of:** 2026-02-04
**policy:** direct (no program scope provided)

**callsite:** propagation/baggage.go:58 (`extractMultiBaggage`)
**attacker control:** inbound HTTP request headers (many `baggage` field-values) → `propagation.HeaderCarrier.Values("baggage")` → repeated `baggage.Parse` + member aggregation

##### root cause

`extractMultiBaggage` iterates over all `baggage` header field-values and parses each one independently, then appends members into a shared slice. the 8192-byte parsing cap applies per header value, but the multi-value path repeats that work once per header line (bounded only by the server/proxy header byte limit).

##### impact

in a default `net/http` configuration (max header bytes 1mb), a single request with many `baggage:` header field-values can cause large per-request allocations and increased latency.

example from the attached PoC harness (darwin/arm64; 80 values; 40 requests):

- canonical: `per_req_alloc_bytes=10315458` and `p95_ms=7`
- control: `per_req_alloc_bytes=133429` and `p95_ms=0`

##### proof of concept

canonical:

```bash
mkdir -p poc
unzip poc.zip -d poc
cd poc
make test
```

output (excerpt):

```
[CALLSITE_HIT]: propagation/baggage.go:58 extractMultiBaggage
[PROOF_MARKER]: baggage_multi_value_amplification p95_ms=7 per_req_alloc_bytes=10315458 per_req_allocs=16165
```

control:

```bash
cd poc
make control
```

control output (excerpt):

```
[NC_MARKER]: baggage_single_value_baseline p95_ms=0 per_req_alloc_bytes=133429 per_req_allocs=480
```

**expected:** multiple `baggage` header field-values should be semantically equivalent to a single comma-joined `baggage` value and should not multiply parsing/alloc work within the effective header byte budget.
**actual:** multiple `baggage` header field-values trigger repeated parsing and member aggregation, causing high per-request allocations and increased latency even when each individual value is within 8192 bytes.

##### fix recommendation

avoid repeated parsing across multi-values by enforcing a global budget and/or normalizing multi-values into a single value before parsing. one mitigation approach is to treat multi-values as a single comma-joined string and cap total parsed bytes (for example 8192 bytes total).

**fix accepted when:** under the default PoC harness settings, canonical stays within 2x of control for `per_req_alloc_bytes` and `per_req_allocs`, and `p95_ms` stays below 2ms.

- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

items.title: LFX Mentorship 2026 Term 2: expand Go compile-time instrumentation support
items.body:
This issue tracks the OpenTelemetry Go compile-time instrumentation proposal for CNCF LFX Mentorship 2026 Term 2 (June-August): **Expanding Go compile-instrumentation support and improving tooling**.

## Background

The OpenTelemetry Go Compile Instrumentation project provides `otelc`, a compile-time auto-instrumentation tool for Go applications. It injects OpenTelemetry instrumentation during the Go build process without requiring users to manually change their application source code.

As the project moves toward v1.0 and continues feature-parity work with mature compile-time instrumentation efforts such as Orchestrion and Loongsuite, a major need is to broaden real-world library coverage while improving the tool and contributor workflow that make new integrations maintainable. This mentorship is intended to help with both: adding several integrations and improving `otelc` based on what we learn while building them.

Related roadmap/backlog items:

- #164
- #261
- #133
- #406
- #543

Candidate integration work may draw from existing/open work such as Kafka, database/cache, logging, Kubernetes client, GenAI SDKs, or other mentor-approved high-impact libraries. The final list should be selected with mentors based on project priorities, existing ownership, and complexity.

## Mentorship scope

The mentee will add compile-time instrumentation support for several widely used Go libraries and improve the instrumentation workflow along the way.

This includes:

- selecting 3-4 target integrations with mentors, depending on complexity and current upstream activity;
- studying the target library APIs and relevant OpenTelemetry semantic conventions;
- writing `otelc` rules and hook implementations;
- defining supported version ranges and compatibility expectations;
- adding tests that prove the instrumented applications build and emit expected telemetry;
- documenting the integrations and the underlying compile-time instrumentation approach.

The project should also teach the “science” behind the work: how Go symbols and versions are matched, how hooks are injected, how semantic conventions shape telemetry, and how compatibility with upstream library releases is verified.

## Expected outcomes

- `otelc` instrumentation support for 3-4 widely used Go libraries, selected with mentors from the roadmap/backlog.
- Instrumentation rules and hook code for each new integration.
- Unit, integration, and/or end-to-end tests for newly added integrations.
- Tooling or workflow improvements discovered during integration work, for example rule validation, hook scaffolding, latest-library compatibility checks, integration layout, or debugging output.
- Documentation, examples, and demos for the new integrations.
- A final write-up that helps future contributors understand how to design, implement, and validate compile-time instrumentation.

## Candidate related issues/PRs

The exact integration list is intentionally flexible, but current examples of relevant upstream work include:

- #296
- #302
- #317
- #318
- #327
- #413
- #426
- #168

## Mentor

- Kemal Akkoyun (@kakkoyun)
- Dario Castañé (@darccio) 

## Acknowledgement

Initial project framing was drafted with help from Azhar Momin (@amazingakai).

items.title: feat(tool): add support for customizable injection in InstRawRule with pattern matching
items.body:
## Description

- `pattern` (string, optional): The position within the function where the raw code should be injected. By default, the code is injected at the start of the function body. If provided, the value must be a valid regular expression.

  The pattern is matched against the canonical gofmt representation for each statement in the function body (not always the exact original source formatting). The injected code is placed immediately before/after the first statement that matches the pattern.

  If no statement matches the pattern, an error is returned.

- `placement` (string, optional): Determines where to inject the raw code when a `pattern` is specified. Can be either `before` (default) or `after`.


## Motivation

It helps customize injection point for raw code inside functions.

Fixes #324

### [`v9.20.1`](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/releases/tag/v9.20.1): 9.20.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/compare/v9.20.0...v9.20.1)

This is a patch release containing bug fixes only. There are no new features or breaking changes; upgrading from 9.20.0 is a drop-in replacement.

#### 🚀 Highlights

##### RESP3 pub/sub message loss fixed

`PeekPushNotificationName` previously inspected only the bytes already buffered by `bufio`, so when a push frame header straddled a buffer fill boundary it could return a **truncated** notification name (e.g. `"messa"` instead of `"message"`). The push processor then mis-routed the frame and `ReadReply` silently dropped it, causing intermittent RESP3 pub/sub message loss. The peek now grows its window (36 bytes → up to 4 KiB) and reads more from the connection until the header is complete, cleanly separating incomplete prefixes from corrupt frames (including overflow-safe bulk-length handling). Fixes [#​3839](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/issues/3839).

([#​3842](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3842)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)

#### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **RESP3 push peeking**: `PeekPushNotificationName` no longer returns a truncated notification name when a push frame header spans a buffer boundary, preventing silent RESP3 pub/sub message loss (fixes [#​3839](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/issues/3839)) ([#​3842](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3842)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **`FT.HYBRID` vector params**: Vector data is now always sent via `PARAMS` with auto-generated param names (`__vector_param_N`, with collision avoidance) when `VectorParamName` is omitted, since Redis no longer accepts inline vector blobs; the `FTHybridOptions.Params` map is no longer mutated, so the same options struct can be reused across calls ([#​3844](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3844)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **`CLUSTER SHARDS` forward compatibility**: Unknown shard- and node-level attributes in the `CLUSTER SHARDS` reply are now skipped via `DiscardNext()` instead of erroring, so clients keep working when the server introduces new fields ([#​3843](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3843)) by [@​madolson](https://redirect.github.com/madolson)
- **PubSub double reconnect**: `PubSub.releaseConn` no longer reconnects twice when a connection is both unusable (or pending handoff) and reports a bad-connection error, avoiding a wasted connection establish-then-close cycle ([#​3833](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3833)) by [@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs)

#### 👥 Contributors

We'd like to thank all the contributors who worked on this release!

[@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs), [@​madolson](https://redirect.github.com/madolson), [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
