items.title: fix(tool): disambiguate trampoline names across do-sequence entries
items.body:
## Problem

A `do:` sequence that applies several modifiers to the same function produced
trampoline and `HookContextImpl` declarations with identical names, so
compilation failed with redeclaration errors.

Root cause: names came from `util.CRC32(rule.String())`, and `String()` returned
only the rule name, which is the same for every `do` entry expanded from one rule.

## Approach

Trampoline and `HookContextImpl` names now derive from what the rule does, not
its name or position.

- `tool/internal/rule/func_rule.go` adds `InstFuncRule.Identity()`: a CRC32 over
  the rule's instrumentation content (target, version, func, recv, before/after
  hooks, path, signature filters). It uses length-prefixed encoding (`len:value`)
  rather than a delimiter, so it stays injective for any content. Type names can
  contain commas or `|`, so no separator is safe to rely on.
- The name-generation sites (`apply_func.go`, `optimize.go`, `trampoline.go`) call
  `rule.Identity()` instead of `util.CRC32(rule.String())`. Identity is the single
  source of every suffix.
- De-duplication (`apply_func.go`, `toolexec.go`): rules with the same identity
  emit their trampoline once instead of redeclaring it. Imports are applied for
  every matching rule first, so a de-duplicated rule never drops imports its hook
  needs.

Do-sequence execution order stays correct through insertion order: the
normalizer expands entries in order and the instrumenter applies them in that
order. Explicit, controllable ordering is deferred (see #583).

## Why content, not position

An earlier revision used a `name#<index>` suffix. As raised in review, that still
collides: `my_hook` `do[1]` renders `my_hook#1`, and a rule named `my_hook#1` at
`do[0]` renders the same string. Content-derived identity avoids this, because the
inputs are full rule bodies rather than a rendered string. The only remaining
collision is between byte-identical rules, which are the same rule and
de-duplicate.

## Testing

- `multiple-hooks-single-func/`: a before-hook (`do[0]`) and an after-hook
  (`do[1]`) on one function emit two distinct trampoline sets in `do` order.
- `dedup-identical-rules/`: two identical rules with different names on one
  function collapse to one trampoline set and compile.
- `TestInstFuncRule_Identity`: do-sequence modifiers stay distinct, the
  `my_hook#1` collision is gone, identical content shares one identity, and
  signature filters participate.
- Func-rule goldens regenerated for the content-derived suffix. Struct, call,
  decl, and raw goldens are untouched.

Verified with `go build ./tool/...`, `make test-unit/tool` (`-race`),
`make check-golden-files`, and `make lint`.

Fixes #544.

items.title: feat(tool): glob matching on target for package selection
items.body:
Rule-to-package matching was exact-only: `runMatch` looked up `rulesByTarget[dep.ImportPath]`, so a rule could target exactly one import path. This adds glob support to the existing `target` selector so a single rule can instrument a package family. `target` stays the only package-selection surface — **no** separate `import_path` field is introduced.

- `tool/internal/rule/target_glob.go`: glob engine. `IsGlobTarget` (detects `* ? [`), `ValidateTarget` (load-time rejection of `**` fused into a path segment and malformed bracket expressions), and `MatchGlobTarget` (segment-wise matcher: `*` = one segment via `path.Match`, `**` = zero-or-more segments).
- `tool/internal/setup/match.go`: `matchDeps` splits rules into an exact-key index (unchanged fast-path map lookup) and a glob slice evaluated against every dependency import path. Targets are validated when rules are parsed, so a bad pattern fails loudly at load time.
- `tool/internal/instrument/instrument_test.go`: the golden harness gained a `targetMatches` gate so glob targets evaluate against the package import path (exact targets pass through unchanged).
- Goldens `target-glob-match/` (a `**` target instruments the package) and `target-glob-no-match/` (an `example.com/svc/**` target leaves the package untouched; golden is byte-identical to source).

Supersedes the dropped `import_path` glob filter (closed #382, which targeted the now-removed `tool/internal/filter/` layout and was used here only as a design reference).

**Glob semantics:** `**` is a whole-segment wildcard matching zero-or-more segments (`example.com/svc/**` matches both `example.com/svc` and `example.com/svc/users/v2`); `*` matches exactly one segment and never crosses `/`. Reversed bracket ranges (`[z-a]`) are not rejected at load time — Go's `path.Match` reports `ErrBadPattern` only for unclosed brackets, so such a pattern simply never matches, consistent with stdlib glob behavior (documented in a code comment).

## Testing

- `go build ./...`
- `go test ./tool/internal/setup/ ./tool/internal/instrument/ ./tool/internal/rule/ -race -count=1` — all pass
- `make lint` — 0 issues
- Verified the no-match golden is byte-identical to its `source.go`; the match golden contains injected trampolines.

## Motivation

Instrumentation rules could not target package families (e.g. all of `example.com/foo/...`), forcing one rule per exact import path.

Fixes #549
Refs #346

items.title: feat(tool): add is_test where.file predicate for test package filtering
items.body:
Adds `is_test`, a `where.file` boolean predicate that selects or excludes **test builds**, plus the `go test` support needed for it to take effect.

## What `is_test` matches

A test build is a compilation the Go toolchain produces only as part of `go test`: a package augmented with its `_test.go` files, an external `xxx_test` package, or the generated `_testmain.go` runner. The tool detects this from the presence of those sources in the compile's source set, surfaced as `setup.MatchContext.IsTest`.

- `is_test: true` — match only test builds
- `is_test: false` — match only non-test builds
- absent — no filtering

Test-ness is **not** an import-path `.test` suffix. The Go toolchain never passes a `.test` import path to `go tool compile`; that suffix lives in the test binary name and the `TOOLEXEC_IMPORTPATH` annotation, never in the compile's `-p` flag. An earlier suffix-based draft could not match in practice, so detection is keyed on the source set instead.

## `go test` support

`otelc` previously accepted only `go build`/`go install`, whose build plan never contains test packages, so `is_test` could never match. This PR accepts `otelc go test` and lists a `go test -a -x -n` plan, which surfaces the test-augmented, external test, and test-main compiles. `splitBuildTargets` also learns the `go test` value flags so `go test ./pkg -run TestX` resolves the package whether flags precede or follow it; `-args` stops target scanning.

## Commits

1. `feat(tool/rule)`: the `is_test` predicate — `FilterDef.IsTest`, `IsTestFilter`, `MatchContext.IsTest`, and `isTestBuild`. Counted as a leaf in the combinator-exclusivity guard, so it cannot be silently combined with `all-of`/`one-of`/`not`.
2. `test(tool)`: unit + golden coverage — leaf-filter unit tests, `Build` construction, `preciseMatching` end-to-end gating (including a production file matched because its build is a test build, and combinator+`is_test` negatives), YAML round-trip fixtures, and instrumentation goldens (a `source_test.go` fixture instrumented; a no-match fixture byte-identical to its source).
3. `feat(tool)`: `go test` build-plan support and test-flag-aware `splitBuildTargets`.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`
- `go test ./tool/... -race -count=1` — pass
- `make lint` — 0 issues
- Goldens: the match fixtures contain injected trampolines; the no-match golden is byte-identical to its `source.go`.

## Motivation

Rules could not opt into or out of test code, so instrumentation that should (or should not) apply under `go test` had no way to express it. `is_test` expresses it, and `go test` support makes it effective.

Fixes #550
Refs #346

items.title: LatestLibRun failed on main (2026-06-03)
items.body:
The [LatestLibRun workflow](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/actions/runs/26907317513) failed on `main`.

This means the latest release of an upstream instrumented library introduced a **runtime behavior change** (removed function, changed signature, dropped instrumentation hook point) that breaks existing integration tests.

## Remediation

1. Identify the failing test and the upstream library version that caused the break.
2. Cap the existing rule's version range in the relevant `pkg/instrumentation/.../*.yaml` file.
3. Open a new rule entry for the new version range and update the hook implementation.

items.title: feat: Remote integration support (a.k.a `otelc.tool.go` file support)
items.body:
> **Original:** This file should help us to define the required dependencies for the instrumentations. Similar logic to [orchestrion.tool.go](https://github.com/DataDog/orchestrion/blob/main/instrument/orchestrion.tool.go).

## Summary

Add a user-facing, source-controlled file that **declares which instrumentations a project enables**, driving compile-time instrumentation from explicit imports rather than the current implicit all-or-nothing matching. This mirrors DataDog Orchestrion's `orchestrion.tool.go` mechanism and realizes the design already sketched in [`docs/ux-design.md`](docs/ux-design.md). 

**This will be eventually super useful to automagically add the remote integrations from any repo using go modules.**

We will support **both** filenames:
- **`otel.instrumentation.go`** — canonical name used throughout `docs/ux-design.md`.
- **`otelc.tool.go`** — alias matching this issue's title and the tool's `otelc.`-prefixed artifacts (`otelc-pkg.gz`, `otelc.runtime.go`, `.otelc-build/`).

The file follows the standard Go ["tools.go" idiom](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Tool_dependencies) — a `//go:build tools`-guarded file whose blank imports enumerate the instrumentation packages to activate:

```go
//go:build tools

package tools

import (
    _ "github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/instrumentation/db"    // database instrumentation
    _ "github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/instrumentation/http"  // net/http client + server
)
```

Because the file is guarded by a build tag, it never compiles into the binary — but `go mod` tracks those imports as real dependencies, giving reproducible, auditable builds.

## Background — today vs. the target

### Today (all-or-nothing)

The setup phase (`tool/internal/setup/`) runs a dry build (`go build -a -x -n`, `find.go`), loads **every** embedded rule from `otelc-pkg.gz` (`loadDefaultRules`, `match.go`), and matches them against **every** discovered dependency. The only escape hatch is `--rules` / `OTELC_RULES` — a full *replacement* of the rule set. There is no declarative "enable these" surface; third-party packages cannot ship their own rules.

A runtime-only `OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` env var exists inside generated hook code (`pkg/instrumentation/shared/otel_setup.go`) but only gates telemetry emission at runtime — it has no effect on what the compiler instrumented.

### Reference: Orchestrion (import-driven, vendor-agnostic)

DataDog's [Orchestrion](https://github.com/DataDog/orchestrion) uses the same `.tool.go` idiom:
1. **Parse** `orchestrion.tool.go` with `go/parser` + `parser.ImportsOnly` (build tag intentionally ignored).
2. **Resolve** each import path to a package via `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages`.
3. **Recursively discover** each resolved package's `orchestrion.yml` (instrumentation config) and nested `orchestrion.tool.go` files, aggregating the full aspect set.
4. A **`pin` command** scaffolds/prunes/validates the file, wires `go.mod`, and runs `go mod tidy`. Auto-pin runs during a build if the file is absent.

This makes Orchestrion **vendor-agnostic**: any third-party package can ship instrumentation by including an `orchestrion.yml`, activated by a single blank import in the user's tool file.

### Target

Adopt the import-driven model so that:
- Projects **explicitly and reproducibly** declare their enabled instrumentations.
- Instrumentation config can be **vendored by any package** that ships an `otel.instrumentation.yml`, not only rules embedded in `otelc-pkg.gz`.

This also realizes the three configuration styles already designed in `docs/ux-design.md` §"Configuration Styles" (lines 151–181):

| Style | Mechanism | Go version |
|---|---|---|
| `otel.instrumentation.go` / `otelc.tool.go` | blank-import tools file | ≥ 1.23 |
| `.otel.yml` | YAML file next to `go.mod` | any (CI/CD friendly) |

## Acceptance Criteria

### File discovery & parsing

- [ ] The tool locates a config file in the **module root** (directory containing `go.mod`), accepting **both** `otel.instrumentation.go` and `otelc.tool.go`. If both exist, behavior is explicitly defined (error or documented precedence), not a silent pick.
- [ ] Parsing uses `go/parser` with `parser.ImportsOnly` and **ignores the `//go:build tools` constraint** — the file is read even though it never compiles into the binary.
- [ ] All blank imports (`_ "path"`) are extracted. Handling of non-blank imports is documented (kept or rejected with a diagnostic).
- [ ] An absent, empty, or zero-import file is handled gracefully — no panic; falls through to the documented fallback behavior (criterion E).

### Import → config resolution (vendor-agnostic)

- [ ] Each extracted import path is resolved to a package using `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages` (consistent with existing setup-phase usage).
- [ ] For each resolved package, the tool discovers that package's `otel.instrumentation.yml` **and** any nested `otel.instrumentation.go` / `otelc.tool.go`, **recursively**, aggregating the resulting instrumentation config.
- [ ] Resolution works for packages **not** bundled in `otelc-pkg.gz` (third-party / external), proving the vendor-agnostic extension path.
- [ ] An imported package that contains no valid instrumentation config produces a clear, actionable diagnostic (and is a prune candidate per criterion D).

### Integration with the matching engine

- [ ] When a config file is present, the declared import set **scopes** which instrumentations are active, replacing all-or-nothing default matching.
- [ ] ~~Precedence across all config sources is explicitly defined, documented, and covered by tests: `otel.instrumentation.go` / `otelc.tool.go` imports → `go tool` deps → `.otel.yml` → `--rules` / `OTELC_RULES` → embedded defaults.~~
- [ ] Aggregated config feeds the existing `matchDeps` flow (`tool/internal/setup/match.go`); the `otelc.runtime.go` and `matched.json` outputs remain correct for the selected set.
- [ ] The existing "Warning: no instrumentation will be applied" path (`match.go:472`) remains correct and is not silently swallowed.

### `pin`-style command (scaffold / prune / validate)

- [ ] A new CLI subcommand (`otelc pin`) **creates** the config file if missing, with the correct `//go:build tools` tag, `package tools`, a descriptive header comment, and a `//go:generate` directive to re-run itself.
- [ ] Flags: `-prune` (default on) removes imports whose packages contain no valid config; `-validate` validates each discovered `*.instrumentation.yml` against the schema; `-generate` manages the `go:generate` directive. Defaults and behavior are documented.
- [ ] The command edits `go.mod` (adds `require` / tool deps, bumps the `go` directive if needed) and runs `go mod tidy`, reusing the replace + tidy logic in `tool/internal/setup/sync.go` where applicable. File writes are atomic (temp file + rename); comments and formatting are preserved (using `dave/dst`).
- [ ] Re-running `pin` on an already-pinned project is **idempotent** — it produces no spurious diffs.

### Auto-pin / clean-room fallback

- [ ] If no config file exists, `otelc go build` self-configures by analyzing the full dependency tree, preserving today's behavior and the clean-room usage mode described in `docs/ux-design.md` §"Clean-Room Usage".
- [ ] Auto-pin emits a clear, user-readable notice describing what it will create/modify (file, `go get`, `go mod tidy`) before acting.
- [ ] Clean-room mode leaves **no** persistent file-system changes after the build completes.

### Alternate config styles

- [ ] ~~`go tool` dependencies (go ≥ 1.24) are recognized as an equivalent declaration source, enabling the simpler `go tool otelc go build` invocation (`ux-design.md:167–170`).~~
- [ ] A `.otel.yml` file placed next to `go.mod` injects project-local instrumentation config using the same schema as `otel.instrumentation.yml`, applied only when building that module's own packages (not when the module appears as a dependency).

### Documentation & tests

- [ ] `docs/ux-design.md` is reconciled with shipped reality: document that both filenames are accepted; note any divergence between the doc's AoP `pointcut`/`advice` schema and the implemented `target`/`where`/`do` rule schema (`docs/rules.md`, ADR-0003).
- [ ] `docs/getting-started.md` and `docs/rules.md` show the new declarative workflow end-to-end.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: parsing (build-tag-ignored, blank imports, both filenames, malformed file), recursive config resolution, precedence ordering, and `pin` idempotency / prune / validate.
- [ ] An integration test (`test/`) builds a demo application whose enabled instrumentations come **only** from a checked-in `otel.instrumentation.go`, and asserts that the declared instrumentation **is** applied and that an un-declared instrumentation is **not** compiled in.

## Out of scope / follow-ups
- Removing `otelc-pkg.gz` embedding entirely (the declarative model may eventually supersede it).

## References

- Orchestrion: https://github.com/DataDog/orchestrion | `orchestrion pin` docs: https://datadoghq.dev/orchestrion/docs/getting-started/
- This repo: [`docs/ux-design.md`](docs/ux-design.md), [`docs/rules.md`](docs/rules.md), [`docs/adr/0003-structured-rule-schema.md`](docs/adr/0003-structured-rule-schema.md)
- Key source files: `tool/internal/setup/{find,match,sync,add}.go`, `tool/internal/rule/`, `tool/cmd/`

items.title: test(ci): establish and enforce >=70% unit-test coverage gate
items.body:
test(ci): establish and enforce >=70% unit-test coverage gate

Related #569
Parent: #261 (Roadmap: release 1.0.0)

---

## What this PR does

Wires a **per-tree ≥70% unit-test coverage gate** into CI so that any PR
that drops coverage below the threshold is blocked from merging.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.github/scripts/coverage-gate.sh` | **New** — threshold enforcement script |
| `Makefile` | **Modified** — three new `test-unit/*-gate` targets |
| `.github/workflows/test-unit.yaml` | **Modified** — gate steps + `done` job checks coverage |
| `docs/testing.md` | **Modified** — Coverage section documenting the target |

---

## How it works

```
make test-unit/coverage
  └─ go test -coverprofile → coverage-tool.txt   (tool/)
  └─ go test -coverprofile → coverage-pkg.txt    (pkg/)

make test-unit/coverage-gate
  └─ .github/scripts/coverage-gate.sh coverage-tool.txt 70.0
  └─ .github/scripts/coverage-gate.sh coverage-pkg.txt  70.0
```

The script parses `go tool cover -func` output, extracts the `total:` line,
and uses `awk` for float comparison (bash doesn't support floats natively).
Exit code `1` + an actionable error message when below threshold.

In CI (`test-unit.yaml`), the gate steps run **after** Codecov upload in the
`test-unit-coverage` job (Linux only, since coverage is deterministic across
platforms). The `Done (Unit Tests)` required status check now checks **both**
`test-unit.result` and `test-unit-coverage.result`, so a coverage regression
blocks merge even when all tests pass.

---

## Design decisions

- **Per-tree enforcement** (`tool/` and `pkg/` independently) prevents one area
  masking regression in the other — consistent with the project's existing
  separation of the two coverage uploads to Codecov.

- **Shell script, not Codecov threshold config** — works locally without any
  Codecov token, and gives immediate feedback in the developer terminal via
  `make test-unit/coverage-gate`. Codecov upload is preserved for historical
  dashboard tracking.

- **Gate only runs when relevant code changes** — mirrors the existing
  `if: needs.changes.outputs.tool == 'true'` conditions so doc-only or
  chore-only PRs are not blocked.

---

## Running locally

```bash
# Generate coverage files
make test-unit/coverage

# Run the gate (both trees, must be ≥70%)
make test-unit/coverage-gate

# Run for a single tree
make test-unit/tool/coverage-gate
make test-unit/pkg/coverage-gate

# Invoke the script directly
.github/scripts/coverage-gate.sh coverage-tool.txt 70.0
```

---

## Checklist

- [x] `make lint/license-header` passes (`All files have proper license headers`)
- [x] New `.sh` file carries Apache 2.0 license header
- [x] New Makefile targets registered in `.PHONY`
- [x] `done` job updated to surface coverage gate failures
- [x] `docs/testing.md` Coverage section added

---

items.title: Add a release-gating version-matrix test to verify supported ranges
items.body:
### Background
We already test forward compatibility against new releases via LatestLibBuild and LatestLibRun (see [docs/testing.md](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/main/docs/testing.md)). But these only test @latest; they never exercise the inside of a declared range like v1.2.3,v4.5.6. We assume those ranges are correct rather than verifying them (related: [#406](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/406)).

### Proposal
Add a release-gating matrix test that, for each instrumented library's declared version range, runs the existing integration suite against a small matrix of concrete in-range versions (at least lower bound + upper bound). 

Define when to run it. It could run as a release gate before each cycle, for example.

Giving a clear pass/fail that every declared range is actually exercised end to end. A failure means the declared range is incorrect, with the same range-splitting remediation as in the existing latest-lib tests.

items.title: test: add versionmatrix to verify declared version range bounds
items.body:
## Description

This adds the VersionMatrix test tier. LatestLibBuild and LatestLibRun only exercise `@latest` so the declared version ranges in the rules were assumed correct but never verified. This tier pins each test app's instrumented deps to the bounds of the declared ranges and runs the existing integration suite once per bound:

1. Lower pass: pins each dep to the lowest declared lower bound.
2. Upper pass: pins each dep to the highest published release covered by any declared range.

Ranges are half open, the cap is the first unsupported version. So for k8s client go `v0.34.0,v0.36.0` the upper bound tested is v0.35.5, not v0.36.0 itself. For open ended ranges the upper bound is the latest release so we keep testing latest as discussed in the issue. It runs weekly plus `workflow_dispatch` same cadence as LatestLibRun and opens an issue labelled `versionmatrix-failure` when it fails on main.

Two notes:

1. The lower pass currently fails for the otel rules, which I believe is the test doing its job. `hooks.yaml` declares v1.39.0 but `pkg/instrumentation/shared/go.mod` requires otel v1.43.0, and the shared module is injected into every instrumented build, so any app pinned below v1.43.0 gets forced up by MVS and otelc fails on the version mismatch. The declared v1.39.0 floor is not buildable as declared. The fix is either raising the bound in `hooks.yaml` to v1.43.0 or lowering the shared and hook module requirements. I would lean towards raising the bound since fixing the declared range is the remediation the issue describes happy to do that in this PR or as a follow up whichever you prefer.
2. The `versionmatrix-failure` label needs to be created in the repo before the notify job can open issues.


Fixes #578

This release adds support for MongoDB's [Intelligent Workload Management (IWM)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/intelligent-workload-management) and ingress connection rate limiting features. The driver now gracefully handles write-blocking scenarios and optimizes connection establishment during high-load conditions to maintain application availability.

Two new methods of `ClientOptions` are available:

- `SetMaxAdaptiveRetries` - specifies the maximum number of times the driver should retry operations that fail with a server side overload error. If not invoked, the default is 2. `MaxAdaptiveRetries` can also be set through the "maxAdaptiveRetries" URI option (e.g. "maxAdaptiveRetries=5").
- `SetEnableOverloadRetargeting` - specifies whether the driver should enable overload retargeting for operations that fail with a server side overload error. If not invoked, the default is false. `EnableOverloadRetargeting` can also be set through the "enableOverloadRetargeting" URI option (e.g. "enableOverloadRetargeting=true").

### [`v2.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/releases/tag/v2.5.0): MongoDB Go Driver 2.5.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v2.4.4...v2.5.0)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.5.0 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Highlights

This release adds a preview of CRUD support for prefix/suffix/substring indexes. Prefix, suffix and substring search are in preview and should be used for experimental workloads only. These features are unstable and their security is not guaranteed until released as Generally Available (GA). The GA version of these features may not be backwards compatible with the preview version.

Also, this release adds `AsFloat64()`, `AsFloat64OK()` to `bson.RawValue`, and `DefaultDocumentMap()` to `bson.Decoder` in the BSON package.

Additionally, this release adds `ErrorCodes()` to parse server error codes from an arbitrary Go error, and exposes `atClusterTime` in snapshot sessions.

Moreover, this release fixes several bugs, including potential heap out-of-bounds read in GSSAPI error handling.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v2.0.1...v2.1.0)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.1.0 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Notes

This release adds support for the new bulk write API added in [MongoDB 8.0](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.0/#new-bulk-write-command) and the new BSON vector datatype used in [Atlas Vector Search](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-vector-search/vector-search-overview/).

**Additionally, support for MongoDB 3.6 and below was deprecated in v2.0.0 and will be dropped in the next minor version release (v2.2.0).**

##### New BulkWrite API

The new [Client.BulkWrite](https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/mongo#Client.BulkWrite) method can perform many insert, update, and delete operations on multiple databases and collections in one request. In contrast, the existing [Collection.BulkWrite](https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/mongo#Collection.BulkWrite) method can only modify a single collection.

##### BSON Vector Datatype

The new [bson.Vector](https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson#Vector) type makes inserting and querying vector data using [Atlas Vector Search](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-vector-search/vector-search-overview/) easier and more efficient.

### [`v2.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/releases/tag/v2.0.0): MongoDB Go Driver 2.0.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v1.17.9...v2.0.0)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.0.0 of the official MongoDB Go driver.

#### Release Notes

This release includes a host of new features and several breaking changes. Below, we provide an overview of the key highlights, changes, and guidance for migrating from version 1.x to 2.0. See the [MongoDB docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/upcoming/whats-new/#what-s-new-in-2.0) for a complete list of breaking changes and additional information on what's new.

This release includes several breaking changes that users must account for when upgrading, including:

- **Options Package**: The approach to managing options has been restructured to use a builder pattern, changing how options are constructed and applied. This alteration allows for more flexible and dynamic option configurations, but may require changes to existing code that directly manipulates options objects.
- **Mongo Package**: The `Client.Connect()` method has been removed, favoring `mongo.Connect()` to streamline connection handling.
- **Event Package**: References to the `description` package have been transitioned to `event.ServerDescription` and `event.TopologyDescription`, impacting how server and topology details are accessed.
- **BSON Package Consolidation**: All previously separate BSON-related packages, including `bsoncodec`, `bsonoptions`, `bsonrw`, and `mgocompat`, have been merged into the single `bson` package. Many functionalities from these packages have been reorganized or renamed. For instance, `bson.NewRegistryBuilder` has been replaced with new APIs tailored for registry configuration, and interfaces like `ValueReader` and `ValueWriter` are now part of the consolidated `bson` package. This consolidation simplifies the package structure but requires updates to import paths and related logic.

To ease the transition to 2.0, **a comprehensive [migration guide](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/docs/migration-2.0.md) has been provided**. This guide includes detailed instructions to navigate the changes, including the updated options pattern, altered imports, and revised method signatures.

Additionally, this release deprecates support for MongoDB server versions below 3.6. Support for MongoDB 3.6 will be dropped in a future update.

New features will no longer be added to the 1.x versions. However, critical bug fixes and CVE resolutions will continue to be back-ported to 1.x versions for one year until January 15, 2026. After that date, support for 1.x versions will be discontinued.

We express our gratitude to our contributors and the community for all the support in developing this release.

items.title: Explicit, controllable ordering for do-sequence modifiers
items.body:
When a `do:` sequence applies several modifiers to one function, they run in
declaration order: the normalizer expands them in order and the instrumenter
applies them in that order. This implicit ordering covers the rules we have
today.

We may later want ordering to be explicit and controllable — an `order:` key, or
ordering across separate rules — rather than tied to declaration position. That
needs design first. In orchestrion we added namespaces to make cross-rule
ordering well defined; the equivalent here deserves the same thought before we
commit to an API.

#560 keeps ordering implicit and removed an earlier `application_index` field
that nothing consumed. This issue tracks making ordering explicit when a feature
actually needs it.

Refs #544, #560.
items.author: kakkoyun

items.title: feat(tool): add import-based instrumentation configuration support
items.body:
## Summary

Adds support for import-based instrumentation configuration through `otel.instrumentation.go` (and the compatibility alias `otelc.tool.go`).

Instrumentations are now discovered from imported instrumentation packages rather than being loaded exclusively from the built-in rule set. Instrumentation packages may recursively compose other instrumentation packages through their own tool files.

To preserve the existing zero-configuration workflow, `otelc go build` continues to support clean-room usage. When no instrumentation file is present, `otelc` generates a temporary `otel.instrumentation.go` derived from the application's dependency graph for the duration of the build and removes it afterwards.

This PR also adds a new `otelc pin` command for generating, validating, and maintaining instrumentation configuration files.

As a side effect, dependency synchronization (`go mod tidy`) now happens during the pinning stage. This ensures rule matching always operates on the final dependency graph (fixing #494).

Closes #567 

Closes #494

## Future Work

#585 -  decouple built-in instrumentations from `otelc-pkg.gz`
#586 - move `pkg/instrumentation/basic` to demo applications
#587 - add support for `.otel.yml` instrumentation configuration
items.author: amazingakai

items.title: feat(tool): decouple built-in instrumentations from `otelc-bundle.tgz`
items.body:
## Problem

Today, all built-in instrumentations are bundled into the `otelc` binary through `otelc-bundle.tgz`. As a result, instrumentation versions are tightly coupled to the version of the tool itself.

This makes it difficult for users to independently manage instrumentation versions. For example, using an older version of a particular instrumentation would require using an older version of `otelc`, even when the tool itself is otherwise compatible.

## Proposal

With `otel.instrumentation.go` support (#584), built-in instrumentations can be distributed as normal instrumentation packages instead of being embedded into the tool.

Users would then manage instrumentation versions through `go.mod`, just like any other Go dependency. `otelc pin` would generate imports to those instrumentation packages rather than relying on embedded rule definitions.

## Benefits

* Instrumentations can evolve independently of the tool.
* Users can pin instrumentation versions through `go.mod`.
* Reduces the amount of embedded data shipped with `otelc`.
* Unifies built-in and third-party instrumentation workflows.

## Related

#849

items.title: chore(pkg/instrumentation): move `pkg/instrumentation/basic` to demo applications
items.body:
## Problem

`pkg/instrumentation/basic` is a demo instrumentation package.

Since its rules target `main`, it matches nearly every application. With #584, this causes `otelc pin` to add it to generated `otel.instrumentation.go` files and pin it in `go.mod`, even though it is typically not needed by the application.

## Proposal

Move `pkg/instrumentation/basic` into the demo applications and enable it explicitly through `otel.instrumentation.go`, rather than including it in automatic instrumentation discovery.
items.author: amazingakai

items.title: feat(tool): add support for `.otel.yml` instrumentation configuration
items.body:
## Problem

The [`ux-design.md`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/5d80db178d06c17e8cc08cc20edc67d86976d04f/docs/ux-design.md) document describes a `.otel.yml` configuration style intended for CI/CD and other workflows where instrumentation configuration is preferred to be managed outside of `otel.instrumentation.go`.

This configuration style is not currently implemented.

## Proposal

Add support for a module-local `.otel.yml` file.

Proposed structure:

```yaml
instrumentations:
  - github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/instrumentation/nethttp/server
  - github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/instrumentation/gin/server
```

The `instrumentations` section declares instrumentation packages and is equivalent to importing them from `otel.instrumentation.go`.

This configuration style can be useful for CI/CD environments and for instrumenting codebases without maintaining an instrumentation tool file.

As described in `ux-design.md`, builds using `.otel.yml` are not expected to be fully reproducible. Unlike `otel.instrumentation.go`, instrumentation dependencies are not tracked directly by the Go toolchain and may be resolved dynamically during the build.
items.author: amazingakai

items.title: test(integration): avoid building unused applications during targeted integration test runs
items.body:
## Problem

The integration test suite currently builds test applications from `main_test.go` before running the tests. This improves performance when many tests reuse the same binaries, but it also means running a single test (for example `go test -run TestK8SClient`) still builds every other integration test application, even though they are not needed by the test.

This increases local iteration time and makes targeted test runs unnecessarily expensive.

## Proposal

Move application builds back to the tests that actually use them.

Tests that need the same executable multiple times can build it once and reuse it across subtests (`t.Run`), preserving the performance benefits of the current approach. At the same time, unrelated test applications would no longer be built when running a subset of the integration test suite.

This should retain the parallelization improvements from #540 while reducing unnecessary work during targeted test runs.

## Extra

Mongo client integration test currently does not use `t.Parallel()` and relies on `BuildAndRun()`, causing the test application to be rebuilt repeatedly.

As part of this work, this test could be updated to build the executable once and reuse it across subtests instead of rebuilding it repeatedly.
items.author: amazingakai

items.title: chore(tool): move `tool/cmd` to `tool/cmd/otelc` or `cmd/otelc`
items.body:
## Problem

The `otelc` command currently lives under `tool/cmd`.

When installed as a Go tool dependency, this results in the command being invoked as:

```bash
go tool cmd
```

instead of the more intuitive:

```bash
go tool otelc
```

In addition, many project docs currently refer to paths such as `cmd/otelc`, which do not match the current repository layout.

## Proposal

Move the command package to either `tool/cmd/otelc` or `cmd/otelc`. This would make the go tool invocation align with the command name (`go tool otelc`) and reduce confusion between the documented and actual package locations.
items.author: amazingakai

items.title: chore(tool): move command package to tool/cmd/otelc
items.body:
Moves the `otelc` command package from `tool/cmd` to `tool/cmd/otelc`.

When installed as a Go tool dependency, the command was invoked as `go tool cmd` instead of the more intuitive `go tool otelc`. Nesting the package one level deeper aligns the invocation with the binary name.

Updates `TOOL_DIR` in the Makefile and the `go build` path in 7 demo Dockerfiles to reference the new location. No Go import paths change since the package stays within the `tool/` tree, so `tool/internal/*` imports remain valid.

As discussed in #589, the `cmd/otelc` move (which would also require relocating `tool/internal/*`) can be done as a separate follow-up.

Fixes #589

### mongo-go-driver has Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in GSSAPI Error Handling
[CVE-2026-2303](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-2303) / [GHSA-cp6g-7hqx-qxhp](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cp6g-7hqx-qxhp)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The mongo-go-driver repository contains CGo bindings for GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication on Linux and macOS. The C wrapper implementation contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability due to incorrect assumptions about string termination in the GSSAPI standard. Since GSSAPI buffers are not guaranteed to be null-terminated or have extra padding, this results in reading one byte past the allocated heap buffer.

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 1.17.2 of the official MongoDB Go driver.

#### Release Notes

This release addresses several issues and tasks to improve the functionality of the Go Driver. It includes a fix for a bug in the `DefaultValueDecoders.ValueUnmarshalerDecodeValue` to avoid  inappropriately instantiating a pointer field decoded from null data if the user defined an `UnmarshalBSONValue`. Additionally, the release resolves a goroutine and memory leak issue found in the Zstandard (zstd) network compression decoding process.

Furthermore, the release includes a task to restore the `ReadCompressedCompressedMessage()` function to the wiremessage API. This function was previously removed under task GODRIVER-3303 with the aim of preventing out-of-bounds runtime errors, as it was identified as complicit in such issues and was not needed by the driver itself. However, it has been identified as a convenient utility for some users of the Go Driver.

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 1.17.0 of the official MongoDB Go driver.

#### Release Notes

This release adds support for client authentication using OpenID Connect (MONGODB-OIDC), and for the Queryable Encryption Range Protocol. The driver now supports MongoDB 8.0. Additionally, `IndexView` has been extended to include methods for dropping indexes by key (i.e. `DropOneWithKey` and `DropWithKey`).

> \[!NOTE]
>
> This is the last planned minor release in the 1.x series.  Future driver versions will be in the 2.x series.  The v1.17.x will still receive security and bug fixes for a year.

##### Queryable Encryption Range Protocol

Added [range protocol](https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver@v1.17.0/mongo/options#RangeOptions) support for [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/upcoming/fundamentals/encrypt-fields/#queryable-encryption).

##### MONGODB-OIDC

Added support OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication for workload identities. A workload identity is an identity you assign to a software workload, such as an application, service, script, or container, to authenticate and access other services and resources.

See the [documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/upcoming/fundamentals/enterprise-auth/#mongodb-oidc) for more details.

items.title: test(integration): avoid building unused applications during targetet integration test runs
items.body:
## Description

Moves integration test application builds from `main_test.go` back into the tests that use them.

Tests that execute the same application multiple times now build the executable once and reuse it across subtests (`t.Run`), preserving the performance improvements from #540 while avoiding unnecessary builds when running a subset of the integration test suite.

## Motivation

Building test applications globally from `main_test.go` means running a single integration test still builds every application in the integration test suite, increasing local iteration time and making targeted test runs unnecessarily expensive.

This change keeps the existing parallelization benefits while ensuring only the applications required by the selected tests are built.

Fixes #588

items.title: fix(util): allow ListFiles to walk hidden root directories
items.body:
## Description

`ListFiles` skips hidden directories during traversal by returning `filepath.SkipDir` when a directory name starts with `.`.

When the root directory passed to `ListFiles` is itself hidden, the walk terminates immediately and no files are returned, even though the caller explicitly requested traversal of that directory.

This change preserves the existing behavior for hidden subdirectories while allowing traversal of a hidden root directory passed directly to `ListFiles`.

## Motivation

`ListFiles` currently treats the root directory the same way as nested hidden directories.

As a result, calling `ListFiles` on a hidden directory returns an empty result because the walk is skipped before any files are visited. This behavior is unexpected when the hidden directory is explicitly provided by the caller.

This PR fixes that edge case and adds a regression test covering hidden root directory traversal.

items.title: feat(demo): move basic instrumentation to basic demo app
items.body:
## Description

This PR relocates the `basic` instrumentation (a test/demo helper module) from the core packages under `pkg/instrumentation/basic` directly to the basic demo application at `demo/app/basic/instrumentation`. 

Additionally, it enables import-based configuration by creating `demo/app/basic/otel.instrumentation.go` to explicitly import the moved instrumentation rather than including it in the default auto-discovery rules in the compiler tool.

Specifically, the following changes were made:
- Moved all source files, YAML configs, and `go.mod`/`go.sum` to `demo/app/basic/instrumentation`.
- Updated module import paths in the moved `go.mod` and rule paths in `demo/app/basic/instrumentation/otelc.yaml` to point to the new location.
- Created `demo/app/basic/otel.instrumentation.go` containing `import _ "github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/demo/app/basic/instrumentation"` to explicitly import the rules.
- Linked `demo/app/basic/go.mod` to use the local copy.
- Relocated command package implementation (`cmd_pin.go` to `tool/cmd/otelc/cmd_pin.go`) to prevent undefined reference build failures due to command structure refactoring in upstream/main.
- Updated documentation in `docs/testing.md` to reflect the path change.

## Motivation

Decoupling demo/testing instrumentation rules (such as `basic`) from the compiler's core registry ensures cleaner separation between actual instrumentation logic and test helpers. By moving it to the demo applications folder and explicitly importing it in the basic app using `otel.instrumentation.go`, we verify the import-based instrumentation configuration flow and keep default discovery rules focused on production-ready instrumentations.

Fixes #586

items.body:
## Description

Move instrumentation packages from `pkg/instrumentation` to a top-level `instrumentation/` directory and separate shared APIs/runtime components into dedicated packages under `pkg/`.

The resulting structure is:

```
instrumentation/
├── basic
├── database/sql
├── github.com/gin-gonic/gin
├── github.com/redis/go-redis/v9
├── go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo
├── go.opentelemetry.io/otel
├── google.golang.org/grpc/{client,server}
├── k8s.io/client-go
├── net/http/{client,server}
└── runtime

pkg/
├── hook
└── runtime
```

## Motivation

This change creates a clearer separation of responsibilities between shared APIs and instrumentation implementations.

`instrumentation/**` contains instrumentation implementations, rules, and semantic convention helpers.
`pkg/hook` contains shared hook APIs and instrumentation context.
`pkg/runtime` contains shared runtime utilities and OpenTelemetry SDK setup.

Fixes #133

items.title: test(integration/grpc): isolate grpc protobuf package into separate module
items.body:
## Description

Move the shared grpc protobuf definitions from `test/apps/grpcserver/pb` to a dedicated `test/shared/grpcpb` module.

Both `grpcclient` and `grpcserver` now depend on `grpcpb` instead of sharing code from within the `grpcserver` module.

## Motivation

Both `grpcclient` and `grpcserver` depended on `test/apps/grpcserver/pb`, which was part of the `grpcserver` module.

During parallel test execution, `otelc` could be building and instrumenting `grpcserver` while simultaneously building `grpcclient`. Instrumenting `grpcserver` updates its `go.mod` temporarily and introduces additional dependencies required by the injected instrumentation.

At the same time, the `grpcclient` build resolves packages from the `grpcserver` module through the shared `pb` package. This can result in Go observing a module state where `grpcserver` now depends on packages that are not yet reflected in the dependency graph visible to `grpcclient`, causing package resolution and build failures.

Example failure:
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/actions/runs/28017367510/job/82924978515?pr=590

By moving the protobuf definitions into a dedicated shared module, both applications depend on a stable package that is not modified during instrumentation, eliminating this source of build-time races.

Split from #584.

This change renames rule files in the built-in instrumentations to `otelc.yaml` and establishes the allowed rule file naming convention:

* `otelc.yaml`
* `*.otelc.yaml`

This aligns built-in instrumentations with the instrumentation package model introduced by `otel.instrumentation.go`, allowing them to be discovered and loaded in the same way as third-party instrumentation packages.

Using a dedicated naming convention instead of loading arbitrary `*.yaml` files makes rule discovery more reliable and avoids accidentally treating unrelated YAML files within instrumentation packages as rule definitions.

items.title: feat(tool): module-scoped (root module) glob target for first-party package selection
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Instrumentation rules select packages via `target` — an exact import path or, since #549, a glob (`tool/internal/rule/target_glob.go`). There is no way to express "instrument all packages in the application's own (root) module" without either hardcoding the module path or relying on `target: main`, which matches only the `main` package and misses sibling first-party packages.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A module-scoped target that selects the root module's packages regardless of their import paths/names.

Prior art: DataDog/orchestrion's most-used package selector is `package-filter: { root: true }` — "instrument the application's own code only" — which matches the pattern against the import path *relative to the root module* (`internal/injector/aspect/join/package.go`). An equivalent here could be:

- a `root: true` qualifier on the rule, or
- a sentinel target, or
- resolving `<module-path>/**` from `go.mod` and feeding it through the existing glob engine.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- `target: <module-path>/**` — works today *if* the author knows the module path, but it is not portable across forks/renames and forces hardcoding.
- `target: main` — only the `main` package; misses first-party sub-packages.

**Additional context**

Surfaced while reviewing #561 (glob `target` matching) against orchestrion's implementation. The glob engine added in #561 is the natural place to build on. Note that ADR-0005 (import-driven instrumentation selection) reduces but does not eliminate the need. Refs #549, #346.

Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.79.3

Security

  • server: fix an authorization bypass where malformed :path headers (missing the leading slash) could bypass path-based restricted "deny" rules in interceptors like grpc/authz. Any request with a non-canonical path is now immediately rejected with an Unimplemented error. (#8981)

Release 1.79.2

Bug Fixes

  • stats: Prevent redundant error logging in health/ORCA producers by skipping stats/tracing processing when no stats handler is configured. (grpc/grpc-go#8874)

Release 1.79.1

Bug Fixes

  • grpc: Remove the -dev suffix from the User-Agent header. (grpc/grpc-go#8902)

Release 1.79.0

API Changes

  • mem: Add experimental API SetDefaultBufferPool to change the default buffer pool. (#8806)
    • Special Thanks: @​vanja-p
  • experimental/stats: Update MetricsRecorder to require embedding the new UnimplementedMetricsRecorder (a no-op struct) in all implementations for forward compatibility. (#8780)

Behavior Changes

  • balancer/weightedtarget: Remove handling of Addresses and only handle Endpoints in resolver updates. (#8841)

New Features

  • experimental/stats: Add support for asynchronous gauge metrics through the new AsyncMetricReporter and RegisterAsyncReporter APIs. (#8780)
  • pickfirst: Add support for weighted random shuffling of endpoints, as described in gRFC A113.

  • xds: Implement :authority rewriting, as specified in gRFC A81. (#8779)
  • balancer/randomsubsetting: Implement the random_subsetting LB policy, as specified in gRFC A68. (#8650)
    • Special Thanks: @​marek-szews

Bug Fixes

  • health: Fix a bug where health checks failed for clients using legacy compression options (WithDecompressor or RPCDecompressor). (#8765)
    • Special Thanks: @​sanki92
  • transport: Fix an issue where the HTTP/2 server could skip header size checks when terminating a stream early. (#8769)

items.title: feat(demo): move basic instrumentation to basic demo app
items.body:
## Description

This PR relocates the `basic` instrumentation (a test/demo helper module) from the core packages under `pkg/instrumentation/basic` directly to the basic demo application at `demo/app/basic/instrumentation`. 

Additionally, it enables import-based configuration by creating `demo/app/basic/otel.instrumentation.go` to explicitly import the moved instrumentation rather than including it in the default auto-discovery rules in the compiler tool.

Specifically, the following changes were made:
- Moved all source files, YAML configs, and `go.mod`/`go.sum` to `demo/app/basic/instrumentation`.
- Updated module import paths in the moved `go.mod` and rule paths in `demo/app/basic/instrumentation/otelc.yaml` to point to the new location.
- Created `demo/app/basic/otel.instrumentation.go` containing `import _ "github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/demo/app/basic/instrumentation"` to explicitly import the rules.
- Linked `demo/app/basic/go.mod` to use the local copy.
- Relocated command package implementation (`cmd_pin.go` to `tool/cmd/otelc/cmd_pin.go`) to prevent undefined reference build failures due to command structure refactoring in upstream/main.
- Updated documentation in `docs/testing.md` to reflect the path change.

## Motivation

Decoupling demo/testing instrumentation rules (such as `basic`) from the compiler's core registry ensures cleaner separation between actual instrumentation logic and test helpers. By moving it to the demo applications folder and explicitly importing it in the basic app using `otel.instrumentation.go`, we verify the import-based instrumentation configuration flow and keep default discovery rules focused on production-ready instrumentations.

Fixes #586

items.title: fix(instrumentation/grpc): prevent reentrant OTel SDK initialization in BeforeDialContext
items.body:
Split from #456.

Prevents a deadlock in applications that use `grpc.DialContext` together with an OTLP gRPC exporter configured via:
```
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=...
```

The fix skips instrumentation for OTLP exporter targets before gRPC instrumentation is initialized, preventing reentrant OpenTelemetry SDK initialization.

items.title: fix(cli): handle -C flag for go build and go install
items.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to OpenTelemetry Go Compile Instrumentation!

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Fill in the description and motivation sections below
2. Complete the checklist before submitting
3. Ensure PR title follows conventional commits format (enforced by CI)

PR TITLE FORMAT (required):
  type(scope): description

  Types: chore, doc, docs, feat, fix, release, refactor, test
  Scopes: tool, pkg, demo, test, docs

  Examples:
  - feat(pkg): add gRPC client instrumentation
  - fix(tool): resolve hook signature matching issue
  - docs(api): update instrumenter interface documentation
  - refactor(pkg): simplify attribute extractor composition

BEFORE SUBMITTING:
  make format  # Format Go code and YAML files
  make lint    # Run all linters
  make test    # Run all tests (unit + integration + e2e)

If your PR adds a new user-facing instrumentation, please also submit a corresponding OpenTelemetry Registry PR:
https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/adding/

For detailed contribution guidelines, see CONTRIBUTING.md
For available make targets, run: make help
-->

## Description

This PR adds support for the `-C <dir>` flag in `otelc go build` and `otelc go install` invocations.

A new `goInvocation` struct is introduced to parse and carry all relevant information from the raw argument slice: the subcommand (`build`/`install`), the build directory extracted from `-C`, its placement relative to the subcommand (before or after), and the remaining build arguments with `-C` stripped out.

The parsed `goInvocation` is threaded through the following call chain:

- `parseGoInvocation` validates the subcommand and extracts `-C <dir>` when it appears in a supported position (immediately before or immediately after the subcommand).
- `getBuildPackages` / `splitBuildTargets` now accept a `buildDir` parameter and set `packages.Config.Dir` so that patterns like `.` and `./...` are resolved relative to `<dir>` instead of the process working directory.
- `absBuildPath`: resolves file-target paths relative to `buildDir`.
- `BuildWithToolexec` / `Cleanup`: reconstruct the `go` invocation with `-C` in the correct position and forward the build directory to all downstream steps.
- `SetupCommand` / `CleanupCommand`: thin CLI adapter wrappers that parse the invocation from `cli.Command` args before delegating to `Setup`/`Cleanup`, keeping the CLI layer decoupled from the core logic.

### Tests added

- `TestParseGoInvocation`: verifies `-C` extraction in all supported positions (before subcommand, after subcommand, and ignored when mid-args).
- `TestGetPackagesWithBuildDir`: verifies that `getBuildPackages` correctly loads packages when invoked from a directory different from the module root.
- Existing `TestGetPackages` and `TestSplitBuildTargets` call sites updated to pass the new `buildDir` parameter.

## Motivation

`otelc go build -C <dir> [pkgs]` did not respect the `-C` flag. The flag was never forwarded to the package loading step: `packages.Config` had no `Dir` set, so package patterns like `.` and `./...` were resolved against the process working directory instead of `<dir>`. This made it impossible to instrument a project located in a different directory without first `cd`-ing into it.

Fixes #507 

---

##### Breaking changes

With the launch of `custom` tools in Chat Completions, `function` tools have been renamed to clarify the difference between the two.

`ChatCompletionToolParam` has become a union and is now named `ChatCompletionToolUnionParam`.

Older versions of the SDK used function tools: to migrate

```diff
- openai.ChatCompletionToolParam{
-  Function: openai.FunctionDefinitionParam{
+ openai.ChatCompletionFunctionTool(
+  openai.FunctionDefinitionParam{
    Name:        "get_weather",
    Description: openai.String("Get weather at the given location"),
    Parameters: openai.FunctionParameters{ … },
+  },
+ )
- },
```

### [`v9.21.0`](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/compare/v9.20.1...v9.21.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/compare/v9.20.1...v9.21.0)

### [`v9.20.1`](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/releases/tag/v9.20.1): 9.20.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/compare/v9.20.0...v9.20.1)

This is a patch release containing bug fixes only. There are no new features or breaking changes; upgrading from 9.20.0 is a drop-in replacement.

#### 🚀 Highlights

##### RESP3 pub/sub message loss fixed

`PeekPushNotificationName` previously inspected only the bytes already buffered by `bufio`, so when a push frame header straddled a buffer fill boundary it could return a **truncated** notification name (e.g. `"messa"` instead of `"message"`). The push processor then mis-routed the frame and `ReadReply` silently dropped it, causing intermittent RESP3 pub/sub message loss. The peek now grows its window (36 bytes → up to 4 KiB) and reads more from the connection until the header is complete, cleanly separating incomplete prefixes from corrupt frames (including overflow-safe bulk-length handling). Fixes [#​3839](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/issues/3839).

([#​3842](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3842)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)

#### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **RESP3 push peeking**: `PeekPushNotificationName` no longer returns a truncated notification name when a push frame header spans a buffer boundary, preventing silent RESP3 pub/sub message loss (fixes [#​3839](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/issues/3839)) ([#​3842](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3842)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **`FT.HYBRID` vector params**: Vector data is now always sent via `PARAMS` with auto-generated param names (`__vector_param_N`, with collision avoidance) when `VectorParamName` is omitted, since Redis no longer accepts inline vector blobs; the `FTHybridOptions.Params` map is no longer mutated, so the same options struct can be reused across calls ([#​3844](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3844)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **`CLUSTER SHARDS` forward compatibility**: Unknown shard- and node-level attributes in the `CLUSTER SHARDS` reply are now skipped via `DiscardNext()` instead of erroring, so clients keep working when the server introduces new fields ([#​3843](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3843)) by [@​madolson](https://redirect.github.com/madolson)
- **PubSub double reconnect**: `PubSub.releaseConn` no longer reconnects twice when a connection is both unusable (or pending handoff) and reports a bad-connection error, avoiding a wasted connection establish-then-close cycle ([#​3833](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3833)) by [@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs)

#### 👥 Contributors

We'd like to thank all the contributors who worked on this release!

[@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs), [@​madolson](https://redirect.github.com/madolson), [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)

### [`v9.20.0`](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/releases/tag/v9.20.0): 9.20.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/compare/v9.19.0...v9.20.0)

#### 🚀 Highlights

##### Redis 8.8 Support

This release adds support for **Redis 8.8**. The README's supported-versions list now includes Redis 8.8 alongside 8.0/8.2/8.4, and CI exercises the `8.8` client-libs-test image across the full suite (Makefile, build workflow, doctests, run-tests action, and docker-compose).

Coverage for the new commands that ship in the 8.x line, rounded out in this release:

- **`AR*` array data type** ([#​3813](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3813)) — new array data structure, exposed via the `ArrayCmdable` interface (see the experimental-features highlight below).
- **`INCREX`** ([#​3816](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3816)) — atomic increment with expiration in a single round-trip.
- **`XNACK`** ([#​3790](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3790)) — explicit negative-acknowledge of pending stream entries.
- **`XAUTOCLAIM` PEL deletes** ([#​3798](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3798)) — `XAUTOCLAIM`/`XAUTOCLAIMJUSTID` now return the list of deleted message IDs from the pending entries list.
- **`TS.RANGE` multiple aggregators** ([#​3791](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3791)) — `TS.RANGE`/`TS.REVRANGE`/`TS.MRANGE`/`TS.MREVRANGE` accept multiple aggregators in a single call.
- **`Z(UNION|INTER|DIFF)` `COUNT` aggregator** ([#​3802](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3802)) — `COUNT` reducer for sorted-set set operations.
- **`JSON.SET FPHA`** ([#​3797](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3797)) — new `FPHA` argument that specifies the floating-point type for homogeneous FP arrays.

CI image bump ([#​3814](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3814)) by [@​ofekshenawa](https://redirect.github.com/ofekshenawa). Command coverage contributions by [@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs), [@​elena-kolevska](https://redirect.github.com/elena-kolevska), [@​Khukharr](https://redirect.github.com/Khukharr), [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov), and [@​ofekshenawa](https://redirect.github.com/ofekshenawa).

##### Stable RESP3 for RediSearch (`UnstableResp3` deprecated)

`FT.SEARCH`, `FT.AGGREGATE`, `FT.INFO`, `FT.SPELLCHECK`, and `FT.SYNDUMP` now parse RESP3 (map) responses into the same typed result objects as RESP2 — `Val()` and `Result()` work uniformly on both protocols, no flag required. Previously, RESP3 search responses required `UnstableResp3: true` and were returned as opaque maps accessible only via `RawResult()` / `RawVal()`.

As a result, the `UnstableResp3` option is now a **no-op** across every options struct (`Options`, `ClusterOptions`, `UniversalOptions`, `FailoverOptions`, `RingOptions`) and has been marked `// Deprecated:`. The field is retained for backwards compatibility — existing code that sets `UnstableResp3: true` will continue to compile and behave identically — but it will be removed in a future release and new code should not set it. `RawResult()` / `RawVal()` continue to work for callers that prefer the raw RESP payload.

([#​3741](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3741)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)

##### Experimental Array Data Structure Commands

Adds an experimental `ArrayCmdable` interface with the `AR*` command family (`ARSet`, `ARGet`, `ARGetRange`, `ARMSet`, `ARMGet`, `ARDel`, `ARDelRange`, `ARScan`, `ARSeek`, `ARNext`, `ARLastItems`, `ARGrep`, `ARGrepWithValues`, `ARInfo`/`ARInfoFull`, and typed reducers `AROpSum`/`AROpMin`/`AROpMax`/`AROpAnd`/`AROpOr`/`AROpXor`/`AROpMatch`/`AROpUsed`) for working with Redis 8.8's new array data type. **API is experimental and may change in a future release.**

([#​3813](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3813)) by [@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs)

#### ✨ New Features

- **RESP3 search parser**: First-class RESP3 parsing for `FT.SEARCH`/`FT.AGGREGATE`/`FT.INFO`/`FT.SPELLCHECK`/`FT.SYNDUMP` responses with backwards compatibility for RESP2 ([#​3741](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3741)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **INCREX**: New `INCREX` command support — atomic increment with expiration ([#​3816](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3816)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **XNACK**: Client support for the `XNACK` stream command for explicitly negative-acknowledging pending entries ([#​3790](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3790)) by [@​elena-kolevska](https://redirect.github.com/elena-kolevska)
- **TS range multiple aggregators**: `TS.RANGE`/`TS.REVRANGE`/`TS.MRANGE`/`TS.MREVRANGE` now accept multiple aggregators in a single call ([#​3791](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3791)) by [@​elena-kolevska](https://redirect.github.com/elena-kolevska)
- **`XAutoClaim` deleted IDs**: `XAUTOCLAIM`/`XAUTOCLAIMJUSTID` now return the list of deleted message IDs from the PEL ([#​3798](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3798)) by [@​Khukharr](https://redirect.github.com/Khukharr)
- **`JSON.SET FPHA`**: `JSON.SET` accepts a new `FPHA` argument that specifies the floating-point type for homogeneous floating-point arrays ([#​3797](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3797)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **Sorted-set union/intersection COUNT**: `ZUNION`/`ZINTER`/`ZDIFF` aggregator now supports `COUNT` ([#​3802](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3802)) by [@​ofekshenawa](https://redirect.github.com/ofekshenawa)
- **`FT.HYBRID` vector validation**: Validates hybrid-search vector input types and adds proper typed vector parameters ([#​3756](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3756)) by [@​DengY11](https://redirect.github.com/DengY11)
- **Cluster pool wait stats**: `ClusterClient.PoolStats()` now accumulates `WaitCount` and `WaitDurationNs` across all node pools (previously always zero) ([#​3809](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3809)) by [@​LINKIWI](https://redirect.github.com/LINKIWI)

#### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **TLS-only Cluster PubSub**: `CLUSTER SLOTS` port-0 entries now fall back to the origin endpoint's port, fixing `dial tcp <ip>:0: connection refused` on TLS-only clusters started with `--port 0 --tls-port <port>` (fixes [#​3726](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/issues/3726)) ([#​3828](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3828)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **Sharded PubSub reconnect routing**: `PubSub.conn()` now passes both regular (`c.channels`) and sharded (`c.schannels`) channels into the per-PubSub `newConn` closure. Previously, `ClusterClient.SSubscribe`-only PubSubs reconnected to a random node (because the routing closure saw an empty channel list), the `SSUBSCRIBE` was sent to the wrong shard, and the resulting `MOVED` reply was silently dropped ([#​3829](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3829)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **ClusterClient `Watch` retry**: User errors returned from a `Watch` callback are no longer subjected to cluster-retry classification; transient cluster errors still retry, but a callback returning e.g. `net.ErrClosed` short-circuits immediately ([#​3821](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3821)) by [@​obiyang](https://redirect.github.com/obiyang)
- **Sentinel concurrent-probe leak**: `MasterAddr`'s concurrent sentinel probe now closes the non-winning sentinel clients instead of leaking them ([#​3827](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3827)) by [@​cxljs](https://redirect.github.com/cxljs)
- **Sentinel rediscovery loop on master-only setups**: `replicaAddrs` no longer tears down the cached sentinel client when the replica list is empty, eliminating a continuous rediscovery loop on master-only Sentinel deployments that flooded logs and added per-operation latency ([#​3795](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3795)) by [@​shahyash2609](https://redirect.github.com/shahyash2609)
- **Pool `CloseConn` hooks**: `Pool.CloseConn` now triggers registered hooks, fixing a memory leak when connections are closed explicitly rather than via the normal removal path ([#​3818](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3818)) by [@​ndyakov](https://redirect.github.com/ndyakov)
- **Dial TCP error redirection**: Wrapped `dial tcp` errors are now correctly classified as redirectable so cluster routing can recover from a single unreachable node ([#​3810](https://redirect.github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/3810)) by [@​vladisa88](https://redirect.github.com/vladisa88)

### [`v2.7.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/releases/tag/v2.7.0): MongoDB Go Driver 2.7.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v2.6.2...v2.7.0)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.7.0 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Highlights

This release adds support for sending afterClusterTime on writes in causally consistent sessions, improving alignment between read and write behavior in session-based workflows. It also continues cleanup of session-related and internal-only APIs by deprecating the experimental session API, helping clarify which surfaces are intended for long-term public use. Alongside that, the release includes a handful of targeted quality improvements across BSON validation, change streams, and error reporting to make the driver more predictable and easier to debug.

### [`v2.6.2`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/releases/tag/v2.6.2): MongoDB Go Driver 2.6.2

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v2.6.1...v2.6.2)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.6.2 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Highlights

This release excludes non-I/O TLS errors from backpressure labels, aligning error labeling more closely with the CMAP specification. This fixes cases where protocol-level TLS handshake failures, such as certificate validation, hostname mismatch, fatal alerts, or malformed record headers, could be incorrectly classified as overload-related errors. As a result, these failures are handled more accurately during connection establishment and SDAM/pool error processing.

<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at v2.6.2 -->

### [`v2.6.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/releases/tag/v2.6.0): MongoDB Go Driver 2.6.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v2.5.1...v2.6.0)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.6.0 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Highlights

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> Go Driver v2.6 will be the last minor version to support MongoDB 4.2. Go Driver v2.7 will require MongoDB 4.4 or newer.

This release adds support for MongoDB's [Intelligent Workload Management (IWM)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/intelligent-workload-management) and ingress connection rate limiting features. The driver now gracefully handles write-blocking scenarios and optimizes connection establishment during high-load conditions to maintain application availability.

Two new methods of `ClientOptions` are available:

- `SetMaxAdaptiveRetries` - specifies the maximum number of times the driver should retry operations that fail with a server side overload error. If not invoked, the default is 2. `MaxAdaptiveRetries` can also be set through the "maxAdaptiveRetries" URI option (e.g. "maxAdaptiveRetries=5").
- `SetEnableOverloadRetargeting` - specifies whether the driver should enable overload retargeting for operations that fail with a server side overload error. If not invoked, the default is false. `EnableOverloadRetargeting` can also be set through the "enableOverloadRetargeting" URI option (e.g. "enableOverloadRetargeting=true").

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v2.4.4...v2.5.0)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.5.0 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Highlights

This release adds a preview of CRUD support for prefix/suffix/substring indexes. Prefix, suffix and substring search are in preview and should be used for experimental workloads only. These features are unstable and their security is not guaranteed until released as Generally Available (GA). The GA version of these features may not be backwards compatible with the preview version.

Also, this release adds `AsFloat64()`, `AsFloat64OK()` to `bson.RawValue`, and `DefaultDocumentMap()` to `bson.Decoder` in the BSON package.

Additionally, this release adds `ErrorCodes()` to parse server error codes from an arbitrary Go error, and exposes `atClusterTime` in snapshot sessions.

Moreover, this release fixes several bugs, including potential heap out-of-bounds read in GSSAPI error handling.

items.title: feat(instrumentation): auto initialize otel sdk on startup
items.body:
## Summary

This PR introduces automatic OpenTelemetry SDK initialization during startup.

## Motivation

1. Prevents reentrant calls to `SetupOTelSDK` in the gRPC client, avoiding potential deadlocks during SDK initialization.
2. Removes the need for third-party instrumentations (#612) to depend on `pkg/runtime` in their `go.mod`. Instrumentations can now assume that the OpenTelemetry tracer and meter providers have already been initialized.
3. With `otel.instrumentation.go` support, users can exclude this instrumentation module and provide their own tracer/metric providers.

---

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format
- [x] Code formatted: `make format`
- [x] Linters pass: `make lint`
- [x] Tests pass: `make test`
- [ ] Tests added for new functionality
- [ ] Tests follow [testing guidelines](docs/testing.md)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [ ] OpenTelemetry Registry updated (if applicable, see [registry guide](docs/instrument-guide.md#4-register-the-instrumentation))

items.title: feat(tool): add root module rule target
items.body:
## Description

Adds `target: $root` for instrumentation rules.

During setup, `$root` is resolved from the build root module and expanded to `<module-path>/**`. Matching then goes through the existing glob target path, so this does not add a separate package-matching branch.

Fixes #611

## Motivation

Rules that target first-party code currently need either `target: main` or a hardcoded module path.

`target: main` only covers the main package, and hardcoding the module path is awkward for forks or renamed modules. `$root` gives rule authors a portable way to match the root package and its subpackages.

---

## Checklist

  - [x] PR title follows [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format
  - [x] Code formatted: `gofmt`
  - [ ] Linters pass: `make lint`
    - `make lint/go` passes locally
    - full `make lint` hits unrelated YAML formatting diffs in this Windows checkout
  - [x] Tests pass: `make test`
  - [x] Tests added for new functionality
  - [x] Tests follow [testing guidelines](docs/testing.md)
  - [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
  - [ ] OpenTelemetry Registry updated (not applicable)
