items.body:
Bumps [google.golang.org/grpc](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go) from 1.75.0 to 1.79.3.
Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.79.3

Security

  • server: fix an authorization bypass where malformed :path headers (missing the leading slash) could bypass path-based restricted "deny" rules in interceptors like grpc/authz. Any request with a non-canonical path is now immediately rejected with an Unimplemented error. (#8981)

Release 1.79.2

Bug Fixes

  • stats: Prevent redundant error logging in health/ORCA producers by skipping stats/tracing processing when no stats handler is configured. (grpc/grpc-go#8874)

Release 1.79.1

Bug Fixes

  • grpc: Remove the -dev suffix from the User-Agent header. (grpc/grpc-go#8902)

Release 1.79.0

API Changes

  • mem: Add experimental API SetDefaultBufferPool to change the default buffer pool. (#8806)
    • Special Thanks: @​vanja-p
  • experimental/stats: Update MetricsRecorder to require embedding the new UnimplementedMetricsRecorder (a no-op struct) in all implementations for forward compatibility. (#8780)

Behavior Changes

  • balancer/weightedtarget: Remove handling of Addresses and only handle Endpoints in resolver updates. (#8841)

New Features

  • experimental/stats: Add support for asynchronous gauge metrics through the new AsyncMetricReporter and RegisterAsyncReporter APIs. (#8780)
  • pickfirst: Add support for weighted random shuffling of endpoints, as described in gRFC A113.
    • This is enabled by default, and can be turned off using the environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_PF_WEIGHTED_SHUFFLING. (#8864)
  • xds: Implement :authority rewriting, as specified in gRFC A81. (#8779)
  • balancer/randomsubsetting: Implement the random_subsetting LB policy, as specified in gRFC A68. (#8650)
    • Special Thanks: @​marek-szews

Bug Fixes

  • credentials/tls: Fix a bug where the port was not stripped from the authority override before validation. (#8726)
    • Special Thanks: @​Atul1710
  • xds/priority: Fix a bug causing delayed failover to lower-priority clusters when a higher-priority cluster is stuck in CONNECTING state. (#8813)
  • health: Fix a bug where health checks failed for clients using legacy compression options (WithDecompressor or RPCDecompressor). (#8765)
    • Special Thanks: @​sanki92
  • transport: Fix an issue where the HTTP/2 server could skip header size checks when terminating a stream early. (#8769)
    • Special Thanks: @​joybestourous
  • server: Propagate status detail headers, if available, when terminating a stream during request header processing. (#8754)
    • Special Thanks: @​joybestourous

Performance Improvements

  • credentials/alts: Optimize read buffer alignment to reduce copies. (#8791)
  • mem: Optimize pooling and creation of buffer objects. (#8784)
  • transport: Reduce slice re-allocations by reserving slice capacity. (#8797)

... (truncated)

[1.43.0/0.65.0/0.19.0] 2026-04-02

  • Synchronization issues in global trace delegate implementation. (#1686)
  • Reduced excess memory usage by global TracerProvider. (#1687)

items.title: chore(integration/kafka): improve the quality assurance
items.body:
LGTM once the other review comments are addressed.

A couple of non-blocking comments from my side:

1. Should we also have an e2e test for this?
2. grpc and net/http instrumentations use `client/` and `server/` subdirectories. Could we follow the same convention here and use `producer/` and `consumer/`? It's not super important right now, but with `otel.instrumentation.go` support users could choose to enable only one of them.

Also, once this is merged, we'll need to add it to the OpenTelemetry registry (same for OpenAI instrumentation), similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io/pull/10609. Would you like to take care of that, or should I?

_Originally posted by @amazingakai in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pull/302#pullrequestreview-4619075652_

## Description

Adds \`has_package\`, a \`where.file\` leaf predicate that matches source files by their declared \`package\` clause (\`AST.Name.Name\`), not by import path (\`target\`) or test-ness (\`is_test\`).

## Motivation

\`target\` and \`is_test\` together can't distinguish \`package foo_test\` from \`package foo\`: they share the same import path and the same test build. The declared package clause is the only discriminator. This matters when a rule should apply only to external test files, or only to internal ones.

This gap was flagged during the \`is_test\` (#562) review and tracked in #551 after target globbing (#561) and \`is_test\` (#562) landed.

## Summary

Consolidates the dependency bumps requested across the currently open dependabot and renovate PRs into a single reviewed change, instead of merging 16 separate PRs. Bumps `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` core to v1.44.0, the otlp exporters, `google.golang.org/grpc`, `golang.org/x/net`, and related third-party deps to the versions those PRs requested, propagated via `make crosslink && make go-mod-tidy` across every module in the repo.


Fixes #641 #640 #639 #638 #634 #633 #632 #631 #626 #615 #613 #614 #602 #601 #600 #599 (dependabot)
Fixes #623 (renovate `all-deps`)

**Left out on purpose** (each one broke real behavior under test, not just a version number):

- **k8s.io/client-go** — bumping to v0.36.2 forces a go1.26 toolchain requirement; capping at v0.35.6 to stay on go1.25 still breaks the compile-instrumentation tool's cached-path tracking during `TestK8SClient` (`cannot replace .../v0.34.0/... with .../v0.35.6/...`). No open dependabot PR requested this bump — only renovate's broad sweep — so it's left untouched.
- **demo/app/basic's `golang.org/x/time`** — `instrumentation/basic/otelc.yaml` has a test fixture with version-range hook rules keyed exactly on this dependency (`v0.14.0,v0.15.0` → one hook fires, `>=v0.15.0` → a different one). Bumping past v0.15.0 (which renovate's own PR also requests) silently crosses that boundary and breaks `TestBasic`.
- **otelmongo** (`go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/otelmongo`) — the v0.52.0 → v0.69.0 jump crosses an OTel semantic-convention migration (`db.operation`/`net.peer.name` → `db.operation.name`/`network.peer.address`), breaking `TestMongoClient`'s assertions on the old attribute names. Left at v0.52.0; everything else in that module (mongo-driver core, snappy, klauspost/compress, etc.) is still bumped.
- **#624** (renovate `major-all-deps`, mongo-driver v1→v2) — a separate breaking major-version migration, not something to fold into a routine dependency bump.

Also bumped several `test/apps/*` fixture modules (grpcclient, grpcserver, logslogrus, logslog, otelsdk, redisclient, mongoclient, openaiclient, ginserver) that pin the same third-party libraries independently of the instrumentation modules they exercise. A version mismatch between a fixture app and the instrumentation library it builds against crashes the compiler toolexec with a stale-cache-path error, so these needed matching bumps to keep the corresponding integration tests passing.

## Test plan

- [x] `make build` — clean
- [x] `make build-demo` — clean
- [x] `make test-unit` — all pass
- [x] `go test -tags integration` for every non-Docker-dependent test (Basic, GRPCClient, GRPCServer, HTTPClient, HTTPServer, DBClient, LogsSlog, LogsLogrus, OtelSDKSpanFromContext, RedisClient, MongoClient, OpenAIClient, GinServer) — all pass
- [ ] `TestKafkaClient` / `TestK8SClient` — not verifiable locally (this sandbox has no working Docker daemon for testcontainers); should run in CI

## Related

Filed #644 for the underlying tool bug this uncovered: the compile-instrumentation tool crashes when a target library's version diverges across `go.mod` files that pin the same package (e.g. an `instrumentation/*` module and its `test/apps/*` fixture). This PR works around it by keeping those pins aligned; #644 tracks fixing it at the tool level.

items.title: chore: Make auto dependency upgrades supported range aware
items.body:
## Summary

Compile-instrumentation crashes when a target library's version diverges between two `go.mod` files that pin it independently, e.g. `instrumentation/google.golang.org/grpc/client` and `test/apps/grpcclient`. The tool writes instrumented output to the old cached module path while the compiler reads the new one:

```
cannot replace .../pkg/mod/<module>@vOLD/file.go with $WORK/.../file.go
```

Hit this three times consolidating #643's bumps: `k8s.io/client-go`, `google.golang.org/grpc` (`test/apps/grpcclient`, `grpcserver`, `test/bench/scenarios/multi`), and `segmentio/kafka-go` (`test/apps/kafkaclient`). Fixed by hand each time.

## Why bots miss it

Dependabot/renovate operate on one `go.mod` at a time and don't cover `test/apps/*` or `test/bench/*` at all, so fixture pins drift silently until an integration build crashes on them.

## Proposed direction

Configure renovate to group updates by package name across each `instrumentation/*` module and its matching `test/apps/*`/`test/bench/scenarios/*` fixture (`packageRules` + `matchFileNames` + `groupName`), so one PR bumps both sides together. Keeps fixtures pinned to exactly what the instrumentation module supports, no separate PR to drift out of sync.

Ref #643.

items.title: fix(instrumentation/otel): decouple trace instrumentation from sdk/trace
items.body:
## Summary

This PR decouples the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` instrumentation
from the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` instrumentation and
reorganizes the OpenTelemetry instrumentation layout.

## Motivation

Previously, the trace instrumentation used `go:linkname` to reference
`spanFromGLS` from the SDK trace instrumentation.

This meant that if an application's build graph contained
`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` but not
`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`, the trace instrumentation would
still be applied, but linking would fail because `spanFromGLS` was not
present in the final binary.

With this change, the SDK trace instrumentation registers its GLS lookup
within `pkg/runtime`. The trace instrumentation retrieves it
through the runtime instead of referencing SDK internals directly.

As a result, applications that do not include the SDK trace package now
build successfully. In those cases, `trace.SpanFromContext` simply
returns its original result, since no GLS state exists.

<details>
<summary>Example build failure</summary>

```
github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/instrumentation/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/hook.spanFromContextOnExit: relocation target go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace.spanFromGLS not defined
Error:
[0] failed to run command "/usr/local/go/pkg/tool/linux_amd64/link" in dir '""' with args: [-o $WORK/b001/exe/a.out -importcfg $WORK/b001/importcfg.link -X=runtime.godebugDefault=cryptocustomrand=1,tlssecpmlkem=0,urlstrictcolons=0 -buildmode=exe -buildid=6Jzn2EIzQ-sdhmAMu1e7/ggJrGToNWo4_RjZo0yLs/bd5xtSEH6fO7cTrbEzqn/6Jzn2EIzQ-sdhmAMu1e7 -extld=gcc $WORK/b001/_pkg_.a]: exit status 2
```



</details>

## Other changes

- reorganize the OpenTelemetry instrumentation layout to make it easier
  to navigate
- remove unused files such as `metric_test_func_holder.go` and
  `span_setup.go`
- add documentation describing the OpenTelemetry SDK instrumentation

items.title: perf(tool): optimize package name discovery for file-only rules to avoid AST parsing on the hot path
items.body:
# Issue: Optimize package name discovery for file-only rules on the hot path

## Description
Currently, in [match.go](file:///d:/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/internal/setup/match.go#L144-L151), the tool chain parses source files on the hot path to discover the package name for file-only rules using `ast.ParseFileOnlyPackage`:

```go
// TODO: Optimize package name discovery for file-only rules to avoid
// parsing source files on the hot path.
tree, err := ast.ParseFileOnlyPackage(dep.Sources[0])
if err != nil {
    return nil, err
}
set.SetPackageName(tree.Name.Name)
```

Since the setup/instrumentation phase runs during compilation, performing AST parsing of source files on the hot path increases build times, especially for large projects with numerous file-level rules.

## Proposed Optimization
We should optimize package name discovery to avoid parsing source files on the hot path. Possible approaches include:
1. Caching discovered package names.
2. Fast regex/string scanning of the package declaration at the start of the source files rather than full AST parsing.
3. Pre-extracting package names during the setup phase.

items.title: refactor(tool): optimize package name discovery for file-only rules
items.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to OpenTelemetry Go Compile Instrumentation!

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Fill in the description and motivation sections below
2. Complete the checklist before submitting
3. Ensure PR title follows conventional commits format (enforced by CI)

PR TITLE FORMAT (required):
  type(scope): description

  Types: chore, doc, docs, feat, fix, release, refactor, test
  Scopes: tool, pkg, demo, test, docs

  Examples:
  - feat(pkg): add gRPC client instrumentation
  - fix(tool): resolve hook signature matching issue
  - docs(api): update instrumenter interface documentation
  - refactor(pkg): simplify attribute extractor composition

BEFORE SUBMITTING:
  make format  # Format Go code and YAML files
  make lint    # Run all linters
  make test    # Run all tests (unit + integration + e2e)

If your PR adds a new user-facing instrumentation, please also submit a corresponding OpenTelemetry Registry PR:
https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/adding/

For detailed contribution guidelines, see CONTRIBUTING.md
For available make targets, run: make help
-->

## PR Title
refactor(tool): optimize package name discovery for file-only rules

fixes #648 

## Description

This PR optimizes the package name discovery phase for file-only rules during the compile setup step. 

Key changes:
- Introduced `ast.ParsePackageName` in `tool/internal/ast/parser.go`, which uses the standard library `go/parser` directly to read the package name without AST/DST decoration.
- Updated `tool/internal/setup/match.go` to use `ast.ParsePackageName` instead of `ast.ParseFileOnlyPackage`.
- Added a unit test `TestParsePackageName` in `tool/internal/ast/ast_test.go` to verify the functionality.
- Added benchmarks comparing `ParseFileOnlyPackage` and `ParsePackageName` in `tool/internal/ast/ast_test.go`.

## Motivation

When executing file-only rules, the setup step previously parsed source files using `ast.ParseFileOnlyPackage`. While this only parsed the package clause, it still invoked full AST/DST decoration and comment mapping via the `decorator` package, introducing unnecessary overhead on the compilation hot path. This optimization avoids the decoration overhead.

### Benchmark Results
Below are the benchmark results comparing the original `ParseFileOnlyPackage` (with DST/AST decoration) against the optimized `ParsePackageName` (without decoration) when parsing `parser.go` (136 lines):

```text
goos: windows
goarch: amd64
BenchmarkParseFileOnlyPackage-16    	    1765	    626382 ns/op	   17141 B/op	      86 allocs/op
BenchmarkParsePackageName-16        	    6126	    204047 ns/op	   12538 B/op	      31 allocs/op
```

- **Execution Speed:** ~3x faster (~204 µs vs. ~626 µs)
- **Allocated Bytes:** ~1.37x less memory (12.5 KB vs. 17.1 KB)
- **Heap Allocations:** ~2.7x fewer allocations (31 vs. 86)

Fixes #648

---

items.title: feat(tool): add otelc pin command
items.body:
Split from https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pull/584

## Summary

This PR introduces the `otelc pin` command for managing `otel.instrumentation.go`.

The setup path has also been updated to use `AutoPin`, which generates a temporary `otel.instrumentation.go` by inferring the required instrumentations from the user's build graph.

Today, `AutoPin` uses the built-in embedded ruleset to determine the required instrumentations. In the future, the intention is to integrate with the OpenTelemetry Registry so that compile-time instrumentations published there can also be discovered and pinned automatically.

## Issues

Closes https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/567

This is the final step needed to complete that work.

Also closes https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/494

This PR moves dependency synchronization (`syncDeps`) into `Pin`.

As a result, if dependency versions change while generating `otel.instrumentation.go`, setup will re-parse the compile commands using the updated dependency graph before matching instrumentation rules. This avoids generating a stale ruleset for the instrumentation phase.

items.title: fix(cli): handle -C flag for go build and go install
items.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to OpenTelemetry Go Compile Instrumentation!

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Fill in the description and motivation sections below
2. Complete the checklist before submitting
3. Ensure PR title follows conventional commits format (enforced by CI)

PR TITLE FORMAT (required):
  type(scope): description

  Types: chore, doc, docs, feat, fix, release, refactor, test
  Scopes: tool, pkg, demo, test, docs

  Examples:
  - feat(pkg): add gRPC client instrumentation
  - fix(tool): resolve hook signature matching issue
  - docs(api): update instrumenter interface documentation
  - refactor(pkg): simplify attribute extractor composition

BEFORE SUBMITTING:
  make format  # Format Go code and YAML files
  make lint    # Run all linters
  make test    # Run all tests (unit + integration + e2e)

If your PR adds a new user-facing instrumentation, please also submit a corresponding OpenTelemetry Registry PR:
https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/adding/

For detailed contribution guidelines, see CONTRIBUTING.md
For available make targets, run: make help
-->

## Description

This PR adds support for the `-C <dir>` flag in `otelc go build` and `otelc go install` invocations.

A new `goInvocation` struct is introduced to parse and carry all relevant information from the raw argument slice: the subcommand (`build`/`install`), the build directory extracted from `-C`, its placement relative to the subcommand (before or after), and the remaining build arguments with `-C` stripped out.

The parsed `goInvocation` is threaded through the following call chain:

- `parseGoInvocation` validates the subcommand and extracts `-C <dir>` when it appears in a supported position (immediately before or immediately after the subcommand).
- `getBuildPackages` / `splitBuildTargets` now accept a `buildDir` parameter and set `packages.Config.Dir` so that patterns like `.` and `./...` are resolved relative to `<dir>` instead of the process working directory.
- `absBuildPath`: resolves file-target paths relative to `buildDir`.
- `BuildWithToolexec` / `Cleanup`: reconstruct the `go` invocation with `-C` in the correct position and forward the build directory to all downstream steps.
- `SetupCommand` / `CleanupCommand`: thin CLI adapter wrappers that parse the invocation from `cli.Command` args before delegating to `Setup`/`Cleanup`, keeping the CLI layer decoupled from the core logic.

### Tests added

- `TestParseGoInvocation`: verifies `-C` extraction in all supported positions (before subcommand, after subcommand, and ignored when mid-args).
- `TestGetPackagesWithBuildDir`: verifies that `getBuildPackages` correctly loads packages when invoked from a directory different from the module root.
- Existing `TestGetPackages` and `TestSplitBuildTargets` call sites updated to pass the new `buildDir` parameter.

## Motivation

`otelc go build -C <dir> [pkgs]` did not respect the `-C` flag. The flag was never forwarded to the package loading step: `packages.Config` had no `Dir` set, so package patterns like `.` and `./...` were resolved against the process working directory instead of `<dir>`. This made it impossible to instrument a project located in a different directory without first `cd`-ing into it.

Fixes #507

items.title: chore: Implement `isSetup` check in the setup phase
items.body:
## Description
In `tool/internal/setup/setup.go`, the function `isSetup()` is a stub that always returns `false`:

```go
// This function can be used to check if the setup has been completed.
func isSetup() bool {
	// TODO: Implement Task
	return false
}
```

Because it always returns `false`, the compilation/setup pipeline executes the entire setup process (extracting embedded modules, matching dependencies to hook rules, generating runtime code, backing up module files, etc.) even when the setup was already successfully completed in a prior invocation.

## Proposed Solution
We can detect whether the setup has been completed by checking if a valid `state.json` file is present. In the tool's architecture, `StateManager.Commit()` is called at the end of a successful `Setup()` invocation to write the `state.json` metadata file to the build temp directory.

By invoking the existing `LoadStateManager()` helper, we can check if the state file is present and readable:
1. If `LoadStateManager()` returns a non-nil `StateManager` and no error, setup has been completed (`isSetup` should return `true`).
2. If it returns a nil `StateManager` or an error, it indicates setup is not yet complete or the state is invalid (`isSetup` should return `false`).

### Proposed Change in `tool/internal/setup/setup.go`
```go
func isSetup() bool {
	stateManager, err := LoadStateManager()
	return err == nil && stateManager != nil
}
```

## Verification Plan
1. Add a unit test `TestIsSetup` in `tool/internal/setup/setup_test.go`.
2. The test should:
   - Verify `isSetup()` returns `false` in a clean environment.
   - Write a mock `state.json` file to the temporary build directory.
   - Verify `isSetup()` returns `true` when the file is present.
   - Remove the state file and verify `isSetup()` returns `false` again.

items.title: chore(integration/kafka): split instrumentation into producer and consumer submodules
items.body:
## Description

The `segmentio/kafka-go` instrumentation lived in a single module that hooked both `(*Writer).WriteMessages` and `(*Reader).ReadMessage`. This splits it into two submodules, following the same `client/` + `server/` layout that `grpc` and `net/http` already use:

- `producer/` holds the write-side hooks (`BeforeWriteMessages` / `AfterWriteMessages`), with its own `go.mod` and `otelc.yaml`.
- `consumer/` holds the read-side hooks (`BeforeReadMessage` / `AfterReadMessage`) and the public `ExtractContext` helper, again with its own `go.mod` and `otelc.yaml`.
- The shared `semconv/` package stays under the root instrumentation module, the same way `grpc/semconv` and `net/http/semconv` do (the old `kafka-go/go.mod` is removed so `semconv` is covered by the root module).

The existing unit tests moved with their hooks into the new packages, so producer and consumer are each covered on their own.

## Motivation

Right now a user pulls in the producer and consumer instrumentation together because they share one module. With the `otel.instrumentation.go` selection mechanism, splitting them lets a service enable only the side it needs, for example a write-only publisher that never consumes. This matches how `grpc` and `net/http` already let you pick `client` or `server` independently, so kafka now follows the same convention.

This came out of the review discussion on #302.

Fixes #635

items.title: bug: go get -tool workflow fails or builds an unusable otelc in v0.5.0
items.body:
## Description

Following the documented Go tool dependency installation workflow does not produce a working `otelc` with v0.5.0.

I found two separate problems while trying to instrument a minimal Go `net/http` application.

## Reproduction

### 1. Documented vanity import path fails

The documented workflow uses:

```sh
go get -tool go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/cmd/otelc@latest
```

With v0.5.0 this fails with:

```text
go: module go.opentelemetry.io/otelc@latest found (v0.5.0), but does not contain package go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/cmd/otelc
```

Trying the apparent package path without the final `/otelc` also fails because the module declares a different module path:

```sh
go get -tool go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/cmd@latest
```

```text
go: go.opentelemetry.io/otelc@v0.5.0 (matching go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/cmd@latest) requires go.opentelemetry.io/otelc@v0.5.0: parsing go.mod:
        module declares its path as: github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation
                but was required as: go.opentelemetry.io/otelc
```

### 2. GitHub module path installs, but the built tool is unusable

Using the GitHub module path and the actual CLI package path succeeds:

```sh
go get -tool github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/cmd@v0.5.0
go tool github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/cmd go build -o bin/http-otelc-demo .
```

But running the tool fails at setup time:

```text
Error:
[0] failed to read file: open otelc-pkg.gz: file does not exist
[1] extracting embedded instrumentation pkg

Stack:
[0] .../tool/data/export.go:18 tool/data.ReadEmbedFile
[1] .../tool/internal/setup/extract.go:133 tool/internal/setup.(*SetupPhase).extract
[2] .../tool/internal/setup/setup.go:247 tool/internal/setup.Setup
[3] .../tool/internal/setup/setup.go:508 tool/internal/setup.GoBuild
```

## Expected behavior

The documented `go get -tool` / `go tool` workflow should install and run a working `otelc`, or the docs should clearly state that users must build from source with `make build` for v0.5.0.

## Actual behavior

* The documented vanity import path does not resolve to the documented CLI package.
* The GitHub module path can compile the CLI package, but the resulting tool cannot run because `otelc-pkg.gz` was not generated/embedded.

## Workaround

Building from source works:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.5.0 https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation.git
cd opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation
make build
```

This generates `tool/data/otelc-pkg.gz` and produces a working `otelc` binary.

## Environment

* otelc version: v0.5.0
* Go version: go1.26.4 linux/amd64
* OS: Linux amd64

## Related

I saw #585, but that appears to be a future design proposal for decoupling built-in instrumentations from `otelc-pkg.gz`. This issue is specifically about the current v0.5.0 documented installation path failing or producing an unusable tool.

items.title: chore: Add E2E tests for Gin and Redis integrations
items.body:
## Summary

The `test/e2e/` directory currently covers three instrumentation stacks:

| E2E Test | File |
|---|---|
| HTTP client + server | `http_test.go` |
| gRPC client + server | `grpc_test.go` |
| Kafka producer + consumer | `kafka_test.go` |

Both **Gin** and **Redis** have solid integration tests (`gin_server_test.go`, `redis_client_test.go`) but **no E2E tests**. Per [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md):

> E2E tests spin up multiple processes (e.g. an instrumented client and an instrumented server) and verify they produce a coherent trace with spans from every participant sharing the same trace ID.

Integration tests use in-process or in-memory dependencies (e.g. `miniredis`). E2E tests go one step further: real external processes + real dependencies.

---

## Motivation

### Gin — E2E test (`test/e2e/gin_test.go`)

The Gin integration test (`gin_server_test.go`) verifies server-side span enrichment in isolation:

- Route pattern resolution (`GET /hello/:name`)
- `c.Error()` surfacing as `span.Status = Error`
- 5xx responses carrying `error.type`

What it **cannot** test: whether the gin server correctly **receives** a trace context from a real HTTP client and links the client and server spans into a single distributed trace. That requires running `httpclient` + `ginserver` as two separate processes sharing a collector — exactly the E2E pattern.

**Proposed `TestGin` structure** (mirrors `http_test.go`):

```go
func TestGin(t *testing.T) {
    f := testutil.NewTestFixture(t)

    f.BuildAndStart("ginserver", "-port=8090")
    testutil.WaitForTCP(t, "127.0.0.1:8090")

    f.BuildAndRun("httpclient", "-addr", "http://127.0.0.1:8090", "-name", "OTel")

    f.RequireTraceCount(1)    // one distributed trace
    f.RequireSpansPerTrace(2) // httpclient span + ginserver span

    clientSpan := testutil.RequireSpan(t, f.Traces(), testutil.IsClient, ...)
    serverSpan := testutil.RequireSpan(t, f.Traces(), testutil.IsServer, ...)

    // Server span must carry the gin-specific http.route attribute
    testutil.RequireAttribute(t, serverSpan, string(semconv.HTTPRouteKey), "/hello/:name")
    // Span name must use route template, not literal path
    require.Equal(t, "GET /hello/:name", serverSpan.Name())
    // Both spans share the same trace ID
    require.Equal(t, clientSpan.TraceID(), serverSpan.TraceID())
}
```

This validates the **full propagation chain**: `httpclient` → W3C `traceparent` header → `ginserver` context extraction → linked consumer span.

---

### Redis — E2E test (`test/e2e/redis_test.go`)

The Redis integration test uses **miniredis** (in-process fake). It cannot verify behavior against a real Redis broker — for example, whether connection metadata attributes (`server.address`, `server.port`) are populated correctly, or whether span creation works under real network conditions.

**Proposed `TestRedis` structure** (uses testcontainers, mirrors `kafka_test.go`):

```go
func TestRedis(t *testing.T) {
    if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
        t.Skip("redis testcontainer not supported on windows")
    }

    addr := startRedisContainer(t)

    f := testutil.NewTestFixture(t)
    f.SetEnv("REDIS_ADDR", addr)

    out := f.BuildAndRun("redisclient")
    require.Contains(t, out, "testvalue")

    // Three operations → three spans
    f.RequireTraceCount(1)
    f.RequireSpansPerTrace(3) // SET + GET + DEL

    traces := f.Traces()

    setSpan := testutil.RequireSpan(t, traces, testutil.IsClient,
        testutil.HasAttribute("db.operation.name", "set"),
    )
    require.Equal(t, "set", setSpan.Name())
    testutil.RequireAttribute(t, setSpan, "db.system.name", "redis")
    testutil.RequireAttributeExists(t, setSpan, "server.address")
    testutil.RequireAttributeExists(t, setSpan, "server.port")
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> The three Redis spans are all emitted from **one** process. `RequireTraceCount(1)` + `RequireSpansPerTrace(3)` here verifies span grouping under a single trace root — distinct from the multi-process case for Gin, but still not possible with miniredis which doesn't exercise the TCP path.

---

## Proposed Work

### Files to add
- `test/e2e/gin_test.go` — `TestGin`: two-process E2E (httpclient + ginserver), trace correlation, `http.route` attribute
- `test/e2e/redis_test.go` — `TestRedis`: single-process against real Redis via testcontainers, `server.address`/`server.port` attributes

### Files to modify
- `test/apps/redisclient/main.go` — read `REDIS_ADDR` env var (currently flag-only `-addr`) so the E2E test can inject it without changing the integration test invocation

### No new test apps needed
Both `ginserver`, `httpclient`, and `redisclient` already exist in `test/apps/`.

---

## Checklist for Implementation

- [ ] `test/e2e/gin_test.go`: `TestGin` with `RequireTraceCount(1)` + `RequireSpansPerTrace(2)`, assert `http.route`, span name uses route template
- [ ] `test/e2e/redis_test.go`: `TestRedis` with real Redis container, assert `server.address`, `server.port`, `db.operation.name` on SET/GET/DEL spans  
- [ ] `test/apps/redisclient/main.go`: fall back to `REDIS_ADDR` env var if `-addr` flag not set
- [ ] `make all` passes (format, lint, test)

---

## References

- [docs/testing.md — E2E Tests](docs/testing.md)
- Existing E2E test pattern: [`test/e2e/http_test.go`](test/e2e/http_test.go), [`test/e2e/kafka_test.go`](test/e2e/kafka_test.go)
- Gin integration test: [`test/integration/gin_server_test.go`](test/integration/gin_server_test.go)
- Redis integration test: [`test/integration/redis_client_test.go`](test/integration/redis_client_test.go)
- Gin instrumentation: [`instrumentation/github.com/gin-gonic/gin/context_hook.go`](instrumentation/github.com/gin-gonic/gin/context_hook.go)
- Redis instrumentation: [`instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/hook.go`](instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/hook.go)

## Summary

- **`OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`** - Early-return from `SetupOTelSDK()` when set to `"true"` (case-insensitive). The upstream Go SDK doesn't support this yet ([#3559](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/3559)).
- **Exporter selection** - All three signals use `autoexport` and honor `OTEL_*_EXPORTER` (`otlp`/`console`/`none`). Traces previously only worked with an OTLP endpoint set.
- **Logger provider** - Added `setupLoggerProvider` mirroring traces and metrics.

Redis E2E is intentionally out of scope for this PR. Redis instrumentation is single-process, so there's no second span to correlate and it can't exercise the cross-process axis this suite is designed to enforce — dropped per @txabman42's review.

## Motivation

We already had integration coverage for Gin behavior, but lacked dedicated E2E validation that proves cross-process propagation into Gin route instrumentation.

This PR:
- Verifies trace header propagation from instrumented client to instrumented Gin server.
- Validates Gin-specific route semantics in E2E output (including route-template behavior).

items.title: fix(state): make StateManager crash-safe with incremental atomic persistence
items.body:
Based on: https://github.com/kakkoyun/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pull/10

## Summary

Make StateManager crash-safe with incremental atomic persistence

Previously the state manifest was written only once at the end of a successful build via an explicit `Commit()`. A crash (SIGKILL, OOM, CI cancellation) before that point left no trace on disk, making it impossible for a subsequent `otelc cleanup` to restore the tree.

## Changes

- `Track()` now calls `Commit()` before returning, persisting the manifest incrementally after every tracked file. No explicit `Commit()` needed from callers.
- `Commit()` uses `WriteFileAtomic` (temp file + rename) so a crash mid-write never leaves a truncated manifest.
- Add `Discard()` to remove the consumed manifest and snapshots after a successful `Revert`.
- A failed revert in `Cleanup()` no longer deletes snapshots, they are preserved as the only recovery path.
- Increase test timeout from 10m to 15m for latestlibbuild, latestlibrun, and versionmatrix tests.

items.title: feat: otelc toolexec drop-in via GOFLAGS fails (missing matched.json; work-dir permission denied in module cache)
items.body:
## What happened

We want `otelc` to work as an Orchestrion-style drop-in, where users point the
Go toolchain at `otelc` through `GOFLAGS` and run a normal `go build`:

```sh
export GOFLAGS="${GOFLAGS} '-toolexec=otelc toolexec'"
go build ./...
```

Today this path fails, while `otelc go build` succeeds on the same module.

## Reproduction

Environment: `otelc` installed via `make install` from `main`
(`v0.0.0-20260710101053-1324a37eb0eb`), Go 1.26.5, macOS. Minimal module with a
`net/http` `main`.

**Case 1 — no prep step:**

```sh
export GOFLAGS="${GOFLAGS} '-toolexec=otelc toolexec'"
go build .
```

```
failed to read file ./.otelc-build/matched.json: open ./.otelc-build/matched.json: no such file or directory
  tool/internal/instrument/match.go:21  (*InstrumentPhase).load
  tool/internal/instrument/toolexec.go:115  interceptCompile
  tool/internal/instrument/toolexec.go:362  Toolexec
```

The compile interceptor expects `.otelc-build/matched.json`, which is only
produced by the setup phase that `otelc go build` runs.

**Case 2 — after `otelc setup`:**

`otelc setup` does generate `.otelc-build/matched.json`, `otel.instrumentation.go`,
and `otelc.runtime.go`. The subsequent drop-in build then fails differently:

```
failed to create work directory ".../go/pkg/mod/golang.org/x/sys@v0.45.0/unix/.otelc-build": mkdir ...: permission denied
  tool/cmd/otelc/main.go:129  initLogger
```

When the toolchain invokes `otelc toolexec` for a dependency package, `otelc`
tries to create its `.otelc-build` work directory inside the (read-only) module
cache directory of that package, rather than under the build root.

## Expected

The `-toolexec=otelc toolexec` drop-in (optionally after an `otelc setup` /
`otelc pin` prep step) should build successfully and produce the same
instrumented binary as `otelc go build`, so `otelc` is a true drop-in for the
Orchestrion `GOFLAGS` workflow.

## Control

`otelc go build -o app .` succeeds on the same module.

## Why now

We plan to document this drop-in usage in the v1 announcement blog post, so it
would be good to have it working before the v1 release.

items.title: fix(setup): serialize concurrent otelc invocations with a build lock
items.body:
## Description

Adds a build lock so concurrent otelc invocations against the same module can no longer corrupt it. Every mutating entry point in the setup package — `Setup`, `GoBuild`, `Cleanup`, and `Pin` — acquires an OS advisory file lock (via `gofrs/flock`) around its whole body. A second invocation logs that it is waiting and blocks until the holder finishes or the wait is canceled with Ctrl-C. Because the lock is advisory, the OS releases it when the holding process dies, so a crashed build can never wedge the module.

Design points worth knowing before reviewing:

- The lock lives in the setup package's entry points, not in the CLI layer, and nested chains reuse the outer lock through a context marker (same idiom as `ContextWithStateManager`). `GoBuild -> Setup -> AutoPin -> Pin` and GoBuild's deferred `Cleanup` therefore never re-acquire, and a verb added later is serialized by construction instead of by remembering boilerplate. `toolexec` runs as a child of the locked build and never calls these entry points, so it stays outside the lock and Go's internal build parallelism is untouched.
- The lock file is a sibling of the build dir (`.otelc-build.lock`), not inside it: `cleanup` deletes `.otelc-build/` while holding the lock, and Windows refuses to delete a file the process itself has open. The Windows CI leg caught this; POSIX unlink had masked it.
- The file exists only while an invocation runs. Release removes it in an order that is safe on POSIX and Windows, every acquisition attempt reopens the path and verifies the locked handle still matches it, and unexpected stat failures surface as errors instead of silent retries. A leftover file from a killed process holds no lock, never blocks anyone, and gets reused and cleaned up by the next run — the waiting message spells out that only a live invocation can cause waiting.
- The work dir is canonicalized through `EvalSymlinks` so `/tmp/x` and `/private/tmp/x` (macOS) contend on one lock, and a work dir that does not exist degrades to a no-op acquisition so `otelc cleanup` on a never-set-up tree stays a true no-op.
- `GoBuild` validates its arguments before locking; a bad command line fails immediately instead of waiting behind a running build.
- `otelc pin` landed while this branch was in progress; it rewrites go.mod/go.sum through the same window, so it is one of the locked entry points.
- `test/go.mod`/`test/go.sum` are retidied: `gofrs/flock` raises the module graph's `golang.org/x/sys` floor to v0.46.0.

`gofrs/flock` (BSD-3, no transitive dependencies beyond `x/sys`) was picked over a hand-rolled `O_EXCL` pidfile because stale-lock handling across the three supported OSes is exactly the part that is easy to get wrong.

Known limitation, documented in code: the lock is scoped to one module's work dir, so in a `go.work` workspace two invocations for different member modules still share `go.work.sum` unserialized. That needs a workspace-scoped lock and is left for a follow-up.

## Motivation

Nothing serializes concurrent otelc runs in one module today. When a second build starts while the first is mid-setup, it snapshots the already-mutated go.mod as its "original"; whichever run restores last bakes the replace directives into go.mod for good. The two runs also race on `.otelc-build/` itself, deleting each other's import-tracking files and clobbering `matched.json`.

This is easy to hit without doing anything unusual: an IDE save-hook firing while a terminal build runs, or two CI jobs sharing a checkout. Reproduced before the fix with two parallel `otelc go build` runs: one build fails, the other "succeeds", and go.mod keeps all 8 replace directives. With the lock, both runs exit 0 and go.mod comes back pristine.

## Verification

- Unit tests: mutual exclusion between concurrent acquisitions, cancellation while waiting, lock-file removal on release, a pre-existing stale file not blocking acquisition, nested re-entrancy through the context marker, and the missing-work-dir no-op.
- `go test ./tool/...` green; golangci-lint clean; the repo-wide `go mod tidy` consistency check passes.
- End-to-end: the concurrent-build repro flips from corrupted go.mod to both builds exiting 0 with go.mod restored.
- Full CI matrix (linux/macos/windows, amd64/arm64) green on my fork first: kakkoyun#11.

---

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format
- [x] Code formatted: `make format`
- [x] Linters pass: `make lint`
- [x] Tests pass: `make test`

- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) — behavior is documented in code; no user-facing doc pages affected

items.title: bug(GLS): reused pool goroutines keep a stale parent span forever, parenting later requests into the wrong trace
items.body:
GLS trace context is copied from parent to child goroutine in one place: the `runtime.newproc1` hook (`instrumentation/runtime/otelc.yaml`), the only call site of `propagateOtelContext`. Nothing removes a span from a goroutine's GLS except that goroutine ending the span itself. `ClearTraceContext` has no callers in any rule, and there is no goexit hook.

Worker pools break this model. Pools like `ants` spawn workers lazily inside `Submit`, so a worker created during one request inherits that request's span and keeps it for its entire life:

1. Request A is in flight; its span is on the handler goroutine's GLS.
2. The pool spawns a worker for the first time from inside that handler. `newproc1` clones the GLS, and the worker now holds span A (`Clone` in `otel_trace_context.go` copies the tail span).
3. Span A ends. `End` removes it from the ending goroutine's GLS only. The worker's copy survives, its `SpanContext` stays valid, and the `recordingSpan` stays pinned for as long as the worker lives.
4. Request B submits a task that starts a span from `context.Background()`. `afterSpanFromContext` (`instrumentation/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace/hook.go`) substitutes the stale span A, and `tracer.Start` uses it as the parent.

From then on, every span started this way on that worker lands in request A's trace. A propagation gap would produce an orphaned root; this produces a wrong parent, silently. Workers pre-spawned before any span exists get empty clones and only produce orphan roots, so whether you get contamination depends on which request happened to spawn the worker. That makes it hard to reproduce and harder to notice.

## Reproduction

Built with `otelc` at `1324a37` (`make build`), Go 1.25.10, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` and `otel/sdk` v1.44.0. Full program below; the pool is a minimal hand-rolled version of what `ants` does (worker goroutine spawned lazily by the first `Submit`), so the mechanism is dependency-free.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/stdout/stdouttrace"
	sdktrace "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace"
	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
)

type pool struct {
	tasks   chan func()
	started bool
}

func (p *pool) Submit(f func()) {
	if !p.started {
		p.started = true
		go func() { // worker spawned here: newproc1 clones the submitter's GLS
			for t := range p.tasks {
				t()
			}
		}()
	}
	p.tasks <- f
}

var workers = &pool{tasks: make(chan func(), 16)}

func spanInfo(prefix string, sc trace.SpanContext) {
	fmt.Printf(">>> %s trace_id=%s span_id=%s\n", prefix, sc.TraceID(), sc.SpanID())
}

func main() {
	exp, err := stdouttrace.New()
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	tp := sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(sdktrace.WithBatcher(exp))
	otel.SetTracerProvider(tp)
	defer func() { _ = tp.Shutdown(context.Background()) }()

	http.HandleFunc("/a", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		spanInfo("REQUEST-A-SERVER-SPAN", trace.SpanFromContext(r.Context()).SpanContext())
		done := make(chan struct{})
		workers.Submit(func() { // first Submit: worker is born under span A
			defer close(done)
			time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
		})
		<-done
		fmt.Fprintln(w, "a done")
	})

	http.HandleFunc("/b", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		spanInfo("REQUEST-B-SERVER-SPAN", trace.SpanFromContext(r.Context()).SpanContext())
		done := make(chan struct{})
		workers.Submit(func() {
			defer close(done)
			// correct Go: a deliberately detached root span
			_, span := otel.Tracer("repro").Start(context.Background(), "job-from-b")
			defer span.End()
			spanInfo("JOB-FROM-B", span.SpanContext())
			time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
		})
		<-done
		fmt.Fprintln(w, "b done")
	})

	fmt.Println("listening on :8123")
	_ = http.ListenAndServe(":8123", nil)
}
```

```
otelc go build -o glsrepro-instr .
./glsrepro-instr &
curl localhost:8123/a; curl localhost:8123/b; curl localhost:8123/b
```

Observed (span records from the stdouttrace exporter):

```
GET        trace: 33f812d2d3eb1917...  span: 866fcc9e92d178a8  parent: none        <- request A
GET        trace: 6040b14277bd4f2e...  span: 11b491150c138f1d  parent: none        <- request B1
job-from-b trace: 33f812d2d3eb1917...  span: c74dcd4c0e1ab6ed  parent: 866fcc9e92d178a8
GET        trace: 4a893d42d43119b5...  span: 725c84375da0eb9e  parent: none        <- request B2
job-from-b trace: 33f812d2d3eb1917...  span: 84674481151d221a  parent: 866fcc9e92d178a8
```

Both `job-from-b` spans, submitted by two different later requests, are parented under request A's
server span, in request A's trace, after span A ended. The application code is correct Go; the
wrong parent comes entirely from the injected propagation.

One precondition worth its own attention: the repro only triggers when the application imports
`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk` itself (here via its own `TracerProvider` setup). In the
zero-config case, where the app imports only the API and `otelc` injects the SDK, the
`instrumentation/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` module is not selected, because module
selection runs against the pre-instrumentation dependency graph. The build then contains the
`newproc1` copy and the `SpanFromContext` fallback but no GLS pushes at all, so cross-goroutine
propagation and `GetTraceAndSpanID` are silently inert. In other words: `otelc` does not instrument
the SDK it injects. That looks like a separate bug; happy to file it separately.

## Prior art

The two GLS lineages this project merged handled the problem differently.

dd-trace-go with Orchestrion never copies GLS at spawn. Its runtime aspects are the `g` field, same-goroutine accessors, and a `goexit1` hook that nils the slot (`internal/orchestrion/gls.orchestrion.yml`). `Finish` pops the entry, entries finished from another goroutine are reclaimed on the holder's next push, and an explicit context always wins over GLS (DataDog/dd-trace-go#4528). Their failure mode at goroutine boundaries is a visible trace split, and their docs call that expected behavior. Contamination requires an application bug, namely a span that never finishes.

loongsuite-go-agent copies at spawn like `otelc` does, and ships dedicated pool plugins (`pkg/rules/goants-v1`, `goants-v2`) because spawn-time copy cannot cover pooled workers.

`otelc` currently has the copy-at-spawn model with neither the pool plugins nor documentation of the limitation.

## Possible directions

In rough order of value per effort:

1. Skip ended spans in the fallback: `afterSpanFromContext` (or `tail()`) ignores spans that have ended. Contamination degrades to an orphan root, matching Datadog's failure mode, and the pinned `recordingSpan` gets released. Needs an "ended" signal readable from the hook.
2. Clean up on span end across GLS clones, or clear GLS in a goexit hook the way Orchestrion does. The goexit hook helps recycled goroutines but not long-lived pool workers.
3. Pool-aware rules for common pool libraries, following loongsuite's goants plugins.
4. Document the limitation and emit a diagnostic (debug log or metric) when the GLS fallback supplies a parent, so the behavior is at least discoverable.

Related, probably separate issues: the same fallback re-parents intentional root spans started from `context.Background()` on any goroutine with a non-empty GLS, and past `OTEL_GLS_MAX_SPANS` the tracker drops adds silently while `tail()` keeps returning a wrong parent. Neither behavior is in `docs/configuration.md`. I can file these separately.

items.title: fix: toolexec goflags dropin
items.body:
Contributing to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/671

This solves `Case 2`, we'll need another PRs for fixing `Case 1`.

Main changes:
1. **Work-dir discovery (DiscoverWorkDir)**: walk up from cwd to .otelc-build, bounded by go.mod, instead of trusting cwd (which may be the read-only module cache for asm/cgo).
2. **GOFLAGS strip at startup**: remove -toolexec so spawned go children don't recurse.
3. **-V=full rewrite**: append an otelc@<version>/<rulesHash> marker to the tool ID so instrumented and plain artifacts never share build-cache entries.
4. **Nested version-only toolexec (OTELC_NESTED_TOOLEXEC)**: keep archives resolved during instrumentation aligned with the outer build's cache keys.
5. **Actionable error when matched.json is missing + docs**.

items.title: fix(gls): prevent stale parents in pooled goroutines
items.body:
## What

A worker reused by a pool could retain a span copied into its GLS after that span had ended. Later work on that worker could then be parented to the old request trace.

## Why

Each goroutine had its own GLS wrapper. Ending a span only removed the wrapper visible to the goroutine that called `End`, so copies held by pooled workers could stay valid indefinitely. This also happened when a span was ended from another goroutine.

## How

  - Track shared lifecycle state for each valid SDK span.
  - Mark that state before removing it when the span ends.
  - Ignore ended GLS entries when reading or cloning context.
  - Add integration coverage for reused workers, cross-goroutine `End`, and sampled-out spans.
  - Verify with `make test`, Go lint, and license-header checks.

  Closes #673

items.title: Add compile-time instrumentation for anthropic-sdk-go (gen_ai.* spans)
items.body:
## Summary

Add zero-code, compile-time instrumentation for `github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go`
producing GenAI client spans, mirroring the merged OpenAI instrumentation
(`instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/`, #604).

## Motivation

- OpenAI Go SDK instrumentation landed in #604 (v1/v2/v3). `anthropic-sdk-go` is the other
  major Go LLM SDK with no otelc coverage.
- Go still trails Python here: `opentelemetry-python-contrib` ships dedicated GenAI
  instrumentations, while Go users get at most an `http.client` span with no `gen_ai.*`
  attributes.
- The cost is low: `anthropic-sdk-go` is Stainless-generated like `openai-go`, so the
  established pattern transfers almost 1:1 — `anthropic.NewClient(opts ...option.RequestOption)`
  accepts `option.WithMiddleware(...)` with the exact same middleware signature the openai
  hook injects (`instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/hook.go`).

## Scope — Phase 1 (traces)

New module `instrumentation/github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go/` following the openai-go
layout (`otelc.yaml`, `hook.go`, `middleware.go`, `streaming.go`, `semconv/`), per
`docs/instrument-guide.md`.

**Hook point** — one `inject_hooks` rule on `anthropic.NewClient` that prepends
`option.WithMiddleware(OtelMiddleware())`, gated by `runtime.Instrumented("ANTHROPIC")`,
with `runtime.SuppressHTTPClientInstrumentation` to avoid a duplicate `net/http` client span
(same as `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/hook.go:46` / `middleware.go:154`).

**Instrumented calls** (both hit `POST /v1/messages`; classified by URL path suffix, so
`/v1/messages/count_tokens` and `/v1/messages/batches` are excluded for free):

- Non-streaming: `client.Messages.New(ctx, MessageNewParams)` (sdk `message.go:56`)
- Streaming: `client.Messages.NewStreaming(ctx, MessageNewParams)` returning
  `ssestream.Stream[MessageStreamEventUnion]` (sdk `message.go:86`) — detected via
  `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, same as openai (`middleware.go:172-177`)

**Span**: name `chat <model>`, `SpanKindClient`, `gen_ai.operation.name=chat`,
`gen_ai.provider.name=anthropic` (host-keyword mapping like openai's `providerMapping`, default
`anthropic`).

**Attributes** (same `semconv/genai.go` helper set as openai):

| Attribute | Anthropic wire source |
|---|---|
| `gen_ai.request.model` | request `model` |
| `gen_ai.request.max_tokens` | request `max_tokens` (required in this API) |
| `gen_ai.request.temperature` / `top_p` / `top_k` | request fields (note: `top_k` exists here, unlike openai) |
| `gen_ai.request.is_stream` | SSE response detected |
| `gen_ai.response.id` / `gen_ai.response.model` | response `id` / `model` |
| `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` | single `stop_reason` (`end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `stop_sequence`, `tool_use`, `pause_turn`, `refusal`) wrapped in a 1-element slice |
| `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` / `output_tokens` | `usage.input_tokens` / `usage.output_tokens` |
| `gen_ai.usage.total_tokens` | computed `input+output` — Anthropic has no `total_tokens` field (design question below) |
| `error.type` + span status | transport error or HTTP ≥ 400, as in `middleware.go:157-170` |

**Streaming accumulation** — Anthropic SSE differs from OpenAI's: named events
(`event: X\ndata: {json}`), no `data: [DONE]`; stream ends with `message_stop`. The
`streamingReader` accumulates:

- `message_start` → response id, model, `usage.input_tokens`
- `message_delta` → `delta.stop_reason` + cumulative `usage.output_tokens`
- `message_stop` → finalize (plus EOF/Close safety net, as in openai `streaming.go:72-87`)
- `gen_ai.response.time_to_first_token` from the first chunk, as today

**Tests/demo**, mirroring #604: unit tests beside hooks; `test/apps/anthropicclient/` +
`test/integration/anthropic_client_test.go` asserting via
`testutil.RequireGenAIClientSemconv` (`test/testutil/semconv.go:136`); optional
`demo/app/anthropic/`.

**Opt-in content capture (new capability — flagged)**: neither openai-go nor any other
instrumentation in this repo currently captures prompts/completions, and there is no
`OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` handling today. I'd like Phase 1 to include opt-in capture of
`messages[]`/`system` (input) and `content[]` blocks (output) as span events, disabled by
default behind an env var — but only if maintainers want this repo to take a position on the
gen-ai content-capture semconv now; otherwise it moves to Phase 2 and Phase 1 stays a strict
port of the openai pattern.

## Scope — Phase 2 (stretch)

- Tool-use visibility: `stop_reason=tool_use` details / `gen_ai.tool.*` when semconv settles
- GenAI client metrics (`gen_ai.client.token.usage`, `gen_ai.client.operation.duration`)
- `Messages.CountTokens` (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`) spans
- Content capture as span events if deferred from Phase 1

## Non-goals

- Batches API (`client.Messages.Batches.*`) — async, not a single client span
- Bedrock/Vertex transports of the SDK (`aws/`, `vertex/` subpackages) — different signing
  clients; base-URL provider mapping covers proxies in the meantime
- Beta namespace (`client.Beta.*`) — same `/v1/messages?beta=true` surface can be a follow-up
- Metrics/logs in Phase 1

## Open design questions for maintainers

1. **SDK version pin**: latest is v1.57.0. Pin the rule with a `version:` lower bound (e.g.
   `v1.0.0,`) or leave open like openai's rule (no version range)? Only one major version
   exists, so no v2/v3-style duplication yet.
2. **`gen_ai.usage.total_tokens`**: Anthropic responses have no `total_tokens`. Compute
   `input+output` (keeps `RequireGenAIClientSemconv` reusable) or omit? Also: cached-token
   counts (`cache_read_input_tokens`) have semconv now — worth adding?
3. **Streaming accumulation approach**: extend the SSE-line reader from openai's
   `streaming.go` to typed Anthropic events (proposed), vs. hooking the SDK's own
   `(*Message).Accumulate` — the middleware approach keeps everything at the HTTP layer and
   avoids depending on SDK internals.
4. **Env-var naming**: reuse the repo-wide `OTEL_GO_ENABLED/DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` gate
   with key `ANTHROPIC` (matching `OPENAI`), yes? And if content capture is in scope, which
   env var name should gate it — the semconv-suggested
   `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT`?
5. **`gen_ai.system`**: openai-go emits both the deprecated `gen_ai.system` and
   `gen_ai.provider.name`. Same for anthropic, or provider.name only?

## Plan (12 weeks, LFX Term 3)

- **W1-2**: finalize design per maintainer answers; scaffold module (`otelc.yaml`, `hook.go`,
  `semconv/`), non-streaming middleware + unit tests → first PR
- **W3-4**: streaming reader (named-event SSE, `message_delta` accumulation, TTFT) + unit tests
- **W5-6**: `test/apps/anthropicclient` + integration test (mock server, streaming +
  non-streaming), error paths (4xx/5xx, transport)
- **W7-8**: demo app + docs (`docs/getting-started.md` entry), review iterations, merge Phase 1
- **W9-10**: content capture (span events, opt-in) or Phase 2 metrics — per maintainer priority
- **W11**: `CountTokens` support; OpenTelemetry registry entry per `docs/instrument-guide.md` §4
- **W12**: buffer for review, hardening, follow-up issues (Beta namespace, Bedrock/Vertex)

## Prior work

- #474 (merged): databasesql DSN parsing coverage (libpq KV, MySQL no-parens, SQLite URI)
- #516 (open, under review): Gin HTTP server compile-time instrumentation — same
  rule+hook+integration-test workflow this proposal follows

items.title: test(test): shard and cache integration test builds
items.body:
## Description

This PR changes the integration test workflow so the suite is split into deterministic top-level test shards, then adds an optional per-app Go build cache for standard integration test apps.

Changes included:

- Add `INTEGRATION_TEST_RUN` to `make test-integration` so CI can pass a top-level test-name regex.
- Split each platform's integration job into three shards with `SHARD_INDEX` and `SHARD_TOTAL`.
- Keep the coverage integration job unsharded and at its existing 20 minute timeout.
- Add `OTELC_TEST_GOCACHE` support in `testutil.Build` for standard `test/apps` builds.
- Use `${OTELC_TEST_GOCACHE}/${app}` as the cache directory so apps never share compile cache entries.
- Drop `-a` only for that cache-enabled standard-app path so warm builds can reuse compile outputs.
- Restore and save the otelc Go build cache in CI with an exact cache key only. There is no broad restore prefix.
- Make the required `done` job fail closed when change detection fails, and require both coverage and sharded integration jobs to pass when relevant files changed.
- Document the sharding and cache behavior in `docs/testing.md`.
- Handle the current `main` lint issue in the build-lock wait path after rebasing.

## Motivation

Issue #676 tracks integration test runtime control. The limiting CI leg on `main` was the Windows integration job from run `29241290051`, which took 17m57s. The Ubuntu amd64 job took 12m57s, the coverage integration job took 12m15s, and the macOS arm64 job took 6m21s.

The slow path is not the subtests. Top-level integration tests spend most of their time in `otelc go build -a`, which recompiles the standard library and dependency tree for each app. Locally, the full integration suite took `real 487.74s` before this change.

This PR tackles the issue in two parts:

1. CI sharding reduces per-job wall-clock by running disjoint top-level test partitions in parallel.
2. Per-app build caches reduce repeated compile work across runs while avoiding cross-app cache collisions.

Fixes #676

## Verification

Local verification run with:

```sh
OTELC_TEST_GOCACHE=/tmp/otelc-test-gocache-phase2 \
DOCKER_HOST=unix://$HOME/.colima/otel-issue-676/docker.sock \
TESTCONTAINERS_DOCKER_SOCKET_OVERRIDE=/var/run/docker.sock \
make all
```

Result:

```text
PASS
ok  go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/test/e2e  56.081s
```

Additional local checks:

- `make lint/action` passed.
- Shard partition check found 24 top-level tests, 8 per shard, with a complete disjoint union.
- One local shard ran end to end and passed 8 top-level tests.
- Cache spike passed `go -C test test -count=2 -tags integration -run '^TestHTTPServer$' ./integration/...`.
- Full local cache measurement passed all 24 top-level tests in both runs:
  - Cold per-app cache: `real 261.12s`, Go package elapsed `226.018s`.
  - Warm per-app cache: `real 154.63s`, Go package elapsed `121.287s`.
- Targeted cache correctness checks passed with `OTELC_TEST_GOCACHE` set:
  - `TestExplicitInstrumentationSelection`
  - `TestVendoredBuild`
  - `TestAutoPin_RemovesGeneratedToolFile`

CI verification on this PR:

- All checks passed.
- Integration workflow run: `29262400645`.
- `Done (Integration Tests)` passed.

Integration job timing comparison:

| Platform | Main baseline | Worst PR shard | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Windows amd64 | 17m57s | 9m32s | 8m25s faster |
| Ubuntu amd64 | 12m57s | 7m27s | 5m30s faster |
| Ubuntu arm64 | 9m05s | 2m58s | 6m07s faster |

The worst sharded integration job is now Windows shard 0 at 9m32s, below the previous 15 minute timeout pressure point.

items.title: feat(instrumentation): add Anthropic Go SDK instrumentation (non-streaming)
items.body:
Adds compile-time instrumentation for github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go, producing GenAI client spans for the non-streaming Messages API. This is the first phase of #679 and follows the pattern established by the openai-go instrumentation.

The rule hooks anthropic.NewClient and injects an HTTP middleware via option.WithMiddleware, gated by the ANTHROPIC instrumentation key. The middleware classifies POST /v1/messages calls (the path suffix keeps count_tokens and batches out of scope), starts a client span, and suppresses the underlying net/http client span so there is no duplicate.

Attributes follow the gen_ai semantic conventions: request model, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, and top_k (top_k is Anthropic specific, with no openai equivalent), provider name, response id and model, finish reasons, and token usage. Anthropic returns a single stop_reason rather than per-choice finish_reason values, so it is wrapped into a one element slice to keep the shared RequireGenAIClientSemconv helper reusable. The API has no total_tokens field, so it is computed from input plus output. Prompt-cache usage (cache_read and cache_creation input tokens) is recorded when present.

Per the design discussion in #679, this covers only the non-streaming path. The streaming reader is left as a documented stub and will land in a follow-up once the accumulation approach is confirmed. Content capture is deferred to a later phase.

The rule is pinned to a v1.0.0 lower bound so the single module covers a broad version range.

Tested with unit tests covering the hook, operation classification, provider mapping, request parsing, and the full span shape including the cache-token cases. An integration test app and mock-server test mirror the openai-go setup and run under the existing integration CI.

Part of #679

Note that actionlint starts to embed the timezone database in the executables from this version so the binary sizes slightly increase. ([#​641](https://redirect.github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/641), thanks [@​martincostello](https://redirect.github.com/martincostello))
  ```yaml
  on:
    schedule:
      # ERROR: The timezone is not a valid IANA timezone string
      - cron: '*/5 * * * *'
        timezone: 'Asia/Somewhere'
  ```
- Support the [`jobs.<job_name>.environment.deployment` configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/control-deployments#using-environments-without-deployments). ([#​639](https://redirect.github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/639), thanks [@​springmeyer](https://redirect.github.com/springmeyer))
- Support the [`macos-26-intel` runner label](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-02-26-macos-26-is-now-generally-available-for-github-hosted-runners/). ([#​629](https://redirect.github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/629), thanks [@​hugovk](https://redirect.github.com/hugovk))
- Fix the [table of webhook activity types](https://redirect.github.com/rhysd/actionlint/blob/main/all_webhooks.go) are outdated by rebuilding the [script to scrape the table](https://redirect.github.com/rhysd/actionlint/tree/main/scripts/generate-webhook-events) from scratch.
- Support Go 1.26 and drop the support for Go 1.24. Now supported versions are 1.25 and 1.26.
- Tests are run on arm64 Windows in CI.
- Update the popular actions data set to the latest.

items.title: Spec-correct messaging instrumentation: shared layer + kafka-go up to spec + IBM/sarama (builds on #705)
items.body:
## Summary

(Reshaped per the Slack discussion with @kakkoyun and @txabman42, and to compose
with #705.)

Bring otelc's messaging instrumentation up to the messaging semantic conventions:
a shared messaging semconv layer, kafka-go migrated onto it with the span-links
fix, a process-span story for the zero-code gap, batch attributes and messaging
metrics, and IBM/sarama as the first new client. nats.go as stretch.

This project deliberately builds on #705 (per-instrumentation configuration):
the links-migration flag becomes one of its config options rather than a
mechanism of its own. If both run in Term 3, #705 ships the mechanism and this
project is its first real consumer.

## Current state (verified against main)

Our only messaging instrumentation is segmentio/kafka-go
(`instrumentation/github.com/segmentio/kafka-go/`). It already does a lot right:
producer-side context injection into message headers, consumer-side extraction,
and a solid attribute set including `messaging.consumer.group.name`, partition,
offset, and message key (`semconv/client.go`). The gaps:

1. **Parent-child where the spec says link.** `AfterReadMessage` starts the
   consumer span with the extracted producer context as its parent
   (`consumer_hook.go`), while its own comment says it "links to the producer".
   The messaging semconv is explicit: "For each message it accounts for, the
   'Process' or 'Receive' span SHOULD link to the message's creation context",
   with span links called out as "the default mechanism to correlate producers
   and consumer(s)". Parent-child appears in the spec only as a MAY for
   "Process" spans in single-message scenarios, documented and with config.
   Ours is a Receive span, undocumented, with no config, and parent-child
   structurally cannot represent batch consumption (a span has one parent) or
   processing inside another ambient context.

2. **No process-span story.** The receive span ends inside `AfterReadMessage`,
   and trace continuity into the user's handler requires manually calling
   `consumer.ExtractContext(msg)`, a manual step in a zero-code tool. The spec
   anticipates the fix: "'Process' spans MAY be created in addition to 'Receive'
   spans for pull-based scenarios... by abstraction layers built on top of
   messaging SDKs." Creating process spans at compile time is the novel design
   work in this project.

3. **Batch semantics and metrics.** No `messaging.batch.message_count`, no
   `messaging.client.*` metrics.

4. **Coverage.** No IBM/sarama (the most-used Go Kafka client), nats.go, or
   amqp091-go.

## Scope (committed)

**Shared messaging semconv layer**: header-carrier abstractions (generalizing
kafka-go's headerCarrier), link-based consumer span creation per spec, receive
vs process operation handling, batch attributes, messaging metrics helpers, and
a reusable `RequireMessagingSemconv` test helper mirroring the GenAI one.

**kafka-go brought up to spec**: hooks migrated onto the shared layer; the
links fix ships behind a configuration flag, which is exactly the config option
the spec anticipates. The flag is exposed through #705's mechanism when it
lands; until then a thin accessor backed by the existing
`OTEL_GO_ENABLED/DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS`-style env var keeps the work
unblocked, so this project does not gate on #705's timeline.

**Process spans**: design + implementation for at least one concrete consumer
shape (kafka-go reader loop and/or sarama `ConsumerGroupHandler.ConsumeClaim`).

**IBM/sarama**: producer and consumer via interceptor injection: sarama's
config exposes `Producer.Interceptors` and `Consumer.Interceptors`, so a
compile-time rule appends an otel interceptor at `sarama.NewConfig()` call
sites, mirroring how the merged openai-go instrumentation injects
`option.WithMiddleware(...)` at `NewClient` (#604). This covers both
SyncProducer and AsyncProducer without touching the channel-based send path.

**Sustainability**: every module wired into the version-matrix (#581) from day
one; e2e reuses the existing kafka harness (`test/e2e/kafka_test.go`).

## Stretch (mentor-prioritized)

- nats.go: core pub/sub with `msg.Header` propagation (JetStream out of scope).
- amqp091-go as an alternative third client if preferred.
- Migrating the links flag default (opt-in now, flip later with deprecation path).

## Plan (12 weeks)

- W1-2: shared-layer design doc + links-gate semantics agreed with mentors
  (including the #705 config-surface handoff) -> review before code
- W3-5: shared layer + kafka-go migration (gated links fix, batch attrs) + tests
- W6-7: process-span design and implementation (the novel piece)
- W8-10: sarama producer/consumer + versionmatrix + e2e
- W11: messaging metrics on the shared layer
- W12: buffer, docs (instrument-guide entry), follow-up issues; nats.go if ahead

## Open design questions

- Links migration default and deprecation path (opt-in first?).
- Zero-code process spans: hook the consume/handler loop vs document the manual
  helper as the boundary.
- Exact config keys under #705's `go:` node for the messaging options.

## Prior work

#501 (gin, merged), #581 (versionmatrix, merged),
open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io#10654 (docs bootstrap, merged). Sibling
proposals: #705 (configuration), #679 (GenAI).

items.title: chore(semconv): add local OTel Weaver registry for the emitted telemetry contract
items.body:
## What

Adds a project-owned [OTel Weaver](https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver) schema registry under `schemas/otelc/` that declares the telemetry this project's instrumentations emit, and validates it in CI against the pinned upstream semantic conventions.

## Why

Today `make lint/semantic-conventions` runs `weaver registry check` against a clone of the upstream `semantic-conventions` repo. Upstream is always valid, so the check gives little signal, and there is no machine-readable description of the metrics/spans/attributes this project actually produces.

This follows the pattern used by [opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation) (OBI), which maintains its emission contract as a Weaver registry under `schemas/obi/`.

## What's included

- `schemas/otelc/registry_manifest.yaml` — registry metadata + a dependency on the upstream semconv version pinned in `.semconv-version`, pre-fetched under `.deps/` (git-ignored).
- `schemas/otelc/groups/http.yaml` — the first instrumentation contract (`net/http` client & server metrics). Upstream attributes are referenced with `ref:`; library-specific telemetry would be declared with `id:`. Other instrumentations can follow this template.
- `scripts/semconv/` — `fetch-upstream-semconv.sh`, `lint-schema.sh`, and `lint-schema-filter.jq`. Weaver runs from the `otel/weaver` OCI image (no host install needed).
- `Makefile` — new `fetch-upstream-semconv` and `lint-schema` targets; `lint/semantic-conventions` now validates the local registry.
- CI `check-registry-diff.yaml` — runs the Docker-based check and asserts the manifest version matches `.semconv-version`.

### Note on `DuplicateMetricName`

Instrumentations mostly emit standard upstream metrics (e.g. `http.client.request.duration`). Weaver has no way to *reference* a metric defined in a dependency, so we re-declare the metrics we emit to pin the contract. Weaver then reports a `DuplicateMetricName` between our registry and the upstream dependency; this specific, expected duplicate is allowlisted in `lint-schema-filter.jq`. Any other diagnostic — including a metric declared twice within our own registry, or an unresolved `ref:` — still fails the lint.

## Scope

Scaffold + `net/http` as the worked example. The remaining instrumentations (grpc, database/sql, kafka, redis, k8s, openai, mongo) can be added incrementally using the same pattern. No runtime Go code is changed.

## Testing

- `make lint-schema` passes locally (Weaver via Docker).
- Reverse-checked: injecting an unresolved `ref:` makes the lint fail as expected.
- `yamlfmt` and `checkmake` are clean.

Requires Docker (or `OCI_BIN=podman`) and `jq`; both are preinstalled on the CI runner.

items.title: Document and define telemetry signal coverage per instrumentation
items.body:
### Problem

Only `net/http` and `grpc` emit metrics; every other instrumentation is spans-only,
even where stable semantic conventions define metrics:

| Instrumentation | Spans | Metrics | Metrics semconv status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net/http`, `google.golang.org/grpc` | ✅ | ✅ | stable / development |
| `database/sql`, `go-redis`, `mongo-driver` | ✅ | ❌ | **stable** (`db.client.operation.duration`) |
| `kafka-go`, `openai-go`, `k8s.io/client-go` | ✅ | ❌ | development |

This coverage is not documented anywhere, so users can't tell what each
instrumentation emits without reading source, contributors have no definition of
done for a new instrumentation, and nothing in CI or review prevents the gap from
growing.

### Proposal

1. Add a signal coverage matrix (`docs/instrumentation-coverage.md`): one row per
   instrumentation with spans / metrics / logs and semconv status. Link it from the README.
2. State in the instrumentation guide that new instrumentations should implement all
   signals with **stable** semantic conventions for their domain; development-status
   signals are optional and marked as such in the matrix.
3. Once agreed, file follow-up issues for the existing gaps, starting with the stable
   ones (`database/sql`, `go-redis`, `mongo-driver`).

### Non-goals

Implementing development-status metrics immediately, and runtime metrics (separate concern).

### Open question

Hand-maintained matrix to start, or generated from package metadata? `otelc.yaml`
currently carries no signal info, so generation would require new metadata.

items.title: refactor(tool): dispatch rule type on the do modifier name
items.body:
Follow-up from #377; closes #541.

## Problem

Branch 0 of the `where`/`do` schema (ADR-0003) parses rules through a normalization layer (`tool/internal/rule/normalize.go`) that translates the structured shape back into the legacy flat field bag, drops the `do` modifier name, and re-infers the rule type from field presence. Each rule makes two YAML round-trips (map → normalize → re-marshal → struct), and the flat and structured shapes both carry the same selectors and modifiers, so they can drift apart.

## Change

Parse structured YAML directly and dispatch on the `do` modifier name:

- a typed payload per modifier (`HookAction`, `CodeAction`, …) and a `DoDef` union, symmetric with `WhereDef`; the modifier name selects the rule type with no re-marshal;
- `rule.ParseRules` is the single parser, shared by the setup phase and the golden-test harness (which previously kept its own copy);
- `normalize.go` and its tests are removed.

The concrete rule structs stay as the execution representation; the typed payloads are the structured layer a future JSON Schema generator (editor validation of rule files) can reflect over. Rationale in ADR-0006.

## Scope

Internal refactor only — the `where`/`do` YAML schema is unchanged. The five `func-sig-*` golden fixtures were the last flat-form rule files in the repo; they are migrated to the structured shape and their generated output is unchanged.

## Verification

- `go build`/`vet`/`gofmt`, repo `golangci-lint`, `markdownlint`: clean.
- All `tool/...` unit tests pass; `rule`/`setup` pass with `-race`.
- Golden instrumentation output is byte-identical (only input `rules.yml` fixtures changed).
- Validation parity with the removed normalizer is covered by new `parse_test.go` tests, including duplicate-key rejection.

Opening as draft to run CI.
