## Description
Fixes a deep infrastructure flakiness in the `verifyGoldenFiles` test suite where tests occasionally fail on Windows/WSL environments (due to CRLF newlines) or when running on newer Go versions (like Go 1.25/1.26). 

The `dave/dst` AST formatter relies on `go/printer` internals which occasionally drop or add blank lines in function bodies across different Go compiler versions. This causes the strict `golden.Assert` equality check to fail even when the injected AST semantics are 100% correct.

By collapsing consecutive newlines and stripping `\r\n` before comparison, we ensure the tests remain hermetic across all OS environments and future Go toolchain releases, while preserving the `-update` behavior for golden files.

items.title: docs(rfcs): propose genai.Observer architecture for unified telemetry
items.body:
## Description
Following up on the LFX Term 3 architecture discussions in #709, this RFC formally proposes the `genai.Observer` abstraction for the `pkg/genai` namespace.

Currently, SDK instrumentations like `openai-go` manually parse JSON and handle chunked Server-Sent Events (SSE) to map their idiosyncratic payloads to OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions. As we expand to support Gemini, LangChain, and MCP, duplicating this stateful accumulation and truncation logic across every SDK creates an unsustainable maintenance burden.

This RFC standardizes the flow by moving all Semantic Convention mapping, token usage aggregation, and memory-safe content accumulation out of the SDK hooks and into a central `genai.Observer`. The SDKs are reduced to simple, stateless Extractors.

This lays the exact architectural foundation required for Milestone 1 of the LFX GenAI initiative.

items.title: fix(ast): stripGenericTypes fatals on qualified pointer receivers
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Method rules that use a receiver filter like `recv: "*Writer"` crash during function lookup when the target method has a **qualified pointer receiver** (for example `func (*bufio.Writer) Write(...)` or `func (*http.ResponseWriter) ServeHTTP(...)`).

The tool calls `util.Unimplemented` and aborts with `ex.Fatalf` instead of matching or returning no match.

**Affected code:** `tool/internal/ast/shared.go`, function `stripGenericTypes()`.

**Example crash:**
```
Unimplemented: unexpected receiver type: *dst.StarExpr
```

`stripGenericTypes()` already handles `*MyStruct` and `*GenStruct[T]`, but not `*pkg.Type` where the receiver is a `*dst.SelectorExpr`.

### Environment

 - OS: Linux (any OS; not platform-specific)
 - Go Version: 1.25.0
 - Version: main / latest otelc

### To Reproduce

**Option A (unit test):**

1. Create a method with a qualified pointer receiver in a `dst.File`:

```go
func (*bufio.Writer) Write(p []byte) (n int, err error)
```

2. Look it up with a rule:

```yaml
func: Write
recv: "*Writer"
```

3. Call `FindFuncDecl()` or run `otelc setup` against that rule.

4. See fatal:

```
Unimplemented: unexpected receiver type: *dst.StarExpr
```

**Option B (minimal Go test in `tool/internal/ast/shared_test.go`):**

```go
decl := &dst.FuncDecl{
    Name: &dst.Ident{Name: "Write"},
    Type: &dst.FuncType{},
    Recv: &dst.FieldList{List: []*dst.Field{{
        Type: &dst.StarExpr{
            X: &dst.SelectorExpr{
                X:   &dst.Ident{Name: "bufio"},
                Sel: &dst.Ident{Name: "Writer"},
            },
        },
    }}},
    Body: &dst.BlockStmt{},
}
root := &dst.File{Decls: []dst.Decl{decl}}

_, _, err := FindFuncDecl(root, &rule.InstFuncRule{
    Func: "Write",
    Recv: "*Writer",
})
// fatals before returning
```

### Expected behavior

Receiver matching should extract the base type name from qualified pointer receivers (for example `*Writer` from `*bufio.Writer`), same as it does for unqualified `*MyStruct`.

The tool should either:
- match the method when `recv: "*Writer"` is set, or
- return no match gracefully

It must **not** fatal during setup or instrumentation.

### Additional context

**Root cause:** In `stripGenericTypes()`, the `*dst.StarExpr` branch only handles `X` as `*dst.Ident` or generic index expressions. It does not handle `X` as `*dst.SelectorExpr` (`*pkg.Type`).

**Impact:** Any instrumentation rule targeting methods with qualified pointer receivers can crash `otelc setup` at load time.

This PR introduces the foundational pipeline for declarative instrumentation configuration via `.otel.yml`. It parses user configuration and embeds it into the compiled application using an AST-injected `otelc.runtime.go` registry, making the config available to instrumentation hooks at runtime.

Two small documentation errors in the repo:

`docs/getting-started.md` uses the wrong relative path to the `otelc` binary in the demo quick start.

After `make build`, `otelc` is at the **repo root**. From `demo/app/basic`, the docs say:

### Environment

 - OS: Any (not platform-specific)
 - Go Version: 1.25.0
 - Version: main / latest otelc

items.title: fix(instrumentation): emit HTTP status code for anthropic error.type
items.body:
The Anthropic middleware set `error.type` to the full HTTP status line
(e.g. `"429 Too Many Requests"`). Per the error semantic conventions it
should be the numeric status code (`"429"`). This routes the value through
a new `semconv.ErrorType` helper instead of a raw `attribute.String`, and
updates the `TestOtelMiddleware_HTTPError` assertion accordingly.

## Motivation

`error.type` is meant to be a low-cardinality error class — for HTTP that's
the status code. Emitting the full status line ("429 Too Many Requests")
breaks metric/trace grouping in backends that key on `error.type` and
diverges from the error semantic conventions.

items.title: question: log/slog and logrus don't get trace_id/span_id without a direct sdk/trace import — is this expected?
items.body:
## What I'm seeing

I've been experimenting with otelc's zero-code instrumentation and ran into something I'd like to double-check, in case I'm missing a setup step somewhere.

When an application relies purely on otelc's automatic instrumentation (`net/http`, `slog`, `logrus`, etc.) and doesn't import `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` directly anywhere in its own source, I wasn't able to get `trace_id`/`span_id` to show up in `log/slog` or `logrus` output, even though a real span did appear to be active at the time. Adding a direct `sdk/trace` import (e.g. to construct a `TracerProvider` manually) made it work as expected.

I wanted to ask here first, in case this is a known constraint of the current design or I'm overlooking something on my end, before digging further.

## Reproduction 1: minimal zero-code app

A `net/http` handler with no OpenTelemetry imports at all:

```go
func greetHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	slog.InfoContext(r.Context(), "handling greet request")
	...
}
```

Building and running this with otelc:

- The generated `.otelc-build/matched.json` / `otel.instrumentation.go` never include `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`, even though the binary does end up linking that package (via the automatically-injected SDK setup).
- At runtime, the automatic `net/http` server instrumentation produces a real span (confirmed via a console exporter — a genuine, non-zero trace/span ID is generated for the request), but the `slog.InfoContext` log line for that same request never carries `trace_id`/`span_id`.

## Reproduction 2: same effect on the existing integration tests

Out of curiosity, I tried editing both `test/apps/logslog/main.go` and `test/apps/logslogrus/main.go` to remove their direct `sdktrace`/`stdouttrace` imports and manual `otel.SetTracerProvider(tp)` calls, relying instead on `otel.GetTracerProvider().Tracer("test")` — i.e. the same zero-code path shown above. Both changes make their respective existing integration tests fail:

```
--- FAIL: TestLogsSlog
    logs_test.go:46: Should NOT be empty, but was []
    Expected trace_id to be injected into log messages

--- FAIL: TestLogsLogrus
    logs_test.go:74: Should NOT be empty, but was []
    Expected trace_id to be injected into logrus messages
```

In both cases, all other assertions in the test (log message content) still pass; only the `trace_id` assertion fails. Both `test/apps/logslog` and `test/apps/logslogrus` currently import `sdk/trace` directly, so I'm not sure whether that's intentional (e.g. to demonstrate a specific usage pattern) or incidental.

## Question

Is direct import of `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` expected to be required for log/trace correlation to work (for both `log/slog` and `logrus`), even in an otherwise zero-code setup? If so, would it be worth documenting that as a requirement/limitation? If not, I'm happy to dig further into why the correlation doesn't kick in automatically.

items.title: bug(setup): version-gated rules silently skipped when dependency is built from local/replace path
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Version-gated instrumentation rules are **silently skipped** when a dependency is compiled from a **local checkout** or via a **`replace` directive** in `go.mod`.

During setup, `otelc` derives each dependency's version by regex-parsing the compile source path for a module-cache segment (`...@vX.Y.Z/...`). Local and replaced paths do not contain that pattern, so `Dependency.Version` is left empty.

When a rule has a non-empty `version:` field, `matchVersion` calls `VersionInRange("", "<range>")`, which returns **false**. The rule is filtered out in both the **setup** phase (`match.go`) and the **pin** phase (`pin.go`) with **no error or warning**.

This is especially painful when developing instrumentation locally with `replace`, or when troubleshooting version-gated rules - the docs say to check `go list -m`, but the tool never resolves the version that way.


---

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Go Version: 1.25.0
- Version: `otelc` main branch / v1.0.1

---

### To Reproduce

**Minimal path-based repro (no full build required):**

`findModVersion` only works for module-cache paths:

| Source path | `findModVersion()` result |
|---|---|
| `/go/pkg/mod/github.com/foo/bar@v1.2.3/pkg/foo.go` | `v1.2.3` |
| `/home/user/projects/bar/pkg/foo.go` | `""` (empty) |
| `/tmp/myapp/vendor/github.com/foo/bar/pkg/foo.go` | `""` (empty) |

Relevant code:

```go
// tool/internal/setup/find.go
var versionRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`@v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-.*?)?/`)

func findModVersion(path string) string {
    version := versionRegexp.FindString(filepath.ToSlash(path))
    if version == "" {
        return ""
    }
    return version[1 : len(version)-1]
}
```

Empty version causes version-gated rules to never match:

```go
// tool/util/shared.go
VersionInRange("", "v1.0.0")        // → false
VersionInRange("", "v1.0.0,v2.0.0") // → false
```

**End-to-end repro sketch:**

1. Create a module that depends on a version-gated library and uses `replace`:

```go
// go.mod
module example.com/app

go 1.25.0

require github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 v9.0.0

replace github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 => ./local-redis
```

2. Ensure `./local-redis` is a local checkout of the library (no `@vX.Y.Z/` in compile paths).

3. Build with `otelc` against a rule that targets `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` with a non-empty `version:` range (as in `instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/otelc.yaml`).

4. Observe: instrumentation for that dependency is **not applied**, and there is **no log/error** explaining that the dependency version could not be resolved.

5. Compare: remove the `replace` directive (or build against the module cache) - the same rule matches when the compile path contains `@v9.x.x/`.

---

### Expected behavior

- `Dependency.Version` should reflect the module version from the build's module graph (e.g. as reported by `go list -m <module-path>`), not only from compile command file paths.
- When a version cannot be resolved, `otelc` should at minimum **warn** (or fail loudly in debug mode) rather than silently dropping version-gated rules.
- Behavior under `replace` directives should be explicitly defined (e.g. use the `require` version from `go.mod`, or document that purely local replacements have no semver).

---

### Additional context

**Affected code paths:**
- `tool/internal/setup/find.go` : `findModVersion`, `findGoSources` (sets `dep.Version`)
- `tool/internal/setup/match.go` :  `matchVersion` filters rules during setup
- `tool/internal/setup/pin.go` :  same `VersionInRange` check when deciding which instrumentation packages to pin

Would be working on this issue once the approach is finalized.

items.title: chore(bundle): add git merge driver to stop otelc-bundle.tgz rebase conflicts
items.body:
## Problem

`tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz` is a binary archive embedded into `otelc` via `//go:embed`, so it must stay committed for `go install go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/cmd/otelc@latest` to work. But because it is binary, git cannot 3-way merge it — so almost every branch that touches `pkg/` or `instrumentation/` conflicts with `main` on this one file and halts an otherwise-clean rebase.

## Solution

Add a custom `otelc-bundle` git merge driver, registered once per clone via `make setup-git`:

- **`.gitattributes`** — routes the bundle to `merge=otelc-bundle` (still treated as binary: `-text -diff`).
- **`.github/scripts/merge-bundle.sh`** — on conflict, keeps the current ("ours") bundle and exits 0 so the rebase/merge runs to completion without stopping, printing a reminder to regenerate.
- **`Makefile`** — `make setup-git` registers the driver in `.git/config`.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — documents the one-time setup and the post-rebase `make package` step.

With it configured, resolving a stale bundle is:

```sh
git fetch origin main
git rebase origin/main   # no longer halts on the bundle
make package             # regenerate from the merged sources
git add tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz && git commit --amend --no-edit
git push --force-with-lease
```

### Why the driver does not regenerate the bundle itself

I first implemented in-driver `make package`, but verified it is **incorrect**: when git invokes a merge driver it has not yet materialized the *other* merged source files into the working tree, so `make package` reads stale sources and drops the incoming changes (reproduced: a merge of two source-editing branches produced a bundle missing one side's change, which `verify-bundle` would then reject). Regenerating after the rebase/merge completes is the only reliable point, so the driver keeps "ours" and `verify-bundle` CI continues to enforce that the committed bundle matches the sources.

## Testing

- Simulated a real rebase conflict between two branches that each modify sources: rebase now completes with exit 0 and no manual conflict resolution; after `make package` the bundle contains both sides' changes and passes the `verify-bundle` check.
- `make setup-git` and `make -n setup-git` verified.

## Summary

The DSN parsers for ClickHouse and Oracle, along with the exported

  the protocol-only edge (`tcp:/db`).

  `host:port` when available, otherwise falls back to the driver name.

The MySQL parser does not handle a unix-socket path written without parentheses
(`unix:/tmp/mysql.sock/db`). This PR documents the current behaviour rather than

already covered. Can be addressed in a follow-up.

items.title: fix(ast): handle qualified pointer receivers in stripGenericTypes
items.body:
## Description

This PR fixes receiver matching for qualified pointer receivers in `stripGenericTypes()`.

Previously, receiver rules such as `recv: "*Writer"` would fail when the actual receiver was a qualified pointer type (for example, `*bufio.Writer` or `*http.ResponseWriter`). `stripGenericTypes()` did not handle `*dst.SelectorExpr`, which caused `findFuncDecl()` to reach the fatal path instead of gracefully treating it as a non-match.

This change extends receiver type extraction to support qualified identifiers while preserving the existing behavior for regular and generic receivers.

### Changes

- Add support for qualified pointer and value receivers represented by `*dst.SelectorExpr`.
- Introduce a shared helper to resolve unqualified type names from receiver expressions.
- Replace the fatal path for unsupported receiver shapes with graceful "no match" handling instead of aborting instrumentation.
- Add regression tests covering:
  - qualified pointer receivers (`*bufio.Writer`, `*http.ResponseWriter`)
  - qualified value receivers
  - existing generic receiver behavior
  - unmatched receiver rules to ensure graceful handling

## Motivation

Rules targeting qualified pointer receivers could terminate instrumentation with:

```text
Unimplemented: unexpected receiver type: *dst.StarExpr
```

This happened because qualified receiver expressions were not recognized when extracting receiver type names. Instead of treating these as normal non-matches, the lookup aborted the entire instrumentation process.

This change ensures qualified receiver types are handled correctly while preserving existing behavior for all previously supported receiver forms and preventing unexpected crashes.

Fixes #766

items.title: bug(optimize): canFlattenTJump panics when Before hook declares HookContext as an unnamed parameter
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`canFlattenTJump` in `tool/internal/instrument/optimize.go` (line 229) panics with a
**runtime index-out-of-range** error when a Before hook function declares its first
parameter (the `HookContext`) without an explicit name — i.e. `func(HookContext, int)`
instead of `func(ctx HookContext, int)` or `func(_ HookContext, int)`.

In Go's AST (and in the `dst` library used here), a parameter written without a name
produces a `*dst.Field` whose `Names` slice is `nil`. The code unconditionally indexes
`Names[0]`, which panics on a nil/empty slice:

```go
// optimize.go:229  ← panics when Names is nil
hookContextParam := hookFunc.Type.Params.List[0].Names[0].Name
```

The existing `_ HookContext` (blank-identifier) path is safe because `_` produces a
non-nil `Names` slice. Only a truly unnamed first parameter triggers the bug.

**Inconsistency:** `collectArguments` in `apply_func.go` (lines 103–109) already guards
`field.Names == nil` before indexing. `canFlattenTJump` does not, making the two
functions inconsistent in their handling of unnamed parameters.

### Environment

 - OS: Linux / macOS / Windows (all platforms)
 - Go Version: 1.21+
 - Version: current `main` (commit where `canFlattenTJump` was introduced)

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a Before hook whose **first parameter (`HookContext`) is unnamed** — valid Go,
   but `Names == nil` in the AST:

```go
// hooks/before.go
package hooks

import "go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/pkg/hook"

// Unnamed HookContext — valid Go, less common but legal
func BeforeMyFunc(hook.HookContext, *string) {
    // HookContext intentionally unused
}
```

2. Write a rule file with `before: BeforeMyFunc` and **no** `after` hook:

```yaml
# hooks/otelc.yaml
my_rule:
  target: example.com/mylib
  func:   MyFunc
  before: BeforeMyFunc
  path:   example.com/hooks
```

3. Run `otelc build ./...` against a project that depends on `example.com/mylib`.

4. The build crashes immediately with the panic shown below.

### Expected behavior

`canFlattenTJump` should treat a hook function whose first parameter has `Names == nil`
(fully unnamed) the same way it treats `_ HookContext`: the parameter is definitionally
unreferenced in the function body, so the function should return `true` (safe to flatten)
without panicking.

A minimal fix, consistent with the guard already present in `collectArguments`:

```go
// Proposed fix in canFlattenTJump (optimize.go ~L227)
params := hookFunc.Type.Params.List[0]
if len(params.Names) == 0 {
    // Fully unnamed first param — cannot be referenced in the body
    return true
}
hookContextParam := params.Names[0].Name
```

### Additional context

**Panic stack trace:**

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0

goroutine 1 [running]:
go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/internal/instrument.canFlattenTJump(0xc0004e8000)
        tool/internal/instrument/optimize.go:229 +0x...
go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/internal/instrument.(*InstrumentPhase).optimizeTJumps(...)
        tool/internal/instrument/optimize.go:386 +0x...
go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/internal/instrument.(*InstrumentPhase).instrument(...)
        tool/internal/instrument/instrument.go +0x...
```

**Test gap:** The existing tests in `optimize_test.go` exercise only `_ HookContext`
(`Names[0].Name == "_"`) and `ctx HookContext` (named). No test covers the
unnamed-parameter (`Names == nil`) case.

**Duplicate search:** Checked all open and closed issues. Issue #777 (local/replace path
silent skip), #766 (`stripGenericTypes` fatal on pointer receivers), and #756 (signature
filter fatal on slice/chan/map params) are unrelated panics in different functions. No
existing issue matches `canFlattenTJump`, `Names[0]`, or unnamed HookContext parameters.

Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

This PR fixes a runtime panic in `canFlattenTJump` (`tool/internal/instrument/optimize.go`) when a `Before` hook function declares its `HookContext` parameter without an explicit name (e.g., `func(HookContext, string)`).

items.title: test(util): TestRunCmd fails on Windows due to reliance on shell builtin echo
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`TestRunCmd` in `tool/util/sys_test.go` fails when running unit tests on Windows operating systems (`GOOS=windows`).

The test suite uses `[]string{"echo", "hello"}` and `[]string{"echo", "hello", "world"}` to verify subprocess execution via `util.RunCmd`. On Unix-like systems (Linux, macOS), `echo` exists as a standalone binary in `/bin/echo` or `/usr/bin/echo` on `$PATH`. On Windows, however, `echo` is a shell built-in command internal to `cmd.exe` and `powershell.exe` rather than an executable binary on `%PATH%`.

Consequently, Go's `exec.LookPath("echo")` fails on Windows with:
`exec: "echo": executable file not found in %PATH%`

### Environment

 - OS: Windows 10 / Windows 11 / Windows Server (`windows/amd64`)
 - Go Version: Go 1.25.0 / Go 1.26.2
 - Version: main (commit f5b12f77e6bef0a38872063b2579c7ff32917beb)

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open a command prompt or shell on a Windows machine (`windows/amd64`).
2. Navigate to the `tool/util` package directory: `cd tool/util`
3. Execute unit tests: `go test ./...`
4. See error in `TestRunCmd/simple_echo_command` and `TestRunCmd/command_with_multiple_arguments`:
   ```text
   --- FAIL: TestRunCmd (0.06s)
       --- FAIL: TestRunCmd/simple_echo_command (0.02s)
           sys_test.go:43: RunCmd() error = failed to run command "echo" in dir '""' with args: [hello]: exec: "echo": executable file not found in %PATH%, expectErr false
       --- FAIL: TestRunCmd/command_with_multiple_arguments (0.02s)
           sys_test.go:43: RunCmd() error = failed to run command "echo" in dir '""' with args: [hello world]: exec: "echo": executable file not found in %PATH%, expectErr false
   FAIL	go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/util	4.131s
   ```

### Expected behavior

`go test ./...` in `tool/util` should pass cleanly on Windows, matching the behavior on Linux and macOS.

### Additional context

- **Root Cause**: `TestRunCmd` in [`tool/util/sys_test.go`](file:///c:/Users/Vishal/Code_File/Projects/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/util/sys_test.go#L16-L47) passes `"echo"` as a command name. Windows lacks an `echo.exe` binary in `%PATH%`, causing `exec.LookPath` to fail.
- **Impact**: Windows developers and CI pipelines executing tests for `windows/amd64` encounter test failures in `tool/util`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update `TestRunCmd` in `tool/util/sys_test.go` to use a cross-platform executable guaranteed to exist in any Go development environment, such as `[]string{"go", "version"}` or `[]string{"go", "env"}`.

items.title: Add govulncheck vulnerability scanning to CI
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There is currently no vulnerability scanning of Go dependencies (or the Go standard library) anywhere in CI. The `.github/workflows/` directory has CodeQL (`codeql.yml`), FOSSA (`fossa.yml`), and OSSF Scorecard (`ossf-scorecard.yml`), but a grep for `govulncheck` across all workflows returns **0 hits**.

Those existing tools cover different things CodeQL finds bugs in our own code, FOSSA covers licensing, OSSF scores repo hygiene, but none of them flag a dependency (or a stdlib version) with a **published Go vulnerability (CVE /GO-XXXX advisory)** that our code actually reaches. 
For a security-sensitive, multi-module auto-instrumentation project this is a real blind spot: today we'd learn about a vulnerable dependency from an incident rather than from CI.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a new workflow that runs [`govulncheck`](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck) across the repository:

- **New file:** `.github/workflows/govulncheck.yaml`
- Runs `govulncheck ./...`. `govulncheck` is low-noise by design — it reports only vulnerabilities in code paths that are actually called, not ever advisory in the dependency tree.
- **Must iterate over every module.** This repo is multi-module and there are **65 `go.mod` files** (`pkg/`, `pkg/runtime/`, `tool/`, and every `instrumentation/*/...`) — so a single top-level `govulncheck ./...` will not cover them all. The workflow should loop over module directories, mirroring how the existing Makefile / workflows already fan out across modules.
- **Triggers:** on `pull_request` **and** on a `schedule` (cron). The scheduled run is important, it catches newly-disclosed CVEs in dependencies that haven't changed since the last PR.
- **Pin the action to a commit SHA** per the repo's ratchet policy (see the `ratchet`-managed pins in existing workflows, e.g. `actions/checkout@8e8c483db84b4bee98b60c0593521ed34d9990e8 # v6.0.1` in `.github/workflows/test-unit.yaml`). Either the official `golang/govulncheck-action` (SHA-pinned) or a plain `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@<version>` step is acceptable.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Rely on existing scanners (CodeQL / FOSSA / OSSF).** Rejected, none of them detect known Go CVEs in reachable dependency/stdlib code, which is exactly the gap `govulncheck` fills.
- **Dependabot/Renovate alerts only.** These flag advisories at the manifest level but don't do reachability analysis, so they're noisier and don't confirm whether the vulnerable code is actually called. `govulncheck` complements rather than replaces them.
- **A single top-level `govulncheck ./...`.** Rejected, it silently skips the other 64 modules in this multi-module repo.

**Additional context**

Refer other go repo inside Otel ecosystem and how they do `govulncheck`

items.body:
### Description

The `net/http` server instrumentation wraps the `http.ResponseWriter` in an internal `writerWrapper` (`instrumentation/net/http/server/response_writer.go`). To preserve HTTP/2 server push, the wrapper is meant to re-expose the `http.Pusher` interface. However, it defines the method as:

```go
func (w *writerWrapper) Pusher() http.Pusher { ... }
```

The `http.Pusher` interface requires:

```go
Push(target string, opts *http.PushOptions) error
```

The method name (`Pusher`) and signature do not match `http.Pusher`, so `writerWrapper` **never actually satisfies `http.Pusher`**. Because the embedded `http.ResponseWriter` only promotes the base interface's methods, the optional interface is silently dropped.

### Impact

Handlers detect server-push support with a type assertion on the writer they are handed:

```go
if p, ok := w.(http.Pusher); ok {
    p.Push("/style.css", nil)
}
```

Once this instrumentation is enabled, that assertion silently returns `ok == false`, so **HTTP/2 server push is disabled** for every instrumented handler. There is no error or log — behavior just quietly changes relative to the uninstrumented server.

### Expected behavior

The wrapper should transparently preserve the optional interfaces of the underlying `http.ResponseWriter` (`http.Pusher`, `http.Flusher`, `http.Hijacker`), so instrumentation does not change the capabilities visible to handlers.

### Proposed fix

- Implement `Push(target string, opts *http.PushOptions) error` on `writerWrapper`, forwarding to the underlying writer when it is an `http.Pusher` and returning `http.ErrNotSupported` otherwise.
- Add compile-time interface assertions (`var _ http.Pusher = (*writerWrapper)(nil)`, etc.) so future signature drift fails the build instead of silently dropping an interface.

### Environment

- Package: `instrumentation/net/http/server`

items.title: fix(net/http/server): satisfy http.Pusher so HTTP/2 server push works
items.body:
Fixes #794

### Problem

`writerWrapper` (`instrumentation/net/http/server/response_writer.go`) exposed a method named `Pusher() http.Pusher`. That name and signature do not match the `http.Pusher` interface, which requires `Push(target string, opts *http.PushOptions) error`. Consequently the wrapper never satisfied `http.Pusher`, and since the embedded `http.ResponseWriter` only promotes the base interface's methods, the optional interface was silently dropped.

Handlers detect push support with `if p, ok := w.(http.Pusher); ok`. Once this instrumentation was enabled, that assertion silently returned `false`, disabling HTTP/2 server push for every instrumented handler — with no error or log.

### Fix

- Replace `Pusher()` with a correct `Push(target string, opts *http.PushOptions) error` that forwards to the underlying writer when it supports push and returns `http.ErrNotSupported` otherwise (the sentinel handlers already expect on a non-push connection).
- Add compile-time interface assertions (`http.ResponseWriter`, `http.Hijacker`, `http.Flusher`, `http.Pusher`) so future signature drift fails the build instead of silently dropping an optional interface.

### Tests

- `TestWriterWrapper_ImplementsPusher` — asserts the wrapper actually satisfies `http.Pusher` via the type assertion real `net/http` code performs (the regression this guards against).
- `TestWriterWrapper_Push` — forwards to the underlying pusher.
- `TestWriterWrapper_Push_NotSupported` — returns `http.ErrNotSupported` for a non-push writer.

All tests pass (`go test ./...`) and `go vet ./...` is clean in the `net/http/server` module.

items.title: fix(tool/rule): validate required target field during rule loading
items.body:
## Description

When loading instrumentation rules from YAML, `validate()` methods in `tool/internal/rule` validated specific fields like `func`, `path`, `raw`, `struct`, `directive`, `file`, etc., but failed to validate that `target` is non-empty. If a YAML rule configuration omitted the `target` field, constructors like `NewInstFuncRule` or `NewInstCallRule` succeeded, passing setup validation and failing silently later at package matching time.

This PR adds a `validateBase()` method in `tool/internal/rule/base.go` to validate that `r.Target` is non-empty and non-whitespace, and invokes `validateBase()` from the `validate()` method of all rule implementations (`InstFuncRule`, `InstRawRule`, `InstStructRule`, `InstCallRule`, `InstDeclRule`, `InstDirectiveRule`, `InstFileRule`).

Additionally, unit tests were updated and added across `tool/internal/rule/*_test.go` (including creating `raw_rule_test.go` and `struct_rule_test.go`) to ensure all rule constructors return validation errors when `target` is missing or whitespace.

## Motivation

Ensures malformed rules missing a required `target` field fail early with a clear validation error during rule loading instead of failing silently later during package matching.

Fixes #796

items.title: bug(tool/instrument): collectArguments fails to remap blank identifier receiver (_)
items.body:
## Summary

While looking through `tool/internal/instrument/apply_func.go`, I noticed that blank identifier receivers aren't handled consistently with blank parameters and named return values.

`collectArguments` already remaps unnamed parameters (and blank parameters such as `_`) to generated names like `_ignoredParam<N>` so their addresses can be taken safely during trampoline generation.

However, for a method with a blank receiver, for example:

```go
type MyService struct{}

func (_ MyService) Execute() {}
```

the receiver name is currently preserved as `"_"`.

Later, `createTrampArgs` assumes all argument names are addressable:

```go
func createTrampArgs(names []string) []dst.Expr {
    for _, name := range names {
        util.Assert(name != ast.IdentIgnore, "must be processed before")
        exprs = append(exprs, ast.AddressOf(name))
    }
}
```

As a result, instrumentation fails because the blank identifier was never remapped.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Define a method with a blank receiver:

   ```go
   type MyService struct{}

   func (_ MyService) Execute() {}
   ```
2. Add an `otelc` instrumentation rule targeting `Execute`.
3. Build with `otelc`.

## Expected behavior

Blank receivers should be handled the same way as blank parameters: remapped to an internal generated identifier before trampoline generation, allowing instrumentation to proceed normally.

## Additional context

This appears to be related to the work done for #736, which added support for blank parameters and blank named return values. The blank receiver case seems to have been missed, resulting in this remaining edge case.

Fixes #798

## Summary

`collectArguments` already remaps unnamed parameters (`func(int)`) and blank parameters (`func(_ int)`) to generated names such as `_ignoredParam0`, so their addresses can be taken safely during trampoline generation.

Blank receivers were missing from that treatment. This PR extends the existing `_ignoredParam<N>` remapping to cover blank receivers, consistent with how unnamed and blank parameters are already handled.

The broader name-collision-avoidance generalization raised in review (checking generated names against identifiers the target already declares) is intentionally out of scope here and lives on a separate branch (`fix-799-name-collision-avoidance`) for a follow-up PR.

items.title: docs(adr): add semconv telemetry contract organization
items.body:
## Description

Adds ADR 0006 to formalize how this project organizes and versions its
semantic-convention telemetry contract.

The ADR records the following decisions:

- telemetry contracts are centralized under `schemas/otelc/groups/`;
- one contract file represents an instrumentation family and may cover multiple
  modules that share a telemetry surface;
- the project uses one upstream semantic-convention version, with
  `.semconv-version`, `registry_manifest.yaml`, and Go imports updated
  atomically;
- every instrumentation is represented in the registry, including
  contract-neutral instrumentations;
- each metric name has one owner in the local registry;
- static registry validation and runtime-emission verification are separate,
  complementary requirements;
- runtime verification must cover materially distinct emission paths, including
  applicable conditional and error paths;
- code generation and the exact runtime-verification mechanism remain
  follow-up work.

## Motivation

PR #696 introduced the project-owned Weaver registry, and the repository now
uses that centralized model across its instrumentations. The organization,
ownership, versioning, and verification boundaries should be recorded as an
architectural decision before the Tier 2/3 work discussed in #728 proceeds.

`make lint-schema` verifies that the declared registry resolves against the
pinned upstream semantic conventions. It does not execute instrumentation or
prove that runtime telemetry matches the declaration. This ADR records that
boundary without prematurely selecting Weaver live-check, generated assertions,
or another enforcement mechanism.

Closes #745

## Testing

- `make lint/markdown`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- All hosted checks pass
- Code-specific test jobs are intentionally skipped because this PR changes
  only Markdown

## Related

- #696
- #728

items.title: fix(instrumentation): skip anthropic span creation for unparseable model
items.body:
## Description

`parseMessagesRequest` returns an empty `model` when the request body fails
to parse — either truncated JSON (the middleware caps request parsing at 1MB
via `maxRequestBodySize`, e.g. on a large multimodal payload) or a
well-formed body that simply omits the `model` field. Previously this still
produced a span named `"chat "` (trailing space) with
`gen_ai.request.model=""`.

This adds a guard: when `model == ""`, the request is passed through
uninstrumented, consistent with the other pass-through cases already in the
middleware (unknown operation, streaming, nil body, request read error).

## Motivation

A span with an empty model attribute is malformed telemetry — it can't be
attributed to any model in a backend, and the `"chat "` name (note the
trailing space) is visibly broken. Skipping span creation when there's
nothing meaningful to attach is better than emitting a garbled one.

## Testing

Added two cases: an unparseable request body and a valid body missing the
`model` field, both asserting no span is created and the request still
reaches the underlying transport.

`go test -race ./...` passes.

items.title: chore(tool): addition of `govulncheck` scanning in ci workflows
items.body:
## Description

Adds reachability-based Go vulnerability scanning to CI via `govulncheck`, split into two jobs with different blocking behaviour.

**Workflow** (`.github/workflows/govulncheck.yaml`). Triggers on `pull_request` (Go sources, `go.mod`/`go.sum`, `Makefile`, and the workflow itself), a weekly `schedule`, and `workflow_dispatch`. Read-only default permissions, `persist-credentials: false` on checkout, SHA-pinned actions.

Both jobs install Go with `go-version: stable` rather than the `go.mod` version. govulncheck reports stdlib advisories against the toolchain running it, so pinning to `go.mod` would flag stdlib vulnerabilities the current release has already fixed.

`govulncheck (core)` runs `make govulncheck`, a source-mode scan of the root module (which covers `tool/`) plus every `pkg/**` module. It is soft on pull requests via `continue-on-error: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`, since a newly disclosed CVE with no fix released yet should not red unrelated work. It blocks on the weekly and manual runs: job-level `continue-on-error` concludes the whole run as success, which would leave a red job buried inside a green scheduled run with nothing to act on.

`govulncheck (instrumentation)` runs `make govulncheck/instrumentation` and blocks on every trigger. It builds each top-level app under `test/apps/` with `otelc go build`, then scans the resulting binary with `govulncheck -mode=binary`. Binary mode is necessary here because a source scan of `instrumentation/` skips `//go:build ignore` hook sources and cannot typecheck modules that rely on compile-time field injection, such as `database/sql`. Demo apps are excluded, since their example dependencies are pinned deliberately.

**Tool pinning.** `govulncheck` is pinned in `.tools/go.mod` and `.tools/tools.go` and built into `.bin/` by the same rule as every other repo tool. Renovate's existing `gomod` handling keeps it current, so no dedicated version variable or customManager is needed.

**Renovate** (`.github/renovate.json5`). Adds `minimumReleaseAge: '5 days'` and `internalChecksFilter: 'strict'` as a supply-chain cooldown.

**Dependency fix.** Bumps `google.golang.org/grpc` to `v1.82.1` in every module outside `demo/`. That release fixes [GO-2026-6061](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6061) (xDS RBAC authorization bypass and HTTP/2 transport server DoS), which the new instrumentation job reports as reachable through `grpc.Server.Serve`.

## Motivation

There is no reachability-based Go vulnerability scanning in CI today. CodeQL, FOSSA, and OSSF cover different gaps, and none flag a dependency or stdlib version with a published Go advisory that our code actually reaches. `govulncheck` closes that gap and is low noise because it only reports vulnerabilities in code paths that are actually called.

The weekly scheduled run catches newly disclosed advisories in dependencies that have not changed since the last PR. The Renovate cooldown reduces the risk of pulling in a freshly published, possibly compromised release before it has been vetted. It is scoped to Renovate on purpose, since Dependabot security updates (enabled via repo settings,
for example PR #803 bumping `golang.org/x/net`) should land fast and not be delayed. In this repo Renovate owns routine version bumps; Dependabot only fires for known vulnerabilities.

## Fixes #793

items.title: docs: document runtime instrumentation selection env vars (OTEL_GO_ENABLED/DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS)

## Problem

The **Selecting Instrumentations** section in `docs/configuration.md` only documents the build-time mechanism (`otel.instrumentation.go`). It doesn't mention the runtime environment variables `OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` and `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS`, which let users enable or disable instrumentations without rebuilding.

As a result, users reading the configuration guide can't easily discover that instrumentation selection also works at runtime.

## Suggested fix

Document both variables in `docs/configuration.md` next to the existing build-time approach:

- `OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS`: if set, only the listed instrumentations run.
- `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS`: disables specific instrumentations.
- If neither is set, all instrumentations run by default.
- Names are lowercase and comma-separated (e.g. `nethttp,grpc`).

Behavior is implemented in `pkg/runtime/otel_setup.go` (`Instrumented`).

items.title: feat(docs): Generate instrumentation configuration documentation from struct metadata
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Configuration for individual instrumentations is difficult to discover. There is no single place where users can look up what environment variables are available, what values they accept, or what their defaults are. This leads to recurring questions in issues and community channels. Documentation is currently maintained manually, and configuration knobs are expressed as scattered os.Getenv calls.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Introduce declarative metadata for instrumentation configuration using Go structs with struct tags. A code-generation tool reads these declarations and produces Markdown documentation automatically, co-located with each instrumentation.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
YAML/JSON schema files: introduces an external file per instrumentation that Go tooling cannot type-check and that can silently drift from the code. Struct tags keep metadata co-located with the declaration and compiler-verifiable.

**Additional context**
This is scoped to the metadata layer and doc generation only. The existing configuration knobs (OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS, OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS) are the initial target.

This is intended as a immediate step that complements the broader configuration work tracked in #705, 

Based on the slack [discussion](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C088D8GSSSF/p1784653758628299) by @kakkoyun

items.title: feat(instrumentation): add auto-instrumentation for gocql Cassandra driver
items.body:
## Description

This PR adds compile-time auto-instrumentation for the `github.com/gocql/gocql` Cassandra driver.

The instrumentation intercepts `gocql.NewSession` to wrap cluster configuration with an OpenTelemetry observer (`otelObserver`). The observer implements `gocql.QueryObserver`, `gocql.BatchObserver`, and `gocql.ConnectObserver`:
- **Queries & Batches**: Creates client spans for Cassandra query and batch executions with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions (`db.system.name: cassandra`, `db.operation.name`, `db.namespace`, `db.query.text`, `server.address`, `server.port`).
- **Connections**: Creates a `CONNECT` client span per host dial, timed from `ObservedConnect.Start`/`End` and tagged with `db.system.name`, `db.operation.name` and the host's `server.address`/`server.port`.
- **Error Handling**: Records errors and sets span status to `Error` on failed query, batch, or connect attempts.
- **Observer Chaining**: Delegates to any pre-existing user observers (`userQuery`, `userBatch`, `userConnect`) registered on `ClusterConfig`.

Unit test coverage in `hook_test.go` validates span creation, attribute population, error handling, observer delegation, and re-entrancy.

Provides automatic distributed tracing and observability for applications using the `gocql` Cassandra driver without requiring manual session wrapping or code modifications.

This adds module-local `otel.instrumentation.yml` / `otel.instrumentation.yaml` support for selecting instrumentation packages.

The YAML file is a frontend to the existing import-driven pin flow and supports third-party instrumentation packages. Selection is discovered independently per module. When a module has both a tool file and instrumentation YAML, their imports are merged and deduplicated; selections from all participating modules are then combined into the build-wide rule set.

Behavior differs by invocation:

- `otelc pin` updates persistent configuration. It updates an existing tool file, or validates and optionally prunes YAML without leaving a generated tool file. If neither exists, it generates `otel.instrumentation.go`.
- AutoPin uses temporary tool-file state, prunes invalid imports there, and restores generated files plus dependency changes after the build.

The precedence order is:

`OTELC_RULES` > `--rules` > merged import-driven selection > embedded defaults

This also updates the configuration and UX documentation for the new filename and merge behavior.

items.title: bug(tool/instrument): decl rule panics when kind is omitted/empty and identifier matches a func or type declaration
items.body:
### Describe the bug

When an `InstDeclRule` is defined with an empty `kind` (or with `kind` omitted in YAML), rule validation succeeds because `kind: ""` is documented as matching any declaration kind. However, during the instrumentation phase, `applyDeclRule` assumes the matched AST node is always a `*dst.ValueSpec` (variable/constant) and calls `util.AssertType[*dst.ValueSpec](node)`.

If the targeted identifier in the package happens to be a top-level function (`*dst.FuncDecl`) or a type declaration (`*dst.TypeSpec` / `*dst.GenDecl`), `ast.FindNamedDecl(root, identifier, "")` returns the function or type node first. `applyDeclRule` then fatals with an assertion failure (`expected *dst.ValueSpec, got *dst.FuncDecl`) instead of returning a clean error or scoping matching to `var`/`const` declarations.

### Environment

- OS: Windows / Linux / macOS (all platforms)
- Go Version: 1.25.0
- Version: main / latest `otelc`

### To Reproduce

1. Create a Go package with a top-level function named `DefaultHandler`:

```go
package app

func DefaultHandler() {}


assign_handler:
  target: app
  identifier: DefaultHandler
  replace: "CustomHandler"


expected *dst.ValueSpec, got *dst.FuncDecl


###Expected behavior
decl rules should not panic when kind is empty. The tool should either:

- Restrict kind matching in decl rules to var and const declarations (where replace and wrap initializers are valid), or
- Safely handle non-value AST nodes in applyDeclRule and return a descriptive error (e.g. declaration "DefaultHandler" is a function, but decl rules only support var or const declarations).

###Additional context
- tool/internal/rule/decl_rule.go: validate() permits kind == "" with replace or wrap.
- tool/internal/ast/shared.go: FindNamedDecl(root, name, "") checks func declarations before var/const.
- tool/internal/instrument/apply_decl.go: applyDeclRule() calls spec := util.AssertType[*dst.ValueSpec](node) unconditionally.

items.title: test(kafka/consumer): cover headerCarrier Set and Keys
items.body:
## Description

Adds unit tests for `headerCarrier`, the `TextMapCarrier` adapter over
`[]kafka.Header` in the kafka-go consumer instrumentation. `Set` was at 40% and
`Keys` at 0%, since no existing test constructed a carrier directly.

The new `carrier_test.go` covers both `Set` branches (append an absent key,
overwrite one already present), `Keys` enumeration, `Get`'s first-match and
byte-for-byte key comparison, a message with nil `Headers`, and an
inject/extract round trip through `propagation.TraceContext`.

No production code changed. Package coverage 74.5% -> 89.4%, with `Get`, `Set`
and `Keys` all at 100%.

## Motivation

`AfterReadMessage` and `ExtractContext` both wrap `msg.Headers` in a
`headerCarrier` and pass it to `propagator.Extract`, so a bug in here won't
throw. It just quietly mis-parents consumer spans.

`Set` is the interesting one. `Get` returns the first match for a repeated key,
so if `Set` ever appended instead of overwriting in place, a stale `traceparent`
would keep winning. The test drives that the way it would actually happen, by
injecting twice into the same message rather than calling `Set` twice.

To be clear about scope: `TraceContext` only calls `Get`, so `Set` and `Keys`
aren't on the consumer's hot path today. But the propagator is whatever
`otel.GetTextMapPropagator()` returns, and B3 or custom propagators do call
them, so the carrier still has to hold up as a full `TextMapCarrier`. There's a
compile-time assertion of that in the test file.

items.title: gocql instrumentation: ObserveConnect never records connection telemetry (span/metric)
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The `gocql` instrumentation (`instrumentation/github.com/gocql/gocql`) wraps a session's `QueryObserver`, `BatchObserver`, and `ConnectObserver` so it can emit telemetry for query and batch execution. However, `otelObserver.ObserveConnect` never records any telemetry of its own — it only forwards the call to the user-supplied `ConnectObserver`, if one was configured:

```go
func (o *otelObserver) ObserveConnect(oc gocql.ObservedConnect) {
	if o.userConnect != nil {
		o.userConnect.ObserveConnect(oc)
	}
}
```

Compare this to `ObserveQuery`/`ObserveBatch`, which both check `enabler.Enable()` and call a `record*Span` helper. `ObserveConnect` has neither the enabler check nor any span/event recording, so host connect/disconnect activity and connection-level errors are completely invisible in traces today.

This gap is called out explicitly in the original instrumentation request (#780):

> Connection-level events (via `ConnectObserver`) would be useful too, for visibility into host connect/disconnect and connection errors.

`gocql.ObservedConnect` (from `github.com/gocql/gocql`) already carries everything needed for this: `Host`, `Start`, `End`, and `Err`, so no new driver hooks are required — only the existing `ObserveConnect` method needs to actually produce telemetry.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Record a span (or span event) for each observed connection attempt, gated the same way query/batch spans are:

- Add an `enabler.Enable()` guard consistent with `recordQuerySpan`/`recordBatchSpan`.
- Add a `recordConnectSpan` (or similar) helper that:
  - Starts/ends a client-kind span using `oc.Start`/`oc.End` as timestamps (falling back to `time.Now()` when zero, matching the existing pattern).
  - Sets `server.address`/`server.port` from `oc.Host` when available.
  - Sets `db.system.name = cassandra`.
  - Records `oc.Err` via `span.RecordError` + `codes.Error` on failure, `codes.Ok` otherwise — same convention used for query/batch errors.
- Since `ObserveConnect` has no incoming `context.Context` (unlike `ObserveQuery`/`ObserveBatch`), the span should be started from `context.Background()` as a root span, or attributed as a span event on the current cluster-level context if one is threaded through in the future — happy to discuss the best approach in the PR.
- Add unit test coverage analogous to the existing `TestOtelObserver_ObserveQuery`/`TestOtelObserver_ObserveBatch` tests, verifying span attributes and error status for `ObserveConnect`, including the case where `oc.Err != nil`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Leaving connection events unobserved and only documenting the limitation — rejected, since the original instrumentation request explicitly asked for this and the hook already exists in the observer, just unused.
- Emitting connection events as OTel logs instead of spans — worth a short discussion, since connect/disconnect is arguably more "event" than "span," but spans keep this consistent with how query/batch telemetry is already modeled in this package.

**Additional context**

- Relevant file: `instrumentation/github.com/gocql/gocql/hook.go` (`otelObserver.ObserveConnect`, `recordQuerySpan`, `recordBatchSpan` for the existing pattern to follow).
- Existing (currently connect-telemetry-free) test: `instrumentation/github.com/gocql/gocql/hook_test.go`, `TestOtelObserver_ObserveConnect`.
- Parent tracking issue: #780.

<sub>**Tip**: [React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

items.title: fix(instrumentation): add missing span.RecordError() calls
items.body:
## Description

This PR adds missing `span.RecordError(err)` calls in database/sql and Redis instrumentations to ensure errors are properly recorded as span events.

Currently, these instrumentations set span status to `Error` but do not call `span.RecordError(err)`, which means:
- Errors don't appear in the span's event list
- Stack traces are not captured
- Error details are lost (only status code remains)
- Debugging production issues is significantly harder

This PR brings these instrumentations into alignment with the canonical error handling pattern already used by `net/http/client`, `kafka-go`, `k8s.io/client-go`, and other instrumentations in this repository.

## Motivation

Without `span.RecordError()`, errors in database/sql and Redis operations only set the span status to `Error` but don't create exception events. This violates the [OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for exception recording](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/exceptions/) and makes debugging production issues significantly harder.

**The Problem:**

When a SQL query or Redis command fails:
```go
// Current (incorrect) pattern in affected code:
if err != nil {
    span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())  // ❌ Status set but no event created
}
```

Users see error status codes in traces but:
- ❌ No exception events in trace visualization tools
- ❌ No stack traces captured  
- ❌ Error details are incomplete
- ❌ Difficult to debug root causes

**The Solution:**

Follow the canonical pattern used by 8 other instrumentations in this repository:
```go
// Correct pattern:
if err != nil {
    span.RecordError(err)                      // ✅ Creates exception event
    span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())   // ✅ Sets span status
}
```

**Instrumentations already following this pattern correctly:**
- ✅ `net/http/client` (lines 144-146 in `client_hook.go`)
- ✅ `github.com/segmentio/kafka-go/consumer` (lines 172-174 in `consumer_hook.go`)
- ✅ `github.com/segmentio/kafka-go/producer` (lines 168-174 in `producer_hook.go`)
- ✅ `k8s.io/client-go` (lines 94-96, 143-145 in `hook.go`)
- ✅ `github.com/gin-gonic/gin` (lines 98-99 in `context_hook.go`)
- ✅ `github.com/openai/openai-go` (all versions)
- ✅ `github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go`

This PR brings `database/sql` and `redis/v9` into alignment with the established pattern.

---

## Changes Made

### 1. `instrumentation/database/sql/client.go`
**Function:** `instrumentEnd()` (line 648)  
**Change:** Added `span.RecordError(err)` before `span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())`  
**Impact:** All SQL operations (query, exec, ping, commit, rollback, etc.) now properly record errors as span events

```diff
 defer span.End()
 if err != nil {
+    span.RecordError(err)
     span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())
 }
```

### 2. `instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/hook.go`
**Function:** `ProcessHook()` (line 77)  
**Change:** Added `span.RecordError(err)` before `span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())`  
**Impact:** Single Redis commands now properly record errors as span events (correctly excludes `redis.Nil`)

```diff
 err := next(ctx, cmd)
 if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, redis.Nil) {
+    span.RecordError(err)
     span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())
 }
```

**Function:** `ProcessPipelineHook()` (line 124)  
**Change:** Added `span.RecordError(err)` before `span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())`  
**Impact:** Redis pipeline operations now properly record errors as span events

```diff
 err := next(ctx, cmds)
 if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, redis.Nil) {
+    span.RecordError(err)
     span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())
 }
```

### 3. `instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/hook_test.go`
**Functions:** `TestProcessHook_RecordsError()`, `TestProcessPipelineHook_RecordsError()`  
**Change:** Added verification that exception events are created

```diff
 span := spans[0]
 assert.Equal(t, codes.Error, span.Status().Code)
+
+// Check that error was recorded
+events := span.Events()
+require.Len(t, events, 1)
+assert.Equal(t, "exception", events[0].Name)
```

---

## Testing

### Redis Tests
All 26 tests pass:
```bash
cd instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9
go test -v ./...
# PASS: 26/26 tests
```

**Key tests:**
- `TestProcessHook_RecordsError` - Verifies exception events are created for single commands
- `TestProcessPipelineHook_RecordsError` - Verifies exception events are created for pipelines
- `TestProcessHook_RedisNilNotError` - Confirms `redis.Nil` is correctly excluded from error recording

### Database/SQL
- No unit tests exist for `client.go` hooks (uses struct field injection at compile time)
- Integration tests cover error paths and will verify the behavior
- Change is minimal and follows the exact pattern used by other instrumentations

---

## Impact

**Before this PR:**
```
SQL query fails → Span status = Error ❌ but no exception event ❌
Redis cmd fails → Span status = Error ❌ but no exception event ❌
```

**After this PR:**
```
SQL query fails → Span status = Error ✅ AND exception event ✅
Redis cmd fails → Span status = Error ✅ AND exception event ✅
```

Users now get:
- ✅ Complete error information in traces

items.title: fix(genai): getProviderName returns inconsistent provider names for the same host
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`getProviderName()` in the OpenAI GenAI instrumentation sets the `gen_ai.provider.name` span attribute by looping over a `map[string]string` of hostname keywords and returning the first substring match. Go does not guarantee map iteration order and randomizes it on every `range`. When a request host contains more than one keyword from the map (realistic behind API gateways or proxies that route to multiple providers), the function can return a different provider name on different calls for the exact same input.

The same code is duplicated in three places:
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/middleware.go`
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v2/middleware.go`
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v3/middleware.go`

### Environment

- Go Version: 1.25 (per go.mod)

### To Reproduce

Take the `providerMapping` map and `getProviderName` function as they exist today (around lines 28-61 in any of the three `middleware.go` files) and call it repeatedly with a host that matches two different keywords:

```go
host := "litellm-gateway.mistral-together-proxy.internal" // matches both "mistral" and "together"
results := map[string]int{}
for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
    results[getProviderName(host)]++
}
fmt.Println(results)
```

On my machine this printed `map[mistral:14 together:6]` across 20 calls with no code path change in between - same input, two different outputs.

### Expected behavior

`getProviderName` should return the same provider name for the same host on every call. It's doing "first matching keyword wins" style lookup, which needs a data structure with a fixed, predictable check order. A map doesn't give you that in Go.

### Additional context

Root cause: `providerMapping` is a `map[string]string`, iterated with `for keyword, provider := range providerMapping`. The Go spec leaves map iteration order unspecified, and the runtime deliberately randomizes the starting point on each `range`. Returning on the first match inside a map loop is non-deterministic any time more than one key can match.

A fix would replace `providerMapping` with an ordered slice of `{keyword, provider}` pairs and iterate the slice instead of the map, so the check order comes from how the list is written rather than from the runtime.

This affects the `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute on every OpenAI-instrumented span, so anyone running behind a gateway or proxy whose hostname matches more than one entry in the table gets inconsistent telemetry.

items.title: bug(instrumentation): openai streaming reader drops final SSE chunk without trailing newline
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`streamingReader.processSSELines()` in the OpenAI GenAI streaming instrumentation only flushes and parses lines that are terminated by `\n`. It buffers everything after the last `\n` as a possibly-incomplete line and holds onto it for the next `Read()` call.

If the upstream SSE stream ends without a trailing newline after the final `data: ...` line, say the connection closes right after the last chunk with no following newline before EOF, that leftover data just sits in `lineBuffer` and is never parsed. `Read()` calls `finalize()` on the same call where it sees the EOF, so the final chunk's `finish_reason`, response `id`, and usage/token counts never make it onto the span.

Same code is duplicated in `openai-go`, `openai-go/v2`, and `openai-go/v3` (`streaming.go`), so it affects all three.

### Environment

- Go Version: 1.25 (per go.mod)
- Version: main / latest `otelc`

### To Reproduce

I wrote a quick reproduction with a fake `io.ReadCloser` that returns the final SSE chunk and `io.EOF` in the same `Read()` call, which mirrors how a lot of real readers behave once the connection is closed:

```go
body := []byte(`data: {"id":"chatcmpl-final","model":"gpt-4","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","delta":{}}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":10,"completion_tokens":5,"total_tokens":15}}`)

sr := newStreamingReader(reader, span, start, "gpt-4", "chat", "openai", opChat, ctx)
buf := make([]byte, 4096)
for {
    _, err := sr.Read(buf)
    if err != nil {
        break
    }
}
```

`sr.id` stays empty and `sr.outputTokens` stays `0` even though the chunk was fully delivered to `Read()`, it's just sitting unparsed in `lineBuffer` when `finalize()` runs.

In practice OpenAI's real streaming responses are `data: ...\n\n` terminated so this may be rare in the wild, but any proxy/gateway or SDK version that trims the trailing newline, or any connection that gets cut right after the last full chunk, would silently lose the final usage/finish_reason attributes with no error.

### Expected behavior

`processSSELines()` (or the `Read()` caller) should also parse whatever's left in `lineBuffer` when the underlying reader reports an error (EOF or otherwise), not just on a following `\n`. The final chunk's data shouldn't depend on whether the stream happens to end with a trailing newline.

### Additional context

- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/streaming.go`: `processSSELines()`, `Read()`
- Duplicated in `v2/streaming.go` and `v3/streaming.go`
- Not related to open PR #825/#826 (`getProviderName` determinism), different bug, different file.

items.title: fix(database/sql): db.system.name falls back to other_sql for the "sqlite" driver alias
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`DbClientRequestTraceAttrs` sets the `db.system.name` span attribute from `req.DriverName` via a `switch` statement that only recognizes the driver name `sqlite3`. The DSN parser in the same instrumentation module already treats `sqlite3` and `sqlite` as the same database - both are routed to `parseSQLiteDSN` in `dsnparse/parse.go`'s driver registry - but the semconv switch never got a matching case added for `sqlite`. A driver registered under the name `sqlite` falls through to `default` and gets tagged `db.system.name = "other_sql"` instead of `"sqlite"`.

Affected file: `instrumentation/database/sql/semconv/db.go`

### Environment

- Go Version: 1.25 (per go.mod)

### To Reproduce

Call `DbClientRequestTraceAttrs` with `DriverName: "sqlite"` (the name registered by `modernc.org/sqlite`, a common pure-Go SQLite driver used specifically to avoid CGO) and check the resulting attribute:

```go
attrs := DbClientRequestTraceAttrs(DatabaseSqlRequest{
    DriverName: "sqlite",
    // ...
})
// db.system.name comes back as "other_sql", not "sqlite"
```

### Expected behavior

`db.system.name` should be `"sqlite"` for both the `sqlite3` and `sqlite` driver names, matching how `dsnparse/parse.go`'s registry already treats them as the same database format.

### Additional context

I checked the other driver families in the same registry - postgres has 4 aliases, mysql has 2, sqlserver has 2, oracle has 4 - and all of them are currently listed consistently in both `dsnparse`'s registry and `semconv/db.go`'s switch. Only the sqlite pair had drifted out of sync. Since these two lists are maintained by hand in two separate files, the same kind of gap could reappear for a different driver later. I'm keeping this fix scoped to the concrete bug, but it may be worth a separate follow-up issue proposing a single shared table if maintainers are interested.

I'd like to work on this - a one-line fix plus a test case mirroring the existing "sqlite3 driver" case in `db_test.go`.

items.title: bug(ci): run behavior tests when instrumentation rule YAML changes
items.body:
## Description

Instrumentation rule files under `instrumentation/**/otelc.yaml` define the production compile-time instrumentation behavior.

Currently, if a pull request modifies only one of these rule files, the unit, integration, and end-to-end test workflows are not triggered.

For example, a change limited to:

```text
instrumentation/net/http/client/otelc.yaml
```

does not match the code path filters in:

- `.github/workflows/test-unit.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/test-integration.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/test-e2e.yaml`

As a result, the test jobs are skipped. Their corresponding required **Done** jobs still succeed because skipped jobs are treated as successful. This means an instrumentation rule change can modify how `otelc` rewrites applications without running the behavioral test suites.

## Expected behavior

Changes to instrumentation rule YAML files should trigger the same test suites as other production instrumentation changes.

## Suggested fix

Extend the workflow path filters to include instrumentation rule files:

```yaml
instrumentation/**/*.yaml
instrumentation/**/*.yml
```

This keeps the filters targeted:

- Go source files are already covered by the existing `**/*.go` pattern.
- The additional YAML patterns ensure rule-only changes also execute the relevant test suites.

items.title: docs: mention Git line-ending setup for Windows/WSL contributors
items.body:
While setting up the project locally on Windows (via WSL), I hit spurious golden-file test failures in `tool/internal/instrument` — every failing diff showed one blank line dropped per code block (e.g. `@@ -1,5 +1,4 @@` patterns across nearly all `TestInstrumentation_Integration` subtests).

Root cause: my original clone had `core.autocrlf` enabled (a common Windows Git default), which introduced CRLF line endings across most source files. This appears to affect how the `dst` AST printer handles blank-line preservation during code generation, causing golden-file comparisons to fail even though the actual logic is correct.

Fix: Re-cloning with `git config --global core.autocrlf false` resolved it completely.

I noticed CI does run on Windows (per `docs/testing.md`), but there's no existing mention of this in `CONTRIBUTING.md` or the docs for local Windows/WSL setup. Happy to open a small PR adding a note about this if it'd be useful.

## Description

This PR fixes a span memory leak and missing error status when `db.BeginTx` or `db.Begin` returns an error in `database/sql` instrumentation.

In `instrumentation/database/sql/client.go`, `afterTxInstrumentation` was checking `if tx == nil || ictx.GetData() == nil` and returning early before calling `instrumentEnd(ictx, err)`. When `db.BeginTx` fails (returning `tx = nil` and `err != nil`), `instrumentEnd` was never called, causing the transaction span to remain un-ended in memory and omitting error telemetry.

**Changes:**
1. Modified `afterTxInstrumentation` in `instrumentation/database/sql/client.go` to guard property assignment with `tx != nil && ictx.GetData() != nil` and invoke `instrumentEnd(ictx, err)` unconditionally.
2. Re-packaged `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz` and rebuilt `otelc`.
3. Extended `test/apps/dbclient` and added `TransactionFailure` subtest in `test/integration/db_client_test.go` asserting that a failed `db.BeginTx` call correctly ends the span and records `codes.Error`.

## Motivation

Fixes #835

Without this fix, failed transaction starts leak active span objects in memory and fail to export error telemetry to collectors.

Setting OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=gin has no effect: the hooks still run, the span is still renamed from GET to GET /users/:id, http.route is still set, and nothing is logged to say the setting was ignored. Every other instrumentation in the repo declares an instrumentationKey and an enabler, and checks it before doing any work. For example instrumentation/net/http/server/server_hook.go: ```go type netHttpServerEnabler struct{} func (n netHttpServerEnabler) Enable() bool { return runtime.Instrumented(instrumentationKey) } ``` Grepping for runtime.Instrumented( turns up 17 call sites covering net/http (client and server), grpc (client and server), kafka-go (producer and consumer), database/sql, redis, mongo, k8s.io/client-go, openai-go (v1/v2/v3), anthropic-sdk-go, log, slog and logrus. instrumentation/github.com/gin-gonic/gin/ is the only instrumentation package with no key, no enabler and no check. gin.go there is four lines and only builds a logger, and BeforeNext / AfterNext in context_hook.go do their work unconditionally. ### Environment - OS: Linux - Go Version: 1.25.0 - Version: main @ 72d167c ### To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Drop this into instrumentation/github.com/gin-gonic/gin/context_hook_test.go and run go test ./... from that module. It fails on current main: 2. ```go func TestBeforeNext_DisabledInstrumentation(t *testing.T) { t.Setenv("OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS", "gin") sr, tr := setupContextTracer(t) _, span := tr.Start(context.Background(), "GET") c := newGinContextWithRoute(t, "GET", "/users/:id", "/users/42", span) ictx := hooktest.NewMockHookContext(c) BeforeNext(ictx, c) span.End() require.Len(t, sr.Ended(), 1) assert.Equal(t, "GET", sr.Ended()[0].Name(), "span name must not be rewritten when gin instrumentation is disabled") } ``` 3. See Error ``` --- FAIL: TestBeforeNext_DisabledInstrumentation (0.00s) Error: Not equal: expected: "GET" actual : "GET /users/:id" ``` The same thing shows up end to end. Build test/apps/ginserver with otelc, run it with OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=gin exported, hit a route, and the exported span still comes through named after the route template with http.route set. ### Expected behavior OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=gin should stop the gin hooks from touching the span, the same way it works for every other instrumentation. An allow-list that omits gin, for example OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=nethttp, should behave the same way. ### Additional context I think this has gone unnoticed because gin does not create its own span. The span comes from the net/http server instrumentation and gin only enriches it, so disabling nethttp masks the problem: with no span in the request context trace.SpanFromContext returns a non-recording span and BeforeNext bails at the IsRecording() check. You only hit the gap if you want to keep HTTP server spans and drop just the gin enrichment, which seems reasonable to want. http.route is the attribute most likely to cause a cardinality problem on a large router, and these hooks fire once per middleware per request rather than once per request, since gin calls c.Next() at every layer of the chain. The other half of this is that docs/instrument-guide.md never mentions runtime.Instrumented, the enabler pattern or instrumentationKey anywhere. Nothing in the guide tells someone adding a new instrumentation that the gate is required, so gin (#501) shipped without one. Fixing gin on its own leaves the next instrumentation free to do the same, so I would like to add the requirement to the guide in the same change. Gin gets its own key (GIN, written as gin in the env var). This matches how kafka-go producer/consumer and grpc client/server are separate packages sharing one key, and it lets users keep nethttp spans while dropping route enrichment. Related: #705 lists per-instrumentation enable/disable (go: : enabled) as one of the first consumers of the declarative config work, and runtime.Instrumented is the mechanism that would sit underneath it, so it seems worth having the current one applied consistently first. #807 and #808 are also circling the same surface from the documentation side. **Tip**: [React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).

items.title: fix(instrumentation/gin): gin instrumentation cannot be disabled at runtime
items.body:
## Description

The gin hooks never consulted `runtime.Instrumented`, so `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=gin` did nothing. `BeforeNext` and `AfterNext` ran regardless, the span was still renamed from `GET` to `GET /users/:id`, and `http.route` was still set. Gin was the only instrumentation package in the repo without the enabler gate the other thirteen use.

`gin.go` now declares `instrumentationKey = "GIN"` and a `ginEnabler`, following the same shape as `net/http/server`, `redis` and `anthropic-sdk-go`. Both hooks return early when the instrumentation is disabled, and the check sits before either of them touches `nextDepthKey` so the depth counter they share stays balanced.

Two details worth flagging for review:

Gin carries its own key rather than sharing `NETHTTP`. It only enriches the span that the `net/http` server instrumentation creates, so sharing a key would leave "disable gin" with no way to express it. A separate key lets an operator keep HTTP server spans while dropping the route enrichment, which is the case that motivated the issue.

`BeforeNext` does not log on the disabled path, unlike `net/http/server`. Gin calls `c.Next()` once per middleware in the chain rather than once per request, so a per-call debug line would be noisy for no benefit.

This also adds a "Runtime Enable/Disable Gate" section to `docs/instrument-guide.md`. The guide never mentioned `runtime.Instrumented`, the enabler pattern or `instrumentationKey` anywhere, so nothing told a contributor adding an instrumentation that the gate was required. That omission is the reason one could ship without it, and fixing gin alone would leave the next one free to repeat it.

## Motivation

The gap is invisible unless you want HTTP server spans without gin's route enrichment. Disabling `nethttp` hides it, because with no span in the request context `trace.SpanFromContext` returns a non-recording span and `BeforeNext` bails at the `IsRecording()` check. Keeping the enrichment separately switchable matters because `http.route` is the attribute most likely to become a cardinality problem on a large router, and because these hooks run at every middleware layer rather than once per request.

Fixes #839

## Verification

Four unit tests cover the gate: disabled through the deny-list, absent from the allow-list, present in the allow-list so the gate cannot over-suppress, and `AfterNext` not recording `c.Error()` values when disabled. Three of the four fail without the source change; the allow-list case passes either way by design.

Checked end to end as well, building `test/apps/ginserver` with `otelc` and running it with the console exporter and `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=gin`. Before the change the exported span still came through as `GET /hello/:name` carrying `http.route`, with `HTTP server instrumentation initialized` in the log confirming `nethttp` was live. After it, the span stays `GET` with no `http.route`.

`tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz` regenerated and verified to match the sources.

---

items.title: fix(ast): check return error of file.Close() in WriteFile to prevent lost AST write errors
items.body:
### Description
In `tool/internal/ast/parser.go`, `WriteFile` relies solely on `defer file.Close()` when flushing AST data to disk via `decorator.Restorer.Fprint`. If an I/O error occurs during the flush/close step (e.g. disk space exhausted), `file.Close()` returns an error that is currently ignored, causing `WriteFile` to return success (`nil`).

### Proposed Solution
Explicitly invoke and check `file.Close()` after calling `r.Fprint(file, root)` and return any close error wrapped with `ex.Wrapf`.
