items.title: test(tool/internal/setup): TestListBuildPlan fails on Windows due to hardcoded sh executable
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Running unit tests for package `tool/internal/setup` on Windows causes `TestListBuildPlan` to fail. The test mock in `find_test.go` attempts to simulate `go build -a -x -n` output by executing `sh -c "<script>"`, hardcoding `sh` and POSIX heredoc syntax (`cat <<'EOF' >&2 ... EOF`).

On Windows environments where `sh` is not available in `%PATH%`, `exec.Command("sh", ...)` fails immediately with `exec: "sh": executable file not found in %PATH%`.

### Environment

 - OS: Windows (Windows 10 / 11 / Windows Server)
 - Go Version: go1.25+
 - Version: `main`

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Clone the repository on a Windows environment (Command Prompt / PowerShell / CI Windows runner).
2. Run unit tests for `tool/internal/setup`:
   ```cmd
   go test -v ./tool/internal/setup
   ```
3. Observe the test failure output:
   ```text
   === RUN   TestListBuildPlan/filters_compile_and_cgo_commands
       find_test.go:409: 
           Error Trace:    c:/Users/Vishal/Code_File/Projects/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/internal/setup/find_test.go:409
           Error:          Received unexpected error:
                           failed to run build plan: 
                           : exec: "sh": executable file not found in %PATH%
           Test:           TestListBuildPlan/filters_compile_and_cgo_commands
   --- FAIL: TestListBuildPlan (1.99s)
       --- FAIL: TestListBuildPlan/filters_compile_and_cgo_commands (0.62s)
       --- FAIL: TestListBuildPlan/passes_additional_build_args (0.30s)
       --- FAIL: TestListBuildPlan/returns_build_failure (0.27s)
       --- FAIL: TestListBuildPlan/empty_build_plan (0.24s)
       --- FAIL: TestListBuildPlan/ignores_malformed_compile_lines (0.23s)
       --- FAIL: TestListBuildPlan/test_subcommand_lists_a_go_test_plan (0.33s)
   ```

### Expected behavior

Unit tests in `tool/internal/setup` should execute and pass cleanly across all supported operating systems (Linux, macOS, and Windows) without assuming a POSIX shell environment.

### Additional context

#### Root Cause Analysis

In [tool/internal/setup/find_test.go](file:///c:/Users/Vishal/Code_File/Projects/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/internal/setup/find_test.go#L382-L397):

```go
execCommandContext = func(
    _ context.Context,
    name string,
    args ...string,
) *exec.Cmd {
    assert.Equal(t, "go", name)
    assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedGoCmd, args)

    script := "cat <<'EOF' >&2\n" + tt.buildPlan + "\nEOF\n"
    if tt.buildFails {
        script += "\nexit 1\n"
    }

    return exec.Command("sh", "-c", script)
}
```

Line 395 hardcodes `exec.Command("sh", "-c", script)`. On native Windows, `sh` is not present in `%PATH%`, causing the sub-process invocation to fail before writing the expected build plan output to `stderr`.

#### Suggested Fix

Replace `exec.Command("sh", ...)` with a standard Go test helper process pattern (`TestHelperProcess` re-executing `os.Executable()`) to print `tt.buildPlan` to `stderr` and exit with status code `0` or `1`. This provides 100% cross-platform compatibility across Windows, Linux, and macOS without relying on external system binaries.

items.title: test: fix Windows test failures due to POSIX shell assumptions
items.body:
Fixes #920

### What changed
Two test files assumed POSIX-only shell tooling that does not exist on Windows:

- `tool/internal/setup/find_test.go`: `TestListBuildPlan` mocked
  `execCommandContext` with `exec.Command("sh", "-c", script)`.
  On Windows there is no `sh`, so all 6 sub-tests failed.

- `tool/util/sys_test.go`: `TestRunCmd` used `echo` as the test
  command. `echo` is a shell built-in on Windows and is not
  exec-able as a standalone binary.

### How it was fixed

**find_test.go** — adopted the standard [TestHelperProcess pattern]
used in the Go standard library: the test binary re-invokes itself
with a dedicated helper function that reads the desired build plan and
exit behavior from environment variables (`GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS`,
`GO_HELPER_BUILD_PLAN`, `GO_HELPER_BUILD_FAILS`). No `sh` required.

**sys_test.go** — replaced `echo` with `go version` / `go env GOOS`,
which are always available wherever Go is installed.

### Testing
- `go test -v -run "TestListBuildPlan|TestRunCmd" ./tool/internal/setup/... ./tool/util/...`
  passes on Windows (all 9 targeted sub-tests pass).
- `go test ./tool/util/...` passes fully on Windows.

items.title: Kafka binary message key causes traces export: string field contains invalid UTF-8
items.body: ### Describe the bug Kafka message keys are binary-safe and may contain arbitrary bytes, such as binary UUID representations, but the Kafka instrumentation writes them into the string attribute without UTF-8 validation.Since OTLP protobuf requires string fields to be valid UTF-8, trace export fails: `traces export: string field contains invalid UTF-8` ### Environment - OS: macOS Sequoia 15.7.4 arm64 - Go Version: 1.26.2 - Version: v1.0.1+eddebad ### To Reproduce 1. copy this minimal example ``` go package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "strings" "time" "github.com/google/uuid" "github.com/segmentio/kafka-go" ) func main() { brokers := strings.Split(env("KAFKA_BROKERS", "localhost:9092"), ",") topic := env("KAFKA_TOPIC", "utf8-repro") writer := &kafka.Writer{ Addr: kafka.TCP(brokers...), Topic: topic, Balancer: &kafka.LeastBytes{}, RequiredAcks: kafka.RequireAll, } defer writer.Close() id := uuid.New() fmt.Printf(string(id[:])) msg := kafka.Message{ Key: id[:], Value: []byte("value"), } ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second) defer cancel() for i := 0; i < 10; i++ { err := writer.WriteMessages(ctx, msg) if err != nil { fmt.Printf("write failed at message %d: %v\n", i, err) } else { fmt.Printf("write completed message %d to topic %s via %v\n", i, topic, brokers) } } time.Sleep(10 * time.Second) } func env(name, fallback string) string { if v := os.Getenv(name); v != "" { return v } return fallback } ``` 2. run `otelc go build` 3. create topic `utf8-repro` and start your Kafka at localhost:9092 4. run the application and you will see `"level":"ERROR","msg":"OpenTelemetry SDK error","error":"traces export: string field contains invalid UTF-8"` ### Expected behavior - OTLP trace export should succeed ### Additional context This issue is similar to the issue I recently discovered and fixed in the sibling project of this repository, https://github.com/alibaba/loongsuite-go (issue: https://github.com/alibaba/loongsuite-go/issues/738). It may be worth considering whether a generic validation layer should be introduced for trace data export. In `loongsuite-go`, the issue was caused by Redis instrumentation not validating UTF-8 strings before adding them to span attributes. In this repository, Redis instrumentation already has UTF-8 validation, but Kafka message keys still lack such validation.Some instrumentations do not have this risk because they only handle data that is guaranteed to be valid UTF-8, while others interact with binary-safe data sources that may legitimately contain arbitrary bytes. When exporting traces through OTLP, span attributes are serialized using Protocol Buffers, and protobuf string fields require valid UTF-8. Could we introduce a common validation layer before exporting trace data to prevent similar issues across different instrumentations?
items.author: Modo-me

items.title: fix(setup): close file handle on stale lock verification in tryAcquire
items.body:
### Problem
In `tool/internal/setup/lock.go`, `tryAcquire` attempts to acquire the build lock using `flock.New(path)`. After acquiring the lock, `lockFileIsCurrent` checks whether the held lock handle matches the file at `path` on disk (guarding against races where another process unlinked the file prior to release).

If `lockFileIsCurrent` returns `!current` or returns an error, `tryAcquire` calls `_ = lock.Unlock()`.

However, in `gofrs/flock`, `lock.Unlock()` only unlocks the flock advisory mechanism but does NOT close the underlying file descriptor (`os.File`). Unlike earlier error paths in `tryAcquire` (lines 133 & 140) which explicitly call `_ = lock.Close()`, lines 145 & 149 omit `lock.Close()`, leaking open file handles when stale lock verification retries occur.

### Proposed Solution
Ensure `_ = lock.Close()` is called whenever `!current` or a `lockFileIsCurrent` error occurs:

```go
if err != nil {
    _ = lock.Unlock()
    _ = lock.Close()
    return nil, false, leftover, err
}
if !current {
    _ = lock.Unlock()
    _ = lock.Close()
    return nil, false, leftover, nil
}
```

## Description
In `tool/internal/setup/lock.go`, `tryAcquire` attempts to acquire the build lock using `flock.New(path)`. After acquiring the lock, `lockFileIsCurrent` checks whether the held lock handle matches the file at `path` on disk.

items.title: fix(tool): preserve spaces in CGO build-plan directories
items.body:
## Description

Updates `parseCdDir` to preserve the complete directory path emitted by the Go build plan, including paths containing spaces.

The parser now:

- Accepts only a valid `cd ` prefix.
- Preserves the full directory path.
- Rejects empty `cd` commands without panicking.
- Ignores unrelated commands such as `cdrom`.

Regression tests cover paths with spaces, malformed commands, trailing whitespace, Windows paths, and `findCommands` filtering.

## Motivation

For CGO packages, the parsed directory is associated with the generated object directory and later used to resolve the original Go source file.

Previously, a path such as `/tmp/test project` was truncated to `/tmp/test`. This could prevent CGO source resolution and cause applicable instrumentation rules to be skipped.

Fixes #912

`ParseImportCfg` (and the underlying `parse`) now configures its `bufio.Scanner` with a custom buffer whose maximum capacity is 10 MiB instead of the default `bufio.MaxScanTokenSize` (64 KiB). items.title: database/sql: IPv6 DSNs produce a malformed server.address and no server.port
items.body:
### Describe the bug

If a DSN contains a literal IPv6 address, the client span gets the port glued onto `server.address` and no `server.port` at all.

`DSNInfo.Addr()` joins with a plain `:`, so `Host="::1"` + `Port="3306"` becomes `::1:3306`. `DbClientRequestTraceAttrs` passes that to `net.SplitHostPort`, which errors with "too many colons in address", and the fallback uses the whole endpoint as `server.address` and drops the port.

Affects mysql/mariadb, postgres/pgx/lib-pq, sqlserver/mssql and clickhouse. Oracle escapes it because `oracleSplitHostPort()` leaves the brackets on. IPv4 and hostname DSNs are fine.

### To Reproduce

Visible at the parser level:

```go
info := ParseDSN("mysql", "user:pass@tcp([::1]:3306)/mydb")
// info.Host "::1", info.Port "3306", both correct
info.Addr()  // "::1:3306"  -> net.SplitHostPort errors
```

End to end:

1. `make build`
2. Build `test/apps/dbclient` with otelc
3. Run with `-op=query -driver=mysql -dsn='user:pass@tcp([::1]:3306)/testdb'`
4. Exported span:

```
attrs=map[... db.system.name:mysql network.transport:tcp server.address:::1:3306]
```

Postgres with `[2001:db8::1]:5432` gives `server.address:2001:db8::1:5432`. Same run with `127.0.0.1` is correct, so it's IPv6 specific.

### Expected behavior

```
server.address:::1
server.port:3306
```

Same as what the grpc and net/http semconv helpers already do for `[::1]:8080`.

items.title: fix(setup): use atomic write for storing matched rules in SetupPhase.store
items.body:
### Description
In `tool/internal/setup/store.go`, `SetupPhase.store` writes the JSON representation of matched rule sets using `os.Create` and `file.Write`, relying on `defer file.Close()`.

If an I/O error or disk flush failure occurs during `file.Close()`, the error is swallowed. Additionally, writing directly to the target file path can leave behind corrupted JSON artifacts if the process is terminated mid-write.

### Location
- `tool/internal/setup/store.go`: lines 84–107

### Proposed Solution
Refactor `SetupPhase.store` to use `util.WriteFileAtomic(f, bs)`, ensuring safe atomic replacements and proper error checking on file close operations.

items.title: fix(database/sql): IPv6 DSNs drop server.port and corrupt server.address
items.body:
## Description

`DSNInfo.Addr()` joined host and port with a plain `:`, so an IPv6 host came out as `::1:3306`. `DbClientRequestTraceAttrs` splits that back apart with `net.SplitHostPort`, which rejects it, and the error path falls back to using the whole endpoint as `server.address` and dropping `server.port`.

Switched the join to `net.JoinHostPort`, which brackets only when it has to. Three supporting changes so it holds everywhere:

- `Addr()` strips brackets off the host before joining. `DSNInfo` is exported and `RegisterDSNParser` is a supported extension point, so a custom parser can hand back `u.Host` (brackets kept) instead of `u.Hostname()`. Without this it double-brackets and breaks the same way.
- The libpq and ADO.NET key=value paths strip brackets too, so the `Host` field stays bare regardless of dialect.
- `oracleSplitHostPort()` is now bracket-aware. It previously split on the last colon, which mangles a bracketed host with no port (`[::1]` gave host `[`, port `:1]`).

Worth noting this can't be fixed downstream: `::1:3306` is itself a valid IPv6 address, so once the strings are joined there's no way to tell the port back out. `Addr()` is the only place it can go.

Tests:

- `parse_addr_test.go` : round-trips `Addr()` back through `net.SplitHostPort` for every dialect, plus the custom-parser path.
- `semconv/db_ipv6_test.go` : asserts the actual `server.address` / `server.port` attributes, including end to end from a parsed DSN.


## Motivation

Any app using an IPv6 literal in its DSN gets a malformed `server.address` and no `server.port` at all, on every span. Affects mysql/mariadb, postgres/pgx/lib-pq, sqlserver/mssql and clickhouse. Oracle escaped it by accident because it left the brackets on.

Fixes #934

items.title: test(util): `TestRunCmd` fails on Windows due to non-existent `echo` executable
items.body:
### Describe the bug

When running unit tests on Windows (`go test ./tool/util/...` or `go test ./...`), `TestRunCmd` in [`tool/util/sys_test.go`](file:///c:/Users/Vishal/Code_File/Projects/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/util/sys_test.go#L16-L47) fails with:

```text
--- FAIL: TestRunCmd (0.04s)
    --- FAIL: TestRunCmd/simple_echo_command (0.03s)
        sys_test.go:43: RunCmd() error = failed to run command "echo" in dir '""' with args: [hello]: exec: "echo": executable file not found in %PATH%, expectErr false
    --- FAIL: TestRunCmd/command_with_multiple_arguments (0.04s)
        sys_test.go:43: RunCmd() error = failed to run command "echo" in dir '""' with args: [hello world]: exec: "echo": executable file not found in %PATH%, expectErr false
```

### Environment

 - OS: Windows (x64)
 - Go Version: 1.25+
 - Version: main / v1.0.1

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Clone the repository on a Windows machine.
2. Run `go test ./tool/util/...`
3. Observe test failure in `TestRunCmd/simple_echo_command` and `TestRunCmd/command_with_multiple_arguments`.

### Expected behavior

Unit tests should pass across all supported operating systems (Linux, macOS, Windows).

### Additional context

**Root Cause:**
`TestRunCmd` uses `"echo"` as the target binary for test execution. On Unix systems (Linux/macOS), `/bin/echo` is a standalone executable available on `$PATH`. On Windows, `echo` is a shell built-in command in `cmd.exe` and `powershell.exe` rather than a standalone executable binary in `%PATH%`. Consequently, Go's `os/exec` fails to find `echo` in `%PATH%`.

**Proposed Fix:**
Update `TestRunCmd` in [`tool/util/sys_test.go`](file:///c:/Users/Vishal/Code_File/Projects/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/util/sys_test.go#L16-L47) to use a cross-platform executable binary such as `"go", "version"` (similar to how `TestRunCmdInDir` is tested in [`tool/util/sys_test.go`](file:///c:/Users/Vishal/Code_File/Projects/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/tool/util/sys_test.go#L124)).

items.title: fix(tool): forward trimpath when resolving import archives
items.body:
## Description

Forward `-trimpath` to the nested `go list -export` calls used to resolve archives for imports introduced by instrumentation. This keeps injected archives in the same build context as the outer `go build`.

Without the flag, an instrumented dependency can be compiled with `-trimpath` while an injected transitive archive is resolved without it. The linker then rejects the pair because their export fingerprints differ.

The database/sql integration build now uses `-trimpath` so this archive-resolution path is covered.

## Reproduction

I reproduced the `pkg/runtime` fingerprint mismatch reported at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/issues/922 on current `main` with Go 1.26.5 on macOS/arm64, in addition to the reported Linux reproductions. Forwarding `-trimpath` removes that fingerprint mismatch.

The full Venator build then reaches a separate duplicate-symbol failure involving log instrumentation. That independent multi-target issue remains outside this PR.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/setup -run TestExtractBuildFlags`
- `go -C test test -tags integration -run ^TestDBClient -count=1 ./integration`
- `make all` was attempted; build and formatting completed, but full lint is currently blocked by pre-existing `goconst`, `modernize`, and `sloglint` findings on current `main`. A prior full integration invocation also exposed the existing Mongo v1/v2 shared-app lock race; the focused database/sql integration test passes.

items.title: bug(pkg): nil pointer dereference in MongoDB client hooks when client options is nil
items.body:
### Describe the bug

A nil pointer dereference panic occurs in BeforeConnect and BeforeNewClient in instrumentation/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/client_hook.go (v1) if the functions are called with nil client options.

When mongo.Connect or mongo.NewClient is invoked with explicit nil client options (e.g. mongo.Connect(ctx, nil)), the compile-time hooks intercept these options. Because the slice loop doesn't check if the option struct itself is nil, evaluating opt.Monitor == nil results in a panic, crashing the user's application at startup.

### Environment

 - OS: Any (platform-independent)
 - Go Version:  1.25.0
 - Version: [main / latest otelc

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Instrument an application using `go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo` (v1).
2. Call `mongo.Connect(ctx, nil)` or `mongo.NewClient(nil)`.
3. Run the instrumented application.
4. See runtime panic:
   ```text
   panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

### Expected behavior

The client hooks should check if each option is nil and skip processing it, preventing any runtime panic

### Additional context

While the v2 MongoDB instrumentation (instrumentation/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/mongo) correctly performs this check:

go
if opt == nil {
    continue
}
The v1 package is currently missing this protection.

items.title: chore(test): add multi-process e2e for gRPC→SQL propagation
items.body:
## Summary

Per [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md), E2E tests spin up **multiple instrumented processes** and assert they form one coherent trace (shared trace ID).

`test/apps/grpcserverdbclient` is documented as a combined gRPC server + SQL client app **for e2e testing**, but today it is only exercised by an **integration** test:

- File: `test/integration/grpcserver_dbclient_test.go`
- The request is made with an in-test (uninstrumented) gRPC client via `grpc.NewClient`
- Asserts 1 trace with 2 spans: gRPC server → SQL client (in-process parent/child)

That does **not** verify cross-process propagation from an instrumented gRPC client into the gRPC→SQL chain.

Existing E2E coverage:

| E2E Test | File |
|---|---|
| HTTP client + server | `http_test.go` |
| gRPC client + server | `grpc_test.go` |
| Kafka producer + consumer | `kafka_test.go` |

items.title: bug(pkg): nil pointer dereference in kafka-go headerCarrier methods
items.body:
### Describe the bug

A nil pointer dereference panic occurs in `headerCarrier` methods (`Get`, `Set`, `Keys`) in both `instrumentation/github.com/segmentio/kafka-go/producer/producer_hook.go` and `instrumentation/github.com/segmentio/kafka-go/consumer/consumer_hook.go`.

When OpenTelemetry propagators (`propagator.Inject` or `propagator.Extract`) invoke methods on `headerCarrier`, if the `headers` slice pointer is nil (`headers == nil` or `*headers == nil`), dereferencing `*c.headers` causes a runtime panic:
`panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`

### Environment

 - OS: Any (platform-independent)
 - Go Version: 1.25.0
 - Version: main / latest otelc

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Instrument an application using `github.com/segmentio/kafka-go`.
2. Produce or consume a message with an uninitialized header carrier (`headerCarrier{headers: nil}`).
3. Call `propagator.Inject` or `propagator.Extract`.
4. See error: `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`

### Expected behavior

`headerCarrier.Get` should return `""`, `Set` should safely no-op, and `Keys` should return `nil` when the underlying headers pointer is nil.

### Additional context

Adding guard checks `if c.headers == nil || *c.headers == nil` across `Get`, `Set`, and `Keys` prevents panics during trace context injection and extraction.

items.title: bug(tool/internal/ast): typename.matches panics via util.Unimplemented on slice, map, chan, and func AST nodes
items.body:
### Description
In `tool/internal/ast/typename.go`, `parsedTypeName.matches` evaluates a `dst.Expr` node to check if it matches a target type string. When encountering composite type AST nodes not explicitly handled in the `switch` statement—such as `*dst.ArrayType` (e.g. `[]byte`), `*dst.MapType`, `*dst.ChanType`, or `*dst.FuncType`—the function executes the `default:` branch and calls `util.Unimplemented(...)`.

`util.Unimplemented` triggers `ex.Fatalf(...)` which panics and terminates the process immediately. As a result, running `otelc` on functions with slice, map, channel, or callback parameters causes `otelc` to crash during compilation.

### Expected Behavior
`typename.matches` should return `false` when an AST type expression does not match the target type, without panicking or aborting compilation.

### Proposed Fix
Modify the `default` case in `typename.matches` to return `false` gracefully:

```go
default:
    // Unsupported AST node types (chan, func, map, slice, array, etc.) cannot match simple type-name filters.
    return false

items.title: bug(ci): required unit and E2E checks ignore coverage job failures
items.body:
### Description

The required `Done (Unit Tests)` and `Done (E2E Tests)` jobs depend on their respective coverage jobs, but only inspect the platform test matrix result.

For example, `Done (Unit Tests)` declares:

```yaml
needs: [changes, test-unit-coverage, test-unit]
but checks only:
result="${{ needs.test-unit.result }}"
The E2E workflow follows the same pattern. As a result, an execution failure in a coverage job can leave the required aggregate check green when the platform tests pass.
This includes failures while:
- running make test-unit/coverage or make test-e2e/coverage;
- setting up the coverage job;
- uploading coverage results.
The Integration workflow already handles this correctly by checking change detection, the coverage job, and the platform matrix result.
Expected behavior
The Unit and E2E aggregate checks should:
- fail if change detection fails;
- succeed when no relevant code changed and test jobs were intentionally skipped;
- require both the coverage job and platform matrix to succeed when relevant code changed;
- fail on missing or unexpected change-detection output.
This should follow the existing Done (Integration Tests) implementation.
Scope
Update:
- .github/workflows/test-unit.yaml
- .github/workflows/test-e2e.yaml
This change should not make the informational 70% Codecov threshold blocking. It should only propagate actual coverage-job execution failures to the required aggregate checks.

items.title: chore(instrumentation/openai): de-duplicate v1/v2/v3 streaming reader logic
items.body:
## Context

The OpenAI GenAI streaming instrumentation (`streamingReader` and its helpers) is triplicated verbatim across the three supported module versions:

- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/streaming.go`
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v2/streaming.go`
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v3/streaming.go`

The three files (and their `streaming_test.go` counterparts) are identical except for the `package` declaration and the `semconv` import path. This predates [PR #828](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pull/828), which fixed a final-chunk-dropped bug (#827) by adding a `flushRemaining()` method plus two regression tests — and had to hand-apply that same change three times to keep the copies in sync.

## Problem

Every future bug fix or behavior change to the streaming reader has to be manually copy-pasted three times, with nothing enforcing that the copies stay identical. That's easy to get wrong (e.g. forgetting the `v3` copy) and adds reviewer overhead re-verifying three near-identical diffs.

## Suggestion

Investigate extracting the shared `streamingReader` logic (buffering, SSE line parsing, chunk processing) into a common internal package that the v1/v2/v3 packages import, with only the version-specific `semconv` glue left in each version's own package. If the semconv APIs differ enough across versions to make a shared package impractical, consider generating the three copies from a single source (e.g. via `go generate`) instead of hand-maintaining three copies.

## References

- Introduced pattern discussion: review of PR #828
- Related bug affected by this duplication: #827
items.author: darccio

items.title: test(e2e): tighten cross-process span-flush budget and evaluate parallelizing E2E tests
items.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from the review of #948. Three related E2E test-infra items around timing and
serialization that are worth tackling together, since fixing one changes the risk profile
of the others.

## 1. `WaitForSpans` cross-process flush budget may be too tight

[`test/testutil/readiness.go:14-19`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/main/test/testutil/readiness.go#L14-L19):

```go
const (
	defaultReadinessTimeout  = 10 * time.Second
	defaultReadinessInterval = 100 * time.Millisecond
	defaultSpanPollTimeout   = 3 * time.Second
	defaultSpanPollInterval  = 25 * time.Millisecond
)
```

`WaitForSpans` gives only 3 seconds to observe the last span after the client process has
already exited — this is the window in which the *server's* span (which outlives the
client call) must still flush to the collector. Readiness (`WaitForTCP`) gets a 10s
budget; span flush gets less than a third of that, even though it runs after two full
process builds + spawns, on runners that can be noticeably slower under load (the gRPC↔SQL
E2E test in #948 took 96s wall-clock on `windows-latest` vs 37s on `ubuntu-22.04-arm`).

The failure mode is a hard `t.Fatalf` with no retry
([readiness.go:35-40](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/main/test/testutil/readiness.go#L35-L40)) — a slow/contended runner turns into a
flaky failure, not a slow-but-passing test. This budget is shared by every E2E test using
`WaitForSpans`, so a fix benefits all of them.

**Possible direction:** raise `defaultSpanPollTimeout` (e.g. to match or approach
`defaultReadinessTimeout`), or scale it with the number of processes/spans involved.

## 2. No `t.Parallel()` in any E2E test

None of `test/e2e/grpc_test.go`, `http_test.go`, `kafka_test.go`, `httpserver_dbclient_test.go`
(and the pending `grpcserver_dbclient_test.go` from #948) call `t.Parallel()`. By contrast,
`test/integration/grpcserver_dbclient_test.go:22` does.

`TestFixture` is explicitly documented as parallel-safe —
[`fixture.go:52-55`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/main/test/testutil/fixture.go#L52-L55) says its env is "fixture-local... safe for use
under `t.Parallel()`" — and `FreePort` allocates a fresh port per test, so nothing
structurally blocks it. E2E tests are the most expensive category (full process builds +
spawns), so serializing them costs the most wall-clock of any suite, and it gets worse with
every new E2E test added.

**Caveat:** each E2E test builds 1-2 apps via `go build -a` — running them in parallel
multiplies concurrent CPU/memory pressure and could destabilize timing-sensitive
assertions like #1 above. This is why the two are grouped together: enabling parallelism
and tightening the span-wait budget should be measured together, not landed independently.

## 3. `FreePort`'s close/rebind race is accepted but undefended

[`test/testutil/readiness.go:54-64`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/main/test/testutil/readiness.go#L54-L64):

```go
// FreePort returns a port the OS just assigned for "localhost:0". The
// listener is closed before returning, so the test app can bind to it.
// There is a tiny race window between close and rebind; acceptable for CI.
func FreePort(t *testing.T) int { ... }
```

Already documented and explicitly accepted as a CI tradeoff — not a bug on its own. Only
worth revisiting if #2 goes forward, since running E2E tests in parallel multiplies the
number of concurrent close-then-rebind windows and could turn a "tiny" race into a more
frequent one.

## Suggested approach

Investigate and land together:
1. Measure current E2E wall-clock per test/platform as a baseline.
2. Raise (or make adaptive) `defaultSpanPollTimeout`.
3. Opt E2E tests into `t.Parallel()` incrementally, watching for regressions tied to #1/#3.
4. Only harden `FreePort` further if parallelism actually surfaces rebind flakes.

Not a blocker for #948 — filed as follow-up work.

items.title: test(e2e): assert client span is the trace root in dbclient propagation tests
items.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from the review of #948. Neither multi-process dbclient E2E test asserts that
the initiating client span is actually the **root** of its trace.

## Where

- Merged: [`test/e2e/httpserver_dbclient_test.go:52-60`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/main/test/e2e/httpserver_dbclient_test.go#L52-L60) (landed via #931)
- Pending: `test/e2e/grpcserver_dbclient_test.go:48-60` in #948

Both assert the full parent chain server→sql and client→server:

```go
require.Equal(t, httpClientSpan.TraceID(), httpServerSpan.TraceID(), "...")
require.Equal(t, httpServerSpan.TraceID(), sqlClientSpan.TraceID(), "...")
require.Equal(t, httpClientSpan.SpanID(), httpServerSpan.ParentSpanID(), "...")
require.Equal(t, httpServerSpan.SpanID(), sqlClientSpan.ParentSpanID(), "...")
```

...but neither asserts `httpClientSpan.ParentSpanID()` / `grpcClientSpan.ParentSpanID()`
is empty/all-zero — i.e. that the client span that kicks off the whole chain has no
parent of its own.

## Why it's low risk today

Both tests already call `RequireTraceCount(1)` + `RequireSpansPerTrace(3)` before
selecting spans, which constrains the trace to exactly 3 spans — there's no fourth span
the client span could secretly be parented under. So this is one assertion short of a
*fully* closed chain, not a real gap in today's test topology.

## Why still worth doing

It's cheap insurance (one more `require.Equal` against an empty span ID) against a future
regression where an ambient/leaked parent context makes the trace-count check pass for the
wrong reason — and it directly completes the propagation-chain assertion these tests are
explicitly about.

## Suggested fix

Add to both files, right after the existing parent/child assertions:

```go
require.True(t, httpClientSpan.ParentSpanID().IsEmpty(), "HTTP client span must be the trace root")
```

(and the gRPC equivalent for `grpcClientSpan` in #948's file, ideally before it merges).

Two files, no coupling to other follow-ups from this review.

items.title: test(apps/grpcserverdbclient): bind gRPC frontend to loopback instead of all interfaces
items.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from the review of #948. `test/apps/grpcserverdbclient` binds its gRPC
frontend to all interfaces instead of loopback.

## Where

[`test/apps/grpcserverdbclient/main.go:24,50`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/blob/main/test/apps/grpcserverdbclient/main.go#L50):

```go
var frontPort = flag.Int("front-port", 50051, "port for gRPC frontend")
...
lis, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf(":%d", *frontPort))
```

Every caller — the integration test and the E2E tests (merged and pending in #948) —
dials `127.0.0.1:<port>`. The server itself listens on `:<port>`, i.e. all interfaces,
for no reason tied to the test's actual usage.

## Why it matters

Low severity — this is an ephemeral, short-lived CI process on a random port — but it's
an easy one-line hardening to match how the app is actually addressed, and it removes
unnecessary network exposure during CI runs.

## Suggested fix

```go
lis, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", *frontPort))
```

One file, one line, no coupling to other follow-ups from this review.

items.title: bug(instrumentation): openai-go middlewares emit full HTTP status line as error.type instead of numeric code
items.body:
## Description

Per the [OTel HTTP semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/http/http-spans/), when an HTTP response is received with an error status (4xx/5xx), `error.type` SHOULD be set to the numeric status code as a string (e.g. `"429"`) — it's meant to be a low-cardinality error class, not the full status line.

The OpenAI instrumentation currently sets it to the full status line (e.g. `"429 Too Many Requests"`), which breaks metric/trace grouping in backends that key on `error.type`:

- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/middleware.go:175`
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v2/middleware.go:175`
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v3/middleware.go:175`

```go
span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("error.type", resp.Status))
```

## Related

This is the same defect fixed for the Anthropic instrumentation in #772. That PR's fix uses `strconv.Itoa(resp.StatusCode)`. Two other instrumentations in this repo already emit `error.type` this way via the official `semconv.ErrorTypeKey` (`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.37.0`) rather than a raw `attribute.String` or a locally-defined key:

- `instrumentation/net/http/semconv/server.go:270`
- `instrumentation/github.com/linode/linodego/v2/semconv/client.go:129`

## Suggested fix

In each of the three files, replace:
```go
span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("error.type", resp.Status))
```
with:
```go
span.SetAttributes(semconv.ErrorTypeKey.String(strconv.Itoa(resp.StatusCode)))
```
importing `semconv "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.37.0"` (aliased if it collides with a local `semconv` package import).

items.title: feat(genai): record span errors and finish_reasons on premature SSE stream aborts
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Hey, while testing the `openai-go` middleware from #740, I noticed a telemetry gap in how we handle abnormal stream terminations in `streamingReader`.

Currently, if an SSE stream drops mid-generation due to a network timeout (`Read` returns a non-EOF error) or client cancellation (`Close` is called before `[DONE]`), the `finalize` logic is triggered. However, `finalize` simply calls `r.span.End()` without ever recording the error or setting the span status to `codes.Error`. 

To the OTel backend, a network crash halfway through a GenAI stream looks like a perfectly successful 200 OK trace, just with a lower token count. We are silently swallowing telemetry failures for aborted streams.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to update `streamingReader` to properly detect and record abnormal terminations:
1. **In `Read()` and `Close()`:** Pass the terminating `error` (if any) to `finalize()`.
2. **In `finalize()`:** If the stream was aborted prematurely (e.g., `[DONE]` was never parsed), automatically call `r.span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "stream aborted")`.
3. **Semantic Fallback:** If the connection dropped before we received the final chunk, inject `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons = ["error"]` to align with the GenAI semantic conventions for failed generations.
4. **Error Recording:** Call `r.span.RecordError(err)` if a specific network/context error triggered the teardown.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Relying on HTTP status codes. But since SSE streams usually return a `200 OK` header phase before the streaming chunk loop begins, standard HTTP instrumentation can't detect a teardown that happens 30 seconds later during the body read. The error state must be managed by the chunk reader.

**Additional context**
Ran into this while mapping out the state-machine requirements for the `genai.Observer` architecture (ADR 0007). I'm happy to push a targeted PR to patch this in the OpenAI instrumentation now, or bundle it into the upcoming mentorship timeline as a broader safety net for the generic adapter. Let me know what fits the roadmap best!

items.title: bug(tool/internal/setup): sort moduleDirs in resolveRulePaths for deterministic package resolution
items.body:
### Description
`resolveRulePaths` in `tool/internal/setup/store.go` iterates over `moduleDirs map[string]bool` directly using `for moduleDir := range moduleDirs`.

Because Go map iteration order is randomized by design, package resolution attempts across candidate module directories occur in arbitrary order. If a package import path exists or resolves differently across multiple candidate module directories, the resolution result or error returned depends on random map order. This introduces non-reproducible build behavior and non-deterministic build artifacts.

### Proposed Solution
Collect and sort the keys of `moduleDirs` using `slices.Sort` prior to iteration to guarantee deterministic path resolution across runs.

### Location
- `tool/internal/setup/store.go:31`

items.title: Our issue and PR intake does not scale
items.body:
We've started feeling the backlog, let's start discussing ideas. All ideas are welcome.

## The numbers (2026-08-05)

- 72 open issues, 52 open PRs.
- July alone: 85 issues and 193 PRs. June was 15 and 52.
- 38% of open issues carry no label at all.
- 84% of issues opened since June 1 have a PR from the same author within 48 hours (112 of 133).
- 1 issue in this repo's entire history has ever been closed as a duplicate.

## How I read this

- Issues are not a backlog/roadmap we work from.
- Duplicates may not be where the cost is.
- Review capacity is the constraint, not contributor supply.

## Root problems, as I see them

1. **Nothing validates work before it is written.** CONTRIBUTING does not ask for an accepted issue before a PR, and does not define how work is claimed. Contributors are behaving exactly as our process rewards them to, and it would be unfair to frame this as their fault.
2. **We cannot slice the backlog.** There is no component axis in our labels, so "what is already open on kafka?" has no answer.
3. **We have no way to say no early.** By the time we can tell that work is not wanted, someone has already spent their evening on it and we have already spent a review.

feat(genai): record span errors and finish_reasons on premature SSE stream aborts

Fixes #970

Aborted OpenAI streaming responses (mid-stream network errors, client
cancellation before `[DONE]`) previously ended the span as a successful 200
with no error recorded. `streamingReader` now tracks stream completion
(finish_reason or `[DONE]` parsed) and, when a stream is torn down before
completion, marks the span errored with description `"stream aborted"`,
records the terminating error as an exception event, and emits
`finish_reasons=["error"]` to align with GenAI semantic conventions.

Design note: completion is defined as a parsed finish_reason OR the `[DONE]`
marker, not `[DONE]` alone — a caller that stops reading after the final
chunk (or a connection closed right after the last chunk) must not be
flagged as an error. The existing `CloseWithoutDrainingFlushesFinalChunk`
and `FinalChunkWithoutTrailingNewline` tests pin this behavior, and
`Close` still flushes the line buffer so the final chunk's attributes are
never lost.

Tests added:
- `TestStreamingReader_AbortOnReadError`
- `TestStreamingReader_AbortOnCloseBeforeCompletion`
- `TestStreamingReader_CloseAfterFinishReasonIsNormal`

All existing `TestStreamingReader_*` tests continue to pass.

Today, all built-in instrumentations under `instrumentation/**` (26 packages: `net/http`, `database/sql`, `google.golang.org/grpc`, `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9`, etc.) plus the shared runtime support library `pkg/` are tarred into `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz`, embedded into the `otelc` binary via `//go:embed`, and extracted to a temp dir every time `otelc` runs. `otelc pin`'s auto-discovery (`generatePinnedProjects` in `tool/internal/setup/pin.go`) extracts this bundle purely to learn "which built-in instrumentation targets which import path, at which version range, and which module path provides it" — via `loadMinimalRules`/`loadModuleRules` (`tool/internal/setup/pin.go` lines ~169-238), which walks the extracted `instrumentation/` tree, finds each nested `go.mod`, and parses each rule file's `target`/`version` fields.

This issue is step 1 of decoupling: introduce a small, git-friendly **manifest** that captures exactly this metadata (and nothing else — no source code) without changing any runtime behavior yet.

## Scope

Add a new manifest package and generator, **unwired** — `otelc pin` continues using the old bundle-extraction path until #981 lands. This PR should be a pure addition, safe to review in isolation.

### Tasks

- [ ] Add `tool/internal/manifest/manifest.go`:
  - `type Entry struct { ModulePath, Target, VersionRange string }`
  - `type Manifest []Entry`
  - `func Generate(instrumentationRoot string) (Manifest, error)` — port of the existing `loadMinimalRules`/`loadModuleRules` walk logic (`tool/internal/setup/pin.go` ~169-238): walk `instrumentationRoot`, find nested `go.mod` files, parse each nested module's rule files (`otelc.yml`/`otelc.yaml`/`*.otelc.yml`/`*.otelc.yaml`, matched via the existing `isRuleFile()` helper in `tool/internal/setup/match.go`), extract `target`+`version` per rule. Unlike today's runtime version, this walks the **real** `instrumentation/` directory directly — no copying to a `*_temp` dir, no `go mod tidy`.
  - `func Load() (Manifest, error)` — parses the embedded JSON produced by the generator below.
  - Sort entries deterministically by `(ModulePath, Target)` before serialization for stable, minimal diffs.
- [ ] Add `tool/cmd/gen-manifest/main.go` — a dev/release-time-only CLI that calls `manifest.Generate("instrumentation")`, marshals to indented JSON, and writes `tool/data/instrumentation-manifest.json`.
- [ ] Add `tool/data/manifest.go`:
  ```go
  //go:embed instrumentation-manifest.json
  var manifestJSON []byte
  func GetManifestJSON() []byte { return manifestJSON }
  ```
  This coexists with the existing `tool/data/export.go` (`//go:embed otelc-bundle.tgz`) for now — do **not** remove the old bundle embed in this PR, that happens in #981.
- [ ] Generate and commit `tool/data/instrumentation-manifest.json` from the current `instrumentation/` tree (run `gen-manifest` once).
- [ ] Add a `make manifest` Makefile target invoking `gen-manifest`.
- [ ] Add a `verify-manifest` CI check (workflow or script) that runs `go run ./tool/cmd/gen-manifest && git diff --exit-code tool/data/instrumentation-manifest.json` to catch a forgotten regeneration. This is cheap (no `go mod tidy`, no temp dirs) — no PR-comment regenerate-bot is needed.
- [ ] Move `TestLoadMinimalRules_*` (currently in `tool/internal/setup/pin_test.go`) to `tool/internal/manifest/manifest_test.go`, adapted to call `manifest.Generate` directly. Add a round-trip test: `Generate` → marshal → `Load`/unmarshal → equal.

## Out of scope

- Wiring this manifest into `otelc pin`'s actual discovery logic (#981).
- Removing `otelc-bundle.tgz`, `tool/data/export.go`, `.tools/bundle/`, or any bundle-sync CI (#981).
- Any change to `sync.go`'s `replace`-injection behavior (#983).

## Acceptance criteria

- `make manifest` regenerates `tool/data/instrumentation-manifest.json` byte-for-byte identical to the committed version (idempotent).
- `go test ./tool/internal/manifest/...` passes.
- No observable behavior change in `otelc` — it still uses the old bundle-extraction path for auto-pin discovery.

items.title: feat(tool): use instrumentation manifest for pin discovery, remove otelc-bundle.tgz [2/6]
items.body:
# feat(tool): use instrumentation manifest for pin discovery, remove `otelc-bundle.tgz` [2/6]

**Tracking:** part of #585 (decouple built-in instrumentations from `otelc-bundle.tgz`)
**Depends on:** #980
**Blocks:** #983 (should land together with, or before, #983 — see note below)

## Background

`otelc` currently embeds all built-in instrumentation source (`instrumentation/**`, 26 packages) and the shared runtime library (`pkg/`) into the binary as `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz` via `//go:embed` in `tool/data/export.go`, extracted at runtime by `tool/internal/setup/extract.go`'s `extractOtelcBundle()`. `otelc pin`'s `generatePinnedProjects()` (`tool/internal/setup/pin.go` lines ~448-511) calls `extractOtelcBundle()` + `loadMinimalRules()` purely to learn which built-in instrumentation modules exist and what they target, in order to decide which blank imports to add to a freshly-generated `otel.instrumentation.go`.

#980 introduced `tool/internal/manifest`, a small JSON manifest holding exactly this metadata (`{modulePath, target, versionRange}` per built-in instrumentation), generated from the real `instrumentation/` tree instead of requiring full source to be embedded — but left it unwired. This issue wires it in and removes the now-redundant bundle machinery.

Everything else in the setup/matching pipeline — `resolveInstrumentationConfigs()` in `tool/internal/setup/config.go`, rule-file discovery in `tool/internal/setup/match.go`, AST-based weaving — already resolves instrumentation packages generically via real Go module mechanics (`golang.org/x/tools/go/packages`) and needs **no changes**; it already works identically for built-in and third-party packages once an import exists in `otel.instrumentation.go`.

## Scope

### Tasks

- [ ] In `tool/internal/setup/pin.go` `generatePinnedProjects()` (~lines 448-511): replace the `extractOtelcBundle()` + `loadMinimalRules(...)` call with `manifest.Load()`. Adjust `matchInstrumentationImports()` (~line 309+) to consume `manifest.Manifest`/`manifest.Entry` instead of the local `yamlRule` type — the matching logic itself (exact/glob target match, root-target always-match, `util.VersionInRange`) does not need to change.
- [ ] Delete `tool/internal/setup/extract.go` and `tool/internal/setup/extract_test.go`. `extractOtelcBundle()` has exactly one call site (in `pin.go`), so this is safe to remove wholesale.
- [ ] Delete `tool/data/export.go`, `tool/data/export_test.go`, and `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz`.
- [ ] Delete `.tools/bundle/` (`main.go` + `go.mod`) — the bundling tool.
- [ ] In the `Makefile`: remove the `package` target, `INST_BUNDLE_*` variables, and `check-embed` target. Update `build`, `install`, and `build-all` targets to depend on `manifest` (added in #980) instead of `package`.
- [ ] Delete `.github/workflows/verify-bundle.yaml` and `.github/workflows/regenerate-bundle.yaml`.
- [ ] Delete `.github/scripts/verify-bundle.sh` and `.github/scripts/merge-bundle.sh`.
- [ ] Remove the `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz` merge-driver line from `.gitattributes`, and remove the `make setup-git` target (it only existed to register that merge driver).
- [ ] Remove leftover `pkgTempDir`/`instTempDir`/`unzippedPkgDir`/`unzippedInstDir` constants if now unused after `extract.go` is deleted.

### Important sequencing note

After this PR, `tool/internal/setup/sync.go`'s `replace`-injection block (lines ~135-157) **still runs unchanged** — it still tries to redirect built-in module paths to `filepath.Join(util.GetBuildTempDir(), unzippedInstDir, ...)`, a directory that no longer gets populated since the bundle is gone. This will break builds that match a built-in instrumentation.

Two options, pick one before merging:
- **(a) Land this together with #983** (which removes the `replace`-injection entirely and replaces it with explicit version-pinned `require` lines) as a single combined PR, avoiding any broken intermediate state.
- **(b) Land independently**, temporarily changing the `replace` targets in `sync.go` to point directly at the real `pkg/`/`instrumentation/` source checkout paths (instead of an extracted-bundle temp dir) as a deliberate stepping stone, to be removed in #983.

Recommendation: (a), unless the maintainers prefer smaller diffs over a clean working state at every commit.

## Out of scope

- Removing the `replace`-injection mechanism itself, or adding explicit version pinning (#983) — unless combined per the note above.
- Any test-infrastructure changes for `test/apps/*` fixtures (#982).
- Release/tagging automation (#984).
- Docs wording updates (#985).

## Acceptance criteria

- No `//go:embed otelc-bundle.tgz` or references to `otelc-bundle.tgz` remain anywhere in the codebase.
- `otelc pin` (combined with #982/#983 as scoped above) still successfully auto-generates `otel.instrumentation.go` for an app depending on a built-in-instrumented library (e.g. `net/http`).
- `make build`/`make install` succeed without the `package` target.

items.title: test(tool): resolve built-in instrumentation via go.work in tests instead of bundle extraction [3/6]
items.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This is part of an on-going discussion. Don't go ahead and implement it. Each issue will be assigned to an owner after each proposal is approved by the maintainers and only the owner will implement the functionality in one or more PRs.

# test(tool): resolve built-in instrumentation via `go.work` in tests instead of bundle extraction [3/6]

**Tracking:** part of #585 (decouple built-in instrumentations from `otelc-bundle.tgz`)
**Depends on:** none directly (can be implemented independently)
**Blocks:** #983 — must land before or alongside it, or CI breaks

## Background

`otelc` is a Go compile-time instrumentation tool. Its repo is a multi-module monorepo: `pkg/`, `pkg/runtime/`, `instrumentation/` (shared anchor module), and 26 nested packages under `instrumentation/**` (e.g. `instrumentation/net/http/client`) each have their own `go.mod`, declaring module paths like `go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/instrumentation/net/http/client`.

Today, `otelc pin`'s `syncDeps()` (`tool/internal/setup/sync.go` lines ~135-157) unconditionally injects `replace` directives into whichever `go.mod` it's operating on, redirecting every built-in instrumentation/`pkg` module path to a locally-extracted copy of `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz`. This is how the repo's own test fixtures under `test/apps/*/` — which are checked into git **with no `require` or `replace` lines at all** — resolve built-in instrumentation modules during `test-integration`, `test-e2e`, `test-latestlibbuild`, `test-latestlibrun`, and `test-versionmatrix` runs: `AutoPin` runs, redirects kick in, the build succeeds locally, and `AutoPin` reverts the generated files afterward.

#585's broader plan removes this `replace`-injection (see #983) so that real users get real, independently-versioned instrumentation modules. But doing that with **no other change** would break every one of the repo's own tests: `go mod tidy` on a `test/apps/*` fixture would try to fetch built-in instrumentation modules from the real module proxy, resolving whatever was last **published** — not the code under test in the current branch/PR — and would require network access in CI for something that should be a pure local build.

## Scope

Fix this with Go's native multi-module workspace support (`go.work`), not with any `otelc`-side special-casing. The repo already has an unused `make go-work` Makefile target (backed by `crosslink`) and `tool/internal/pkgload/pkgload.go` already shells out to `go env GOMOD GOWORK` (confirmed workspace-aware) — `go build`/`go mod tidy` invoked by `otelc`'s `syncDeps`/`runModTidy` will pick up `GOWORK` automatically from the working directory with zero code changes in `otelc` itself.

### Tasks

- [ ] Extend the existing `make go-work` target to generate a `go.work` file at the repo root that `use`s:
  - `pkg`, `pkg/runtime`
  - `instrumentation` (the shared anchor module)
  - all ~26 nested modules under `instrumentation/**`
  - every module under `test/apps/*`
- [ ] Wire `make go-work` as a prerequisite of the `test-unit/tool`, `test-integration`, `test-e2e`, `test-latestlibbuild`, `test-latestlibrun`, and `test-versionmatrix` Makefile targets, in place of their current dependency on `package` (the bundle-build target being removed in #981).
- [ ] Update the corresponding CI workflow YAML files (`.github/workflows/test-unit.yaml`, `test-integration.yaml`, `test-e2e.yaml`, `test-latestlibbuild.yaml`, `test-latestlibrun.yaml`, `test-versionmatrix.yaml`) if any of them invoke `make package` or rely on the bundle explicitly rather than going through the Makefile dependency graph.
- [ ] Confirm `go.work` / `go.work.sum` remain gitignored (they already are) so this stays a pure dev/CI concern and never affects what's shipped to end users or how a real user's build resolves dependencies.
- [ ] Run the full test suite locally with only `make go-work` + the relevant `test-*` target (no bundle, no `replace`-injection) to validate the workspace correctly resolves all built-in instrumentation and `pkg` imports to local source.

## Out of scope

- Removing the `replace`-injection mechanism itself (#983) — this issue only ensures tests don't depend on it.
- Any change to how a real (non-monorepo) user's build resolves instrumentation versions.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `otelc-bundle.tgz` and its extraction machinery already removed (post #981) and the `replace`-injection removed (post #983), `make go-work && make test-integration` (and the other affected test targets) pass without any network access beyond what's already required for non-monorepo dependencies (e.g. `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` itself).
- CI workflows for the affected test targets pass green on a PR that also includes #983's changes.

items.title: feat(tool): pin real instrumentation module versions instead of local bundle replace [4/6]
items.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This is part of an on-going discussion. Don't go ahead and implement it. Each issue will be assigned to an owner after each proposal is approved by the maintainers and only the owner will implement the functionality in one or more PRs.

# feat(tool): pin real instrumentation module versions instead of local bundle `replace` [4/6]

**Tracking:** part of #585 (decouple built-in instrumentations from `otelc-bundle.tgz`) — this is the semantic core of the issue
**Depends on:** #981, #982
**Blocks:** none directly (but #984's value only materializes after this lands)

## Background

This is the change that actually decouples instrumentation versions from the `otelc` tool version — everything in #980/#981/#982 is groundwork for this.

`tool/internal/setup/sync.go`'s `syncDeps()` (lines ~120-194) currently contains this, at lines ~135-157:

```go
// Add replace directives for modules imported to otel.instrumentation.go
replaces := make(map[string]string, len(modPaths))
for m := range modPaths {
    if path, isEmbedded := strings.CutPrefix(m, util.OtelcInstRoot+"/"); isEmbedded {
        replaces[m] = filepath.Join(util.GetBuildTempDir(), unzippedInstDir, path)
    }
}

// Add replace directive for special pkg module
// TODO: Since we haven't published the instrumentation packages yet,
// we need to add the replace directive to the local path.
// Once the instrumentation packages are published, we can remove this.
replaces[util.OtelcPkgRoot] = filepath.Join(util.GetBuildTempDir(), unzippedPkgDir)
replaces[util.OtelcPkgRoot+"/runtime"] = filepath.Join(util.GetBuildTempDir(), unzippedPkgDir, "runtime")
replaces[util.OtelcInstRoot] = filepath.Join(util.GetBuildTempDir(), unzippedInstDir)
```

This unconditionally rewrites the **user's own `go.mod`** to redirect every built-in instrumentation module, `pkg`, `pkg/runtime`, and the shared `instrumentation` anchor module to a local, bundle-extracted copy — which is precisely why instrumentation versions can't be independently pinned today: no matter what a user's `go.mod` says, the tool silently overrides it with a `replace` pointing at whatever source shipped inside the running `otelc` binary. The maintainers' own TODO comment above already flags this as the thing to remove once instrumentation packages are independently resolvable (which #981 + #982 make true).

There is one real coupling risk to account for when removing this: `tool/internal/instrument/apply_func.go` embeds `api.tmpl` (via `//go:embed`), a snapshot of the `HookContext` interface shape copied from `pkg/hook/context.go` at `otelc`'s **own** build time (via the Makefile's `API_SYNC_SOURCE`/`API_SYNC_TARGET` variables and `make check-api-sync`). Generated hook/trampoline code assumes this exact shape. If a user's build resolves a `pkg`/`pkg/hook` version whose `HookContext` shape has drifted from what the running `otelc` binary's `api.tmpl` expects, generated code can mismatch. The fix is to pin `pkg`'s required version explicitly to the running tool's version, not to leave it to bare `go mod tidy` resolution.

## Scope

### Tasks

- [ ] Delete the `replace`-injection block in `tool/internal/setup/sync.go` (~lines 135-157) in full, including the TODO comment. Remove the `addReplace` helper (~lines 50-66) if it has no remaining call sites after this — check first.
- [ ] Generalize `ensureOtelcRequireVersion(f *modfile.File, version string)` (`tool/internal/setup/pin.go` ~lines 240-261, currently hardcoded to `util.OtelcRoot`) into `ensureRequireVersion(f *modfile.File, modPath, version string) (bool, error)`. Keep a thin wrapper calling it with `util.OtelcRoot` for the existing call site in `ensureOtelcRequire` (~lines 263-307) to avoid unrelated churn. Preserve the existing safety guard exactly: skip pinning when `version` is invalid, `"v0.0.0"`, or a pseudo-version (this is what lets local/dev/pre-release builds — where `util.Version` isn't a real tag — fall back to ordinary `go mod tidy` resolution inside the `go.work` workspace from #982, without any special-casing).
- [ ] In `generatePinnedProjects()` (`tool/internal/setup/pin.go` ~lines 448-511), after computing the matched `imports` set, call `ensureRequireVersion(..., util.Version)` for each of:
  - `util.OtelcPkgRoot` (`go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/pkg`)
  - `util.OtelcPkgRoot + "/runtime"`
  - `util.OtelcInstRoot` (`go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/instrumentation` — the shared anchor module; it holds real cross-instrumentation semconv helper packages with no `go.mod` of their own, imported by several nested instrumentation submodules, so it must be pinned too, not just the matched leaf modules)
  - every key in `imports` that carries the `util.OtelcInstRoot + "/"` prefix (i.e. each matched built-in instrumentation submodule)

  Then proceed with the existing `go mod tidy` step as before.
- [ ] Delete `TestSyncDeps_WithMods` and `TestSyncDeps_ExistingReplace` (and the shared `setupSyncDepsTest` helper, if now dead) in `tool/internal/setup/sync_test.go`.
- [ ] Add tests for `ensureRequireVersion`, mirroring the existing `TestEnsureOtelcRequire` pattern in `pin_test.go` (~lines 312-439): adds a `require` line when absent, bumps the version when the running version is newer, no-ops when older/equal, and skips entirely when `util.Version` is invalid/pseudo/`v0.0.0`. Cover all four pinned module paths above.
- [ ] Rewrite `TestGeneratePinnedProjects` (`pin_test.go` ~lines 825-882) to seed a fake manifest (via a test seam / package-level override in `tool/internal/manifest`) instead of depending on the real committed `tool/data/instrumentation-manifest.json`, so the unit test is independent of the current instrumentation tree's contents.
- [ ] Add a `test/integration/pin_test.go` case: running `otelc pin` on a fresh app depending on e.g. `net/http` produces a `require go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/instrumentation/net/http/client vX.Y.Z` line and **no** `replace go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/...` line in the resulting `go.mod`. This test must run inside the `go.work` workspace set up in #982 (otherwise `go mod tidy` has no real local source to resolve to when `util.Version` is a dev/pseudo-version).
- [ ] Extend `test/e2e` (or `test/integration`) with a scenario proving a built-in instrumentation resolved via normal module fetch (not bundle extraction) is still correctly matched and woven — e.g. build `test/apps/httpclient` via `otelc go build` and assert the resulting binary actually emits a span.

## Known, pre-existing gap (explicitly out of scope here)

The same `HookContext`-shape coupling described above applies identically to **third-party** instrumentation packages using `inject_hooks` — and those are never version-pinned today either way (`syncDeps` is only reached from the auto-generate path, gated on at least one *built-in* match). This is a pre-existing gap, not introduced or worsened by this change. Worth flagging as a follow-up issue, not fixing here (scope creep risk).

## Out of scope

- Release/tagging automation to make the pinned versions resolvable to real tagged releases (#984) — this PR's pinning logic works correctly with `go.work`-resolved local versions in CI/dev regardless of whether real tags exist yet.
- Docs updates (#985).

## Acceptance criteria

- No `replace go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/...` directives are ever injected into a user's `go.mod` by `otelc pin`/`AutoPin`.
- A fresh `otelc pin` run against an app depending on a built-in-instrumented library produces explicit, version-pinned `require` lines for `pkg`, `pkg/runtime`, the `instrumentation` anchor module, and the matched instrumentation submodule(s).
- `otelc go build` against `test/apps/httpclient` (or equivalent) still produces a correctly instrumented binary end-to-end, running inside the `go.work` workspace from #982.

items.title: ci(release): tag pkg/ and instrumentation/** submodules on release [5/6]
items.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This is part of an on-going discussion. Don't go ahead and implement it. Each issue will be assigned to an owner after each proposal is approved by the maintainers and only the owner will implement the functionality in one or more PRs.

# ci(release): tag `pkg/` and `instrumentation/**` submodules on release [5/6]

**Tracking:** part of #585 (decouple built-in instrumentations from `otelc-bundle.tgz`)
**Depends on:** should land after #983 (its value only materializes once real version pinning exists), though the tagging logic itself can be implemented and dry-run tested independently
**Blocks:** none

## Background

`otelc` is a multi-module monorepo: alongside the root `go.opentelemetry.io/otelc` module, `pkg/`, `pkg/runtime/`, `instrumentation/` (shared anchor), and 26 nested packages under `instrumentation/**` each declare their own `go.mod` with correct module paths (e.g. `go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/instrumentation/net/http/client`). Because this is a public GitHub repo, Go's module proxy can already resolve these nested modules via automatic pseudo-versions derived from commits — but pseudo-versions aren't clean, human-meaningful releases, and there's currently no way to `go get` an explicitly older *tagged* version of a specific built-in instrumentation.

#983 makes `otelc pin` explicitly pin every built-in instrumentation module's `require` line to `util.Version` (the exact version of the running `otelc` binary). For that pin to resolve to something real and fetchable for actual end users (not just inside this repo's own `go.work`-based tests), the corresponding nested-module versions need to actually exist as tagged releases.

Today, `.github/workflows/release.yml` only tags and releases the root module: triggered on `v*.*.*` tag push, it runs `make build-all` and uploads binaries. No automation tags any nested module.

## Scope

Lockstep tagging only — every instrumentation/pkg module always shares the exact same version number as the root release tag for now. True independent release cadence (a maintainer tagging just `instrumentation/net/http/client` off-cycle from the tool) is **not** part of this issue; it's a natural follow-up once this mechanism exists and is closer in spirit to issue #849 (OpenTelemetry Registry-based discovery).

### Tasks

- [ ] Extend `.github/workflows/release.yml` (already checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`) to, after the existing `make build-all` + release-upload steps (or in a separate job), create and push nested version tags at the same commit as the root tag for every `go.mod` found under `pkg/**` and `instrumentation/**`:
  - `pkg/vX.Y.Z`
  - `pkg/runtime/vX.Y.Z`
  - `instrumentation/vX.Y.Z` (the shared anchor module)
  - `instrumentation/<path>/vX.Y.Z` for each of the ~26 nested instrumentation modules (e.g. `instrumentation/net/http/client/vX.Y.Z`, `instrumentation/database/sql/vX.Y.Z`, etc.)
- [ ] Derive the module list the same way the `Makefile`'s `ALL_GO_MOD_DIRS` variable already does (`find . -name go.mod`), filtered to paths under `pkg/` and `instrumentation/`, converting each directory path relative to the repo root into its corresponding nested-module tag prefix.
- [ ] Add a dry-run / `workflow_dispatch`-triggered mode that computes and logs the tag list without pushing, so the logic can be validated before it's wired into a real release.
- [ ] Ensure tag-push permissions are correctly scoped (the workflow already has `permissions: contents: write` for the release job).
- [ ] Briefly document the tagging scheme (lockstep versioning across the whole module tree) in whichever doc holds the release process (`RELEASE.md` or the relevant `CONTRIBUTING.md` section).

## Out of scope

- Independent per-module release cadence/versioning.
- Any change to `otelc pin`'s pinning logic itself (already done in #983) — this issue only makes the pinned versions resolvable.

## Acceptance criteria

- A dry-run of the extended release workflow produces the expected, complete list of nested tags for the current module tree.
- After a real tagged pre-release, `go get go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/instrumentation/net/http/client@vX.Y.Z` (run outside this repo, against the real module proxy) resolves successfully to that exact tagged version.
- `go get -tool go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/tool/cmd/otelc@vX.Y.Z` followed by `go tool otelc pin` on a fresh external app produces a working, correctly-pinned `go.mod` with no local monorepo context required.

items.title: docs: remove bundle-sync instructions, describe manifest-driven instrumentation versioning [6/6]
items.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This is part of an on-going discussion. Don't go ahead and implement it. Each issue will be assigned to an owner after each proposal is approved by the maintainers and only the owner will implement the functionality in one or more PRs.

# docs: remove bundle-sync instructions, describe manifest-driven instrumentation versioning [6/6]

**Tracking:** part of #585 (decouple built-in instrumentations from `otelc-bundle.tgz`)
**Depends on:** soft dependency on #981 and #983 for wording accuracy (this issue describes the post-change state) — can be drafted early, but should be merged after those land
**Blocks:** none

## Background

Prior to #585, contributors had to run a git merge driver setup step (`make setup-git`) and manually regenerate `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz` (`make package`) after every rebase touching `pkg/` or `instrumentation/`, documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s "Keeping the bundle in sync" section. Several docs pages also describe built-in instrumentation discovery in terms of an "embedded rule bundle."

Once #981 removes the bundle mechanism entirely (replaced by a small committed JSON manifest that merges/diffs like ordinary text, needing no custom merge driver) and #983 makes built-in instrumentation versions genuinely independently pinnable via `go.mod`, this documentation needs a pass to match reality and to explain the new, more flexible versioning model to users.

## Scope

### Tasks

- [ ] Remove the "Keeping the bundle in sync" section from `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the part describing `make package`, the git merge driver, and `git commit --amend` after every rebase).

items.title: stripCompleteFlag mutates caller's slice in place; WriteFile exits process on close error
items.body:
While reading through tool/ ahead of an LFX application, I found two small correctness issues:

1. **stripCompleteFlag** (tool/internal/instrument/toolexec.go, ~line 86-93)
Removes the -complete flag via append(args[:i], args[i+1:]...). This shifts the remaining elements left in the same backing array the input slice uses. Since the returned slice and the caller's original slice share that array, the caller's slice (e.g. ip.compileArgs) is silently modified even though it was never reassigned.

2. **WriteFile** (tool/util/sys.go, ~line 147-164)
Calls ex.Fatal(err) (which exits the process) inside the deferred file.Close() error check. A file-writing helper shouldn't unilaterally terminate the process on a close error — that should be returned to the caller to handle.

I have fixes and tests for both ready — will open a PR shortly.

items.title: test(testutil): harden FreePort against close/rebind race conditions
items.body:
Track recently allocated ports in a synchronized map to prevent parallel test runs from colliding on the same ephemeral port before the subprocess server binds to it.

<!--
Thank you for contributing to OpenTelemetry Go Compile Instrumentation!

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Fill in the description and motivation sections below
2. Complete the checklist before submitting
3. Ensure PR title follows conventional commits format (enforced by CI)

PR TITLE FORMAT (required):
  type(scope): description

  Types: chore, doc, docs, feat, fix, release, refactor, test
  Scopes: tool, pkg, demo, test, docs

  Examples:
  - feat(pkg): add gRPC client instrumentation
  - fix(tool): resolve hook signature matching issue
  - docs(api): update instrumenter interface documentation
  - refactor(pkg): simplify attribute extractor composition

BEFORE SUBMITTING:
  make format  # Format Go code and YAML files
  make lint    # Run all linters

If your PR adds a new user-facing instrumentation, please also submit a corresponding OpenTelemetry Registry PR:
https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/adding/

For detailed contribution guidelines, see CONTRIBUTING.md
For available make targets, run: make help
-->

## Description

This PR introduces a thread-safe registry to prevent concurrent test runs from colliding on duplicate port allocations:
* Adds a global `allocatedPorts` map guarded by `sync.Mutex` in `test/testutil/readiness.go`.
* Automatically sweeps/evicts registry entries older than 30 seconds to keep the memory footprint minimal.
* Hardens the `FreePort` helper to check incoming OS-assigned ephemeral ports against the registry. If a port was recently allocated (within the last 30 seconds), it discards it, sleeps briefly, and retries.

## Motivation

Now that E2E tests are parallelized (following PR #991), multiple test fixtures run concurrently. This heavily increases the likelihood of a race condition where the OS assigns and closes the same ephemeral port to two parallel tests before either subprocess server can bind to it, causing flaky socket collisions and test timeouts. By tracking and temporarily reserving recently returned ports, we eliminate this class of flaky port collisions.

Fixes #959 part(3/4)

items.title: bug(instrumentation/logrus): direct package-level log calls do not inject trace/span IDs
items.body:
### Describe the bug

The compile-time auto-instrumentation for `github.com/sirupsen/logrus` hooks `logrus.New`, `(*Entry).WithField`, and `SetFormatter` to register the OpenTelemetry trace hook on loggers and entries.

However, if an application directly uses the global `logrus` package-level logging functions (e.g., `logrus.Info("message")`, `logrus.Warn(...)`) without calling `New()`, `WithField()`, or `SetFormatter()` beforehand, the package-level `std` standard logger is never registered with the trace hook. Consequently, trace and span IDs are silently missing from all package-level logs even when an active span is present.

### Environment

 - OS: macOS / Linux / Windows
 - Go Version: 1.22+
 - Version: v0.1.0 (main branch)

### To Reproduce

1. Build a Go application using compile-time auto-instrumentation (`otelc`).
2. Write a function that creates a span and writes a log using a package-level function:
   ```go
   ctx, span := tracer.Start(ctx, "my-span")
   defer span.End()
   logrus.Info("Hello, this is a standard log call!")
   ```
3. Run the application.
4. Observe that the log output does not contain the `trace_id` and `span_id` fields.

### Expected behavior

Package-level logging functions (using the global standard logger) should automatically have trace and span IDs injected without requiring manual initialization triggers like `SetFormatter` or `WithField` to be called first.

### Additional context

We can automatically register the trace hook on `logrus.StandardLogger()` inside an `init()` block when the logrus instrumentation module is blank-imported, guaranteeing standard logger coverage out of the box.

items.title: feat(tool/rule): no selector matches a composite literal
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There is no `where` selector that matches a composite (struct) literal, so a value built inline as `&T{...}` cannot be instrumented.

```go
// otelc has no selector that can reach this literal:
// `struct` matches the type declaration, `function_call` matches call
// expressions, and `identifier` matches package-level var/const.
t := &http.Transport{MaxIdleConns: 100}
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A selector that matches composite literals of a given type, and a way to set or override fields on the matched literal.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

`inject_code` with a `pattern` regex, one rule per construction site. It only works when the literal is assigned to a variable, so a literal in a `return`, an argument, or a nested field stays unreachable.

**Additional context**

Instrumentation sometimes needs to distinguish values by *who created them*, and the only place that information exists is the construction site.

Concrete case: a tracer's own HTTP traffic must stay out of the trace, otherwise the request that exports a span produces the next span and an idle application traces itself forever. dd-trace-go handles this with Orchestrion by [adding an `internal` marker field to the `net/http.Transport` struct declaration and setting it to `true` on every `&http.Transport{...}` literal the tracer builds for itself](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/blob/61f964796777d56288cf506113ae3b22877a8aca/contrib/net/http/orchestrion.client.yml#L12-L46). The client instrumentation then skips transports carrying the marker.

otelc can add the field but cannot set it, because there is no `http.NewTransport` to hook and no way to match the literals. The field must be set *only* on the tracer's own transports, so it cannot be done from inside `net/http` where the instrumentation runs, and the transports there are indistinguishable from application ones.

Not covered by the Orchestrion parity checklist in #164 — OP3 lists five join points and struct literals is not one of them.
