items.title: bug(tool): vet fails on cgo packages instrumented with inject_hooks
items.body:
### Describe the bug

When otelc instruments a cgo function with `inject_hooks`, `otelc go test` fails during the normal vet pass:

```text
vet: ...cgo1.go: undefined: HookContext
```

The package compiles successfully. The failure occurs only when vet checks the instrumented cgo source.

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Go Version: 1.25.0
- Version: `main` at `69d47e2`

### To Reproduce

Create this structure:

```text
cgo-vet/
├── answer.go
├── go.mod
├── otel.instrumentation.go
└── instrumentation/
    ├── go.mod
    ├── hooks.go
    └── otelc.yaml
```

Initialize the application and instrumentation modules:

```sh
mkdir -p cgo-vet/instrumentation
cd cgo-vet
go mod init example.com/cgo-vet

cd instrumentation
go mod init example.com/cgo-vet/instrumentation
go get go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/pkg/hook
cd ..

go mod edit -require=example.com/cgo-vet/instrumentation@v0.0.0
go mod edit -replace=example.com/cgo-vet/instrumentation=./instrumentation
```

Create `answer.go`:

```go
package cgovet

/*
static int answer(void) { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

func Answer() int {
	return int(C.answer())
}
```

Create `instrumentation/hooks.go`:

```go
package instrumentation

import "go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/pkg/hook"

func Before(ctx hook.HookContext) {
	_ = ctx
}
```

Create `instrumentation/otelc.yaml`:

```yaml
instrument_cgo:
  target: example.com/cgo-vet
  where:
    func: Answer
  do:
    - inject_hooks:
        before: Before
        path: example.com/cgo-vet/instrumentation
```

Create `otel.instrumentation.go`:

```go
//go:build tools

package tools

import _ "example.com/cgo-vet/instrumentation"
```

Run:

```sh
go mod tidy
CGO_ENABLED=1 otelc go test ./...
```

Vet fails with:

```text
vet: ...cgo1.go: undefined: HookContext
```

The nested instrumentation module matches the layout used by existing instrumentation packages.

### Expected behavior

`otelc go test ./...` completes with the default vet configuration enabled.

### Additional context

Both control commands succeed:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=1 otelc go build ./...
CGO_ENABLED=1 otelc go test -vet=off ./...
```

The Go toolchain passes cgo's generated `.cgo1.go` file to both the compiler and vet. otelc rewrites that file to reference generated declarations such as `HookContext`.

The compiler receives the instrumented cgo file and the generated declarations. Vet receives the instrumented cgo file without those declarations, so it reports `undefined: HookContext`.

This affects cgo-based libraries such as `confluent-kafka-go`.

items.title: Manifest generator accepts invalid rule targets
items.body:
### Description

Manifest generation accepts malformed, non-empty `rule.target` values that are rejected during normal rule loading.

For example:

```yaml
broken:
  target: example.com/[svc
  version: v1.0.0
```

Manifest generation accepts this target and may write it to `instrumentation-manifest.json`.

However, normal rule loading rejects the same target through `rule.ValidateTarget`.

### Expected behavior

Manifest generation should validate non-empty `rule.target` values using the same target validation as normal rule loading and return an error for malformed targets.

### Actual behavior

Manifest generation accepts malformed, non-empty targets and includes them in the generated manifest.

### Proposed fix

Validate non-empty manifest-side `rule.target` values while loading manifest entries, preferably by reusing `rule.ValidateTarget`.

Add focused regression tests covering:

* Rejection of malformed targets
* Acceptance of valid exact targets
* Acceptance of valid glob targets
* Preservation of the existing empty-target omission behavior

The broader shared-validation refactor between setup and manifest loading can remain separate.

items.title: bug(instrumentation/redis): db.query.text captures full command argument values by default, leaking sensitive data
items.body:
### Describe the bug

The Redis (`go-redis/v9`) instrumentation sets `db.query.text` on every client span to the **full, unredacted command, including argument values** — by default, with no opt-in and no way to disable it. This contradicts the OpenTelemetry Redis semantic conventions, which say query text "SHOULD NOT be collected by default unless there is sanitization that excludes sensitive data" (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/db/redis/), and it goes further than the general DB semconv guidance that only *parameterized* query text is safe to collect by default — parameter *values* require explicit opt-in (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/db/sql/).

Redis commands don't separate "query" from "parameters" the way SQL does: the arguments to `SET`, `HSET`, `LPUSH`, etc. *are* the data being written. Capturing them verbatim means every value an application stores in Redis — session tokens, API keys, emails, free-text fields — is copied into every client span and shipped to whatever trace backend is configured, unconditionally.

This is a different, broader problem than #1091 (closed): #1091 fixed the special case of `AUTH`/`HELLO` connection-handshake credentials being leaked. The redaction added for that fix (`redisV9CredentialRedactRange` in `hook.go`) only recognizes the `auth` and `hello` command names — every other command's arguments, including the data values of ordinary write commands, are still serialized in full with no redaction and no way to turn it off.

### Environment

- OS: any (not OS-specific)
- Go Version: 1.25 (repo's `go.mod` minimum)
- Version: main @ `234ca1f`

### Evidence

`instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/semconv/client.go:27-33`:
```go
attrs := []attribute.KeyValue{
    semconv.DBSystemNameRedis,
    semconv.DBOperationName(req.FullName),
    semconv.ServerAddress(host),
    semconv.NetworkTransportTCP,
    semconv.DBQueryText(req.Statement),   // <- always included, unconditionally
}
```

`req.Statement` comes from `getRedisV9Statement` in `instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/hook.go:151-173`, which appends every command argument via `redisV9AppendArg` (`hook.go:219-267`) except the narrow `AUTH`/`HELLO AUTH` range computed by `redisV9CredentialRedactRange` (`hook.go:178-206`) — a switch on only `"auth"` and `"hello"`. There is no config surface (env var, `otelc.yaml` option, code constant) anywhere in the package that gates this — confirmed by grepping the package for `redact`/`sensitive`/`capture`/`config`.

### To Reproduce

```go
rdb := redis.NewClient(&redis.Options{Addr: "localhost:6379"})
rdb.AddHook(newOtelRedisHook(rdb.Options().Addr)) // done automatically by afterNewRedisClientV9

rdb.Set(ctx, "session:42", "s3cret-session-token", 0)
rdb.HSet(ctx, "user:42", "email", "alice@example.com")
```

Inspect the resulting client spans:

```
db.query.text = "set session:42 s3cret-session-token"
db.query.text = "hset user:42 email alice@example.com"
```

Both the session token and the user's email are now stored verbatim in the trace backend, for every `SET`/`HSET`/etc. call an application makes, with no way to prevent it short of not using this instrumentation.

### Expected behavior

`db.query.text` should not contain unredacted argument values by default. It should either be omitted/limited to the command name (and optionally the key) by default with a documented opt-in for full capture, or have values sanitized by default — consistent with the OTel Redis and DB semantic-convention guidance on when raw query text/parameters are safe to collect.

### Root cause

`getRedisV9Statement`/`RedisClientRequestTraceAttrs` treat "redact known credential commands" as equivalent to "safe to capture by default." They are not: the OTel Redis semantic conventions explicitly call for query text to be opt-in / sanitized by default, not blocklist-redacted for two command names. There is no default-off or default-sanitized behavior, and no configuration knob for users who need one.

### Impact

- **Security/privacy**: sensitive data (credentials, tokens, PII, arbitrary application values) is exported to trace backends by default, for every user of this instrumentation, with no indication in the README (there isn't one for this package) that this happens.
- Affects every command whose arguments carry data: `SET`, `SETEX`, `HSET`, `LPUSH`, `RPUSH`, `SADD`, `ZADD`, `GETSET`, `MSET`, pipelines containing any of these, etc. — not an edge case, this is normal Redis usage.
- Violates the semantic convention this instrumentation otherwise claims to implement (`db.query.text` per `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.37.0`).

### Affected components

- `instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/hook.go` (`getRedisV9Statement`, `redisV9CredentialRedactRange`, `ProcessHook`, `ProcessPipelineHook`)
- `instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9/semconv/client.go` (`RedisClientRequestTraceAttrs`)

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `db.query.text` is not populated with full argument values by default — either omitted by default and gated behind explicit opt-in (e.g. an env var consistent with this repo's `OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` conventions), or values are sanitized/redacted by default while the command name and key remain visible (matching how other mature Redis instrumentations approach this).
- [ ] The existing `AUTH`/`HELLO` credential redaction keeps working under whatever default is chosen (no regression of #1091).
- [ ] Behavior is documented (this package currently has no README — add one, or extend the closest existing docs) so users know what is captured by default and how to opt in/out.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: default behavior emits no sensitive argument values for a representative write command (`SET`/`HSET`), and the opt-in/sanitized path (whichever is chosen) is exercised explicitly.

### Suggested solution direction

Do not collect argument values in `db.query.text` by default. Keep the command name (`db.operation.name` already carries this) and, if desired, the key (first argument) — Redis commands are `<CMD> <key> [args...]`, and the key alone is far lower-risk than the values that follow it while still being useful for debugging ("what command touched what key"). Gate full-argument capture behind an explicit opt-in, following the pattern OTel semconv recommends for `db.query.parameter.<key>` (opt-in) versus the query "template" (default-on). This is a bounded, well-scoped change: it touches `getRedisV9Statement`/`redisV9AppendArg` and the enabler/config plumbing already established elsewhere in the repo (`runtime.Instrumented`), plus tests asserting the redacted default and the opt-in path.

items.title: fix(instrumentation/redis): redact command argument values from db.query.text by default
items.body:
## Description

`db.query.text` on Redis client spans captured every command argument verbatim by default, including data values (`SET`'s value, `HSET`'s field/value pairs, `LPUSH`'s elements, etc.). Only `AUTH`/`HELLO` credentials were redacted (#1092/#1101); everything else - session tokens, PII, arbitrary application data - was shipped to the trace backend on every write, with no opt-out.

```go
rdb.Set(ctx, "session:42", "s3cret-session-token", 0)
// db.query.text = "set session:42 s3cret-session-token"
```

This fix redacts command argument values by default, keeping only the command name and (conventionally) the key, matching the OpenTelemetry [Redis semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/db/redis/), which call for query text to be sanitized or opt-in rather than collected by default.

### Root cause

`getRedisV9Statement` redacted only the index range returned by `redisV9CredentialRedactRange`, which matched exclusively on the `auth`/`hello` command names. Every other command fell through to "not redacted."

### Fix

Redis commands don't separate a query template from bindable parameters the way SQL does, so there's no general way to know which argument is safe to show. `redisV9CredentialRedactRange` is renamed to `redisV9RedactRange` (it's no longer only about credentials) and gets a `default` case: for any command other than `auth`/`hello`, redact every argument after `args[1]` (`args[0]` is the command name, `args[1]` is conventionally the key). The existing `AUTH`/`HELLO` rule is unchanged.

This is a conservative, safe-by-default choice with two accepted trade-offs (documented in the code): it over-redacts a few non-sensitive trailing arguments (e.g. `EXPIRE`'s TTL), and for multi-key commands like `MSET` it treats keys past the first as if they were values. Both err toward never leaking a value.

## Motivation

Why is this change needed? What problem does it solve?

Sensitive Redis command values (credentials, tokens, PII, arbitrary application data) were exported to trace backends by default for every user of this instrumentation, for ordinary Redis usage (`SET`, `HSET`, `LPUSH`, ...), not an edge case. This violates the semantic convention this instrumentation otherwise implements.

Fixes #1200.

---

## Testing

- Added `TestGetRedisV9Statement_RedactsCommandValues` (`SET`, `HSET`, `LPUSH`, `GET`, `PING`) and `TestProcessHook_RedactsCommandValues`, the latter exercising the full `ProcessHook` path and asserting the exact reproduction case from #1200 (a session token) never reaches the span.
- Updated existing table tests whose expectations assumed the old unredacted behavior (`SET`, `HSET`, `DEL`, `EXPIRE`, bool args) to the new redacted output; `AUTH`/`HELLO` cases are untouched and still pass.
- Updated `TestRedisClient` (`test/integration/redis_client_test.go`), which asserted the literal leaked value (`"set testkey testvalue"`) - now asserts `"set testkey ?"`.
- `go test ./...` in `instrumentation/github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` and its `semconv` subpackage: pass.
- `go test -tags integration -run TestRedisClient ./integration/...`: pass, building a real `otelc`-instrumented binary against miniredis.
- Ran unit tests across every other `instrumentation/*` module (mirroring `make test-unit/instrumentation`) to confirm the regenerated bundle doesn't affect unrelated packages: all pass.
- `golangci-lint run --config .tools/golangci.yml ./...` inside the redis module: no new findings beyond this package's pre-existing lint debt (unrelated `interface{}`-vs-`any` and `testifylint` style issues that predate this change).
- `go build` / `go vet` for the module and for the `otelc` tool binary: clean.
- `tool/data/otelc-bundle.tgz` regenerated and verified with `git diff --exit-code`, matching CI's `verify-bundle` check (`make` wasn't available in my environment, so I ran the underlying `cp`/`go mod tidy`/bundle-tool steps directly).

## Impact

Default-behavior change: `db.query.text` for write commands (and any command with more than a key argument) no longer contains argument values, only the command name and key. This is a deliberate, spec-aligned fix for a data-leak default. Nothing structural changes (span names, `db.operation.name`, other attributes).

## Checklist

`make` was not available in my environment, so I ran the underlying `go build`/`go vet`/`go test`/`golangci-lint` commands directly, scoped to the changed files/module, rather than the full repo-wide `make lint`/`make test` targets - see Testing above for exactly what ran. `golangci-lint fmt --diff` on every changed file reports no diff, so formatting is checked; I'm leaving lint/test unchecked since I can't claim the full repo-wide targets passed, only their scoped equivalents.

items.title: [Bug]: net/http client instrumentation panics on nil request or nil Request.Header in (*Transport).RoundTrip
items.body:
### Describe the bug

In `instrumentation/net/http/client/client_hook.go`, `BeforeRoundTrip` intercepts `(*http.Transport).RoundTrip(req *http.Request)` but makes two unsafe nil assumptions:
1. `req.Context()` is invoked without checking if `req == nil`, causing an immediate nil-pointer dereference panic if `req` is nil.
2. `propagator.Inject(ctx, propagation.HeaderCarrier(req.Header))` is called directly on `req.Header`. If `req.Header` is `nil` (which is standard and legal in Go when constructing requests like `&http.Request{Method: http.MethodGet, URL: u}` without calling `http.NewRequest`), `HeaderCarrier.Set` attempts `h[key] = []string{value}` on a nil map, causing:
   ```text
   panic: assignment to entry in nil map
   ```
3. `req.URL.String()` in debug logging also panics if `req.URL` is nil.

In standard library Go, calling `(*http.Transport).RoundTrip` with a manually initialized `&http.Request{Method: "GET", URL: u}` and nil `Header` works properly. Compile-time instrumentation should not introduce panics on valid stdlib usage.

### Environment

 - OS: macOS / Linux / Windows
 - Go Version: 1.24+
 - Version: main

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce:
1. Instrument an application using `otelc`.
2. Issue an HTTP request via `http.DefaultTransport.RoundTrip(&http.Request{Method: "GET", URL: u})` with a `nil` `Header`.
3. The hook executes `BeforeRoundTrip`, attempting `propagator.Inject` on `propagation.HeaderCarrier(nil)`.
4. Observe panic: `panic: assignment to entry in nil map`.

### Expected behavior

`BeforeRoundTrip` should safely handle nil `req`, guard `req.URL` in debug logging, and ensure `req.Header` is initialized (`if req.Header == nil { req.Header = make(http.Header) }`) before injecting trace context headers.

- Early returns when `req == nil` before dereferencing `req.Context()`.

- Ensures `req.Header` is initialized before passing to `propagator.Inject(ctx, propagation.HeaderCarrier(req.Header))` to prevent `panic: assignment to entry in nil map`.

items.title: bug(instrumentation/database/sql): spans leak when instrumentation is disabled mid-operation
items.body:
## Describe the bug

The database/sql client instrumentation has the same span-lifecycle issue #1094 fixed for net/http, in a subsystem #1094 did not touch.

A span is created in the before hook and ended in the after hook, but the after path re-checks `Enable()` and returns before ending the span. If instrumentation is enabled when the before hook runs, so the span is created and stored, and then disabled before the after hook runs, the span is never ended and leaks.

The re-check sits in front of `span.End()` in two layers:

- `instrumentEnd` (`instrumentation/database/sql/client.go:633`) starts with `if !clientEnabler.Enable() { return }`, ahead of the `defer span.End()` on the stored span.
- every after hook that ends a span (`afterPingContextInstrumentation`, `afterExecContextInstrumentation`, `afterQueryContextInstrumentation`, `afterTxInstrumentation`, `afterTxCommitInstrumentation`, `afterTxRollbackInstrumentation`, and the rest) starts with the same `if !clientEnabler.Enable() { return }` before delegating to `instrumentEnd`.

Because `Instrumented()` reads `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` fresh on every call, a mid-operation disable skips `span.End()` at both layers.

## Reproduce

1. Enable the db instrumentation and run a before hook (e.g. `beforeExecContextInstrumentation`) so a span is created and stored.
2. Set `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=databasesql`.
3. Run the matching after hook.

The stored span is never ended. This mirrors the net/http case #1094 describes, where `AfterServeHTTP` re-checked enablement before retrieving the span so it never got ended.

## Expected behavior

The after path should end a span created by the before hook regardless of the current enablement state, the same way net/http does after #1094. `instrumentEnd` already guards on the stored data (`ictx.GetData() == nil` and `span == nil`), and the field-injecting after hooks (`afterTxInstrumentation`, `afterConnInstrumentation`) already guard on their stored `GetData()` payload, so the `Enable()` re-check is redundant with guards that are already present.

## Proposed fix

Remove the redundant `if !clientEnabler.Enable() { return }` from `instrumentEnd` and the after hooks, keeping it in the before hooks and `instrumentStart` where span creation is correctly gated. This matches #1094 for net/http.

## Note on testing

Unlike net/http, the database/sql instrumentation does not build standalone (it reads tool-injected fields such as `db.Endpoint`), so it has no hook unit tests today; coverage runs through the e2e db app harness. Happy to send the fix.

items.title: bug(tool/internal/setup): -toolexec flag breaks when otelc's own executable path contains a space
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`buildWithToolexec` builds the `-toolexec` flag by just string-concatenating otelc's own executable path with no quoting:

```go
// tool/internal/setup/setup.go:541-545
execPath, err := os.Executable()
insert := "-toolexec=" + execPath + " toolexec"
```

If `execPath` has a space in it, `go`'s own `-toolexec` parser splits on whitespace and only picks up the first chunk as the executable , so it tries to run something like `C:\Users\...\my` instead of `C:\Users\...\my tool\otelc.exe`. Build just breaks. Any otelc install path with a space in it hits this  `Program Files` on Windows being the obvious one, but any user dir with a space works too.

### Environment

 - OS: Windows 11
 - Go Version: not version-specific, this is about how `cmd/go` parses `-toolexec`, happens on any recent Go
 - Version: v1.0.1 

### To Reproduce

1. Install/run otelc from a path with a space in it, e.g. `C:\Program Files\otelc\otelc.exe`, or just `.../my tool/otelc.exe`
2. Run `otelc go build .` on any module
3. otelc constructs `-toolexec=<path with space> toolexec` and hands it to `go build`
4. `go` truncates at the space and fails

Minimal repro without even needing otelc installed anywhere weird,  just simulating the same flag construction:

```go
func TestToolexecBreaksOnSpacePath(t *testing.T) {
	tempDir := t.TempDir()
	os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(tempDir, "go.mod"), []byte("module testmod\n\ngo 1.22\n"), 0644)
	os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(tempDir, "main.go"), []byte("package main\nfunc main() {}\n"), 0644)

	execPath := filepath.Join(tempDir, "my tool", "otelc.exe")
	insert := "-toolexec=" + execPath + " toolexec"

	cmd := exec.CommandContext(context.Background(), "go", "build", "-n", insert, ".")
	cmd.Dir = tempDir
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	t.Logf("Output:\n%s\nError: %v", string(out), err)
}
```

Output:

```
go: error obtaining buildID for go tool compile: exec: "C:\Users\...\my": executable file not found in %PATH%
```

### Expected behavior

`go build` should run fine regardless of whether otelc's own path has spaces in it,  the `-toolexec` value needs to be quoted so `go` doesn't split it on whitespace.

### Additional context

Fix is to quote `execPath` before it goes into the `-toolexec=` value.

Worth being careful about how it gets quoted though, `strconv.Quote` doesn't work here. `cmd/internal/quoted.Split` does no unescaping inside quotes, it just strips the matching outer pair and takes whatever's inside literally. So a Windows path comes back out with doubled backslashes (`C:\\Program Files\\otelc.exe`) and it's still broken.

The repo already has the right thing for this, `util.QuoteGoflagsToken` in `tool/util/go.go`. It does `quoted.Join` semantics, wraps in `'` or `"` depending on which one isn't already in the token, errors if both are.

Also there's two places building this flag, not one:
- `tool/internal/setup/setup.go:541-545` (`buildWithToolexec`), the CLI case
- `tool/internal/instrument/toolexec.go:472` (`EnableNestedToolexec`), the nested `GOFLAGS` case

The second one already quotes the whole flag for `GOFLAGS`, but `go` splits twice, once on `GOFLAGS` and then again on the `-toolexec` value after stripping the prefix. So the inner `execPath` needs quoting there too, otherwise nested `go list -export` calls break the same way.

One edge case that falls out of this: if the path has a single quote in it, the inner quoting has to use double quotes, and then the nested token has both kinds in it. `GOFLAGS` can't encode that at all since `quoted.Split` has no escape syntax. Erroring out and saying so seems better than emitting a flag `go` will quietly misparse.

items.title: fix(setup): quote the toolexec executable path so spaces survive go's splitting
items.body:
Fixes #1207.

## Root cause

`buildWithToolexec` builds the flag by plain concatenation:

```go
insert := "-toolexec=" + execPath + " toolexec"
```

`cmd/go` splits the `-toolexec` value on whitespace (`internal/quoted`), so an install path with a space — `C:\Program Files\...` on Windows being the obvious case, any user dir with a space works too — makes `go` run only the first chunk, and the build fails with `executable file not found` for the truncated path (the issue's exact repro).

## Fix

Wrap the path in **plain double quotes** — not `strconv.Quote`: go's splitter does not process backslash escapes, so `strconv.Quote` would corrupt Windows paths by doubling every backslash (verified against the splitter semantics; a first draft using `strconv.Quote` produced doubled-backslash tokens). Like `go` itself, values containing a literal double quote cannot be represented.

## Test

`TestToolexecFlagQuotesPathWithSpaces` splits the constructed flag value the way cmd/go's `internal/quoted` does (double-quoted runs are one token) and asserts the executable token is the **whole** path, the ` toolexec` argument survives as its own token, and the unquoted construction demonstrably breaks at the space (pinning the bug).

Package passes with the fix; differential with `setup.go` reverted fails on the broken-split assertions. `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.

items.title: fix(instrumentation/database/sql): end spans when disabled mid-operation
items.body:
## Description

The database/sql client instrumentation had the same span-lifecycle issue #1094 fixed for net/http, in a subsystem #1094 did not touch.

A span is created in the before hook and ended in the after hook, but the after path re-checked `Enable()` and returned before ending the span. Because `Instrumented()` reads `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` fresh on every call, a span created while instrumentation was enabled leaked if instrumentation was disabled before the operation completed.

The redundant re-check sat in front of `span.End()` in two layers:

- `instrumentEnd` started with `if !clientEnabler.Enable() { return }`, ahead of the `defer span.End()` on the stored span.
- every after hook that ends a span started with the same check before delegating to `instrumentEnd`.

This change removes the `Enable()` re-check from the after hooks and `instrumentEnd`, keeping it in the before hooks and `instrumentStart` where span creation is correctly gated. `instrumentEnd` already guards on the stored data (`ictx.GetData() == nil` and the span type assertion), and the field-injecting after hooks (`afterTxInstrumentation`, `afterConnInstrumentation`) already guard on their stored payload, so the re-check was redundant with guards that are already present. A disabled before hook stores nothing, so the after path is a safe no-op; a span that was created is always ended.

This mirrors the net/http fix in #1094, and the same lifecycle principle was reaffirmed by a maintainer on #1137.

## Motivation

A span that is never ended is never exported and holds its resources for the life of the process. Disabling an instrumentation at runtime should stop new spans, not strand in-flight ones.

## Note on testing

The database/sql instrumentation does not build standalone (it reads tool-injected fields such as `db.Endpoint`), so it has no hook unit tests. This change is validated by the existing database/sql e2e apps in CI. The removed re-check is redundant with nil-guards that remain in place, so no behavior changes when instrumentation is enabled throughout an operation.

Fixes #1206

items.title: fix(tool): quote otelc path in -toolexec so spaced paths work
items.body:
## Description

`buildWithToolexec` built the `-toolexec` flag by concatenating otelc's own path in unquoted. `cmd/go` parses the `-toolexec` value with `cmd/internal/quoted.Split`, so an unquoted executable path containing a space was read as a path plus extra arguments. A build run from `C:\Program Files\otelc\otelc.exe` failed with `exec: "C:\Program": executable file not found in %PATH%`.

Added `util.BuildToolexecFlag`, which quotes `execPath` with the existing `QuoteGoflagsToken`, and used it at both construction sites. The nested `GOFLAGS` entry now quotes twice on purpose: the inner quote survives the `-toolexec` value split, the outer one survives the `GOFLAGS` split.

A path containing a single quote leaves both quote kinds in the nested token, which `GOFLAGS` cannot encode since `quoted.Split` has no escape syntax. That case now fails with an error naming the path as the cause rather than silently producing a flag the go command misparses.

## Motivation

Any otelc install path with a space in it hits this, `Program Files` on Windows being the obvious one, but any user directory with a space works too. Build just breaks with a confusing error pointing at a truncated path.

Fixes #1207

items.title: bug(instrumentation/openai): detect SSE content types case-insensitively
items.body:
### Describe the bug

The OpenAI instrumentation identifies streaming responses with:

```go
  strings.HasPrefix(resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), "text/event-stream")
```

This comparison is case-sensitive, although HTTP media types are case-insensitive. A valid SSE response such as `Content-Type: Text/Event-Stream` is therefore treated as a non-streaming response.

This affects the OpenAI Go SDK v1, v2, and v3 instrumentation.

### Environment

  - OS: Windows 11
  - Go Version: go version go1.25.5 windows/amd64
  - Version: current main

### To Reproduce

  1. Build an application using an instrumented OpenAI Go SDK client.
  2. Send a chat-completions request to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that returns an SSE response.
  3. Return an SSE response with this header:
```http
     Content-Type: Text/Event-Stream
```
  4. Read the response as a stream.

The middleware does not recognize the response as streaming because the header value does not start with the lowercase string `text/event-stream`.

### Expected behavior

Any valid `text/event-stream` media type should be recognized as an SSE response regardless of casing, including:

  ```http
  Content-Type: text/event-stream
  Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
  Content-Type: Text/Event-Stream
  ```

The response body should be wrapped by the streaming reader so the span remains open for stream consumption and can record streaming response attributes.

### Additional context

The affected check appears in:

  - `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/middleware.go`
  - `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v2/middleware.go`
  - `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v3/middleware.go`

A small fix would be to parse `Content-Type` with Go’s standard-library `mime.ParseMediaType` and compare the parsed media type case-insensitively. Existing tests cover lowercase `text/event-stream`, but not a mixed-case media type.

### Suggested solution direction

Parse the response Content-Type with Go’s standard-library mime.ParseMediaType instead of checking the raw header with a case-sensitive prefix. Treat the parsed media type as streaming when it equals text/event-stream, while preserving existing handling for parameters such as charset=utf-8.

This is a small, shared change across the OpenAI Go SDK v1, v2, and v3 middleware paths. Add regression coverage for lowercase, parameterized, and mixed-case SSE media types.
items.author: macayu17

items.title: fix(instrumentation): detect SSE content types case-insensitively
items.body:
## Description

The OpenAI (v1/v2/v3) and Anthropic middlewares decided whether a response was an SSE stream with a case-sensitive prefix check:

```go
strings.HasPrefix(resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), "text/event-stream")
```

HTTP media types are case-insensitive (RFC 9110 §8.3.1), and servers behind OpenAI-compatible gateways do send e.g. `Text/Event-Stream; charset=utf-8`. Such responses fell into the non-streaming path: `gen_ai.request.is_stream` was never set and the body was buffered instead of being finalized incrementally by the streaming reader.

## Fix

Parse the header with `mime.ParseMediaType` (which also strips parameters) and compare the resulting media type with `strings.EqualFold`. Applied consistently in:

- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go` (v1)
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v2`
- `instrumentation/github.com/openai/openai-go/v3`
- `instrumentation/github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go`

## Testing

- New integration test in the v1 package sends `Content-Type: Text/Event-Stream; charset=utf-8` and asserts `gen_ai.request.is_stream=true` plus the streamed response attributes — fails on the old prefix check, passes with the fix.
- Table-driven `TestIsSSEContentType` unit tests in all four packages cover mixed case, parameters, `text/event-streamx`, empty, and malformed-parameter headers.
- `go test ./...` passes in all four module directories.

Fixes #1212

items.title: refactor(instrumentation/database/sql): query attributes are rebuilt with avoidable allocations
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Two things in instrumentation/database/sql/semconv/db.go allocate on every
query, and neither needs to.

OperationName only wants the first word of a statement, so it can set
db.operation.name. It gets that word by calling strings.Fields on the whole
statement, which builds a slice holding every token in the query and then uses
element zero. The longer the statement, the bigger the slice that gets thrown
away. On a fairly ordinary join with a where clause and an order by, that is
480 bytes for one word.

DbClientRequestTraceAttrs builds its attribute slice from a literal with five
entries, then appends the server port and the database system name after it.
The literal has room for exactly five, so those appends regrow and copy the
slice on almost every query.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

For the first, cut the trimmed statement at the first space instead of
splitting all of it. strings.TrimSpace and strings.Fields both treat space the
same way, so taking everything up to the first unicode space character gives
the same answer with no slice.

For the second, create the slice with room for all seven entries up front.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Caching operation names by statement. Statements vary too much for that to
  pay off, and it would need a bound to avoid growing forever.
- Leaving the attribute slice alone since one regrow is small. It is small per
  query, but it is on the path every query takes, and asking for the right size
  costs nothing.

**Additional context**

There is a related one I have left out of this to keep it small: the endpoint
is split with net.SplitHostPort and strconv.Atoi on every query, even though it
is fixed when the pool is opened. Parsing it once at open time is a bigger
change across client.go, so I would rather do it separately if it is wanted.

I have this implemented and benchmarked and can open a PR.

items.title: refactor(instrumentation/log): trace id injection allocates six times per log line
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The hook in instrumentation/log/log_hook.go that appends trace_id and span_id
runs on every line written through the standard log package, and it allocates
six times to do it.

It converts the whole line to a string to check whether the trace id is already
present, which copies the line onto the heap. It then builds the suffix with a
strings.Builder, converts that result back into a []byte, and inserts it using
a nested append that first builds the suffix and the line ending into another
temporary slice.

None of that is needed to produce the line it produces.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Search the line as bytes rather than converting it to a string. Build the
suffix in a small array, since trace and span ids have a known width, and put
it in place with slices.Insert.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- A sync.Pool for the suffix buffer. More machinery than a fixed width suffix
  needs, and a pool has its own cost on a path this short.
- Keeping strings.Builder and only fixing the string copy in the check. That is
  the single biggest one, but it leaves four of the six.
- Writing the ids into the line at the point where the line is first built.
  That would mean reaching further into how the log package formats a line,
  which is more invasive than this is worth.

**Additional context**

The behaviour is meant to be identical. The existing tests already cover the
cases that matter here, LF and CRLF endings, an id that is already present, an
empty line, and no trace context, so it should be visible whether a change
holds them.

I have this implemented and benchmarked and can open a PR.

This PR replaces `ex.Fatal(err0)` in the deferred `gzReader.Close()` cleanup inside `extractGZip` (`tool/internal/setup/extract.go`) with silent error handling (`_ = gzReader.Close()`). items.title: bug(tool/internal/ast): ImportAliasMap overwrites map entries on colliding default import aliases
items.body:
### Describe the bug

In `tool/internal/ast/typename.go`, `ImportAliasMap` parses package imports and maps local package identifiers to their full import paths. The docstring notes that it disambiguates:

> *"distinct import paths that happen to share a last path segment (e.g. `text/template` vs `html/template`, both conventionally `template`)"*

However, the implementation currently overwrites existing keys in `aliases` directly:

```
```go
// tool/internal/ast/typename.go:161-179
aliases := make(map[string]string, len(specs))
for _, imp := range specs {
	...
	alias := defaultImportAlias(path)
	if imp.Name != nil {
		alias = imp.Name.Name
	}
	...
	aliases[alias] = path // Overwrites previous entry if alias is identical
}
```



If a source file imports both text/template and html/template without explicit aliases, aliases["template"] will be overwritten by whichever import appears last in file.Imports, discarding the first entry and breaking type matching for that package.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS / Linux / Windows
- Go Version: not version-specific
- Version: main

**To Reproduce**

1. Parse a source file that imports two unaliased packages with identical path tails (e.g., text/template and html/template).
2. Pass the file to ImportAliasMap(file).
3. Notice that aliases["template"] only contains the second package path, overwriting the first.



**Expected behavior**
When multiple unaliased imports collapse to the same default alias, ImportAliasMap should detect the collision and remove the ambiguous alias from the map (unless one of the imports uses an explicit alias).

**Additional context**
Related files:

- tool/internal/ast/typename.go:160-181 (ImportAliasMap)
- tool/internal/ast/typename_test.go:324-360

items.title: bug(tool/internal/setup): go test -exec flag value is parsed as a package target
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`otelc go test` invocations that use the `go test -exec <prog>` flag fail during setup, because the flag's value is misclassified as a package target.

Example:

otelc go test -exec sudo ./...

Setup aborts with an error like:

failed to load packages for patterns sudo ./...

The program name (`sudo`) passed to `-exec` is being loaded as a package pattern instead of being recognized as the value of a test flag.

### Environment

 - OS: any
 - Go Version: 1.25.5
 - Version: current main (7e576e0)

### To Reproduce

1. Run `otelc setup` in any project
2. Run `otelc go test -exec <some-program> ./pkg...`
3. Setup fails with "no required module provides package <some-program>" / "failed to load packages"

Note: the joined form works correctly — `go test -exec=<prog> ./pkg...` succeeds. Only the separated-value form breaks.

### Expected behavior

`-exec` is a documented `go test` flag that takes a separate value argument (like `-run TestX` or `-vet off`). Its value should be skipped when `splitBuildTargets` in `tool/internal/setup/setup.go` scans arguments for package targets.

### Additional context

Root cause: flags in separated form only have their next argument skipped when listed in the `flagsWithPathValues` or `testFlagsWithValues` lookup tables. `-exec` is missing from both tables, so its value falls through to the package classifier and is treated as a build target.

## Description

`parseSnippetFuncDecl` in `tool/internal/instrument/call_template.go` wrapped a source
snippet in `package _\nfunc _() { ... }`, parsed it with `go/parser`, and decorated it into
a `dst.File` to get at the parsed statements. This duplicated `AstParser.ParseSnippet` in
`tool/internal/ast/parser.go`, which does the same wrap/parse/decorate for the same purpose.
`compileExpression` in the same file had its own third copy of this logic inlined.

This PR:

- Replaces `parseGoExpression` and `parseGoTypeExpression`'s use of `parseSnippetFuncDecl`
  with `AstParser.ParseSnippet` directly, and removes `parseSnippetFuncDecl`.
- Replaces `compileExpression`'s inline `go/parser` + `decorator` call with `AstParser.ParseSnippet`.
- Preserves existing error-message behavior: an empty/whitespace-only result still reports
  "function body is empty" (handled explicitly, since `ParseSnippet` would otherwise report
  the less specific "empty source"), and the existing single-expression-statement /
  single-declaration-statement checks are kept.
- As a side effect of routing through `ParseSnippet`, `parseGoExpression` and
  `parseGoTypeExpression` now explicitly reject multi-statement input (e.g. `"a(); b()"`)
  instead of silently keeping only the first statement and discarding the rest — the
  previous implementation never checked for more than one statement at these two call sites.

No behavior change for any existing call site under `tool/internal/instrument`
(`apply_call.go`, `apply_lit.go`, `apply_decl.go`).

## Motivation

Fixes #1223, which asks to deduplicate `parseSnippetFuncDecl` against the existing
`AstParser.ParseSnippet`, and (per the issue's follow-up comment) do the same for the
snippet-parsing code inlined in `compileExpression`.

items.title: bug(instrumentation): linodego and k8s.io/client-go leak spans when disabled mid-operation
items.body:
## Describe the bug

Two more instrumentations have the span-lifecycle bug #1094 fixed for net/http and #1209 fixes for database/sql: an after hook re-checks `Enable()` and returns before ending a span the before hook already created. Because `Instrumented()` reads `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` fresh on every call, a span created while enabled leaks if instrumentation is disabled before the operation completes.

### linode/linodego

- `BeforeDoRequest` starts and stores a span (`hook.go`).
- `AfterDoRequest` (`hook.go`) starts with `if !enabler.Enable() { return }` ahead of retrieving the span and its `defer span.End()`.
- `afterAPICall` (`public_method.go`) has the same shape.

### k8s.io/client-go

- `beforeProcessDeltas` and `beforeProcessDeltasInBatch` start and store a span (`hook.go`).
- `afterProcessDeltas` and `afterProcessDeltasInBatch` start with `if !k8SEnabler.Enable() { return }` ahead of the span retrieval and `defer span.End()`.

In every case the `!ok || span == nil` guard sits after the `Enable()` re-check, so the guard already covers the disabled-at-before case (no span was stored), which makes the `Enable()` re-check redundant with a check that is already present.

## Reproduce

1. Enable the instrumentation and run the before hook so a span is created and stored.
2. Set `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` to that instrumentation.
3. Run the matching after hook.

The stored span is never ended. `k8s.io/client-go`s `TestAfterProcessDeltas` "instrumentation disabled" case already sets this exact scenario up (a span in hook data, env disabled) and currently asserts 0 ended spans, documenting the leak.

## Expected behavior

The after hook should end a span created by the before hook regardless of the current enablement state, matching net/http after #1094. Remove the redundant `Enable()` re-check from the after hooks, keeping it in the before hooks where span creation is correctly gated.

Both packages build and test standalone, so this can carry a mid-operation-disable regression test, like `TestAfterRoundTrip_DisabledAfterStart_Regression` in net/http.

Happy to send the fix.

items.title: fix(instrumentation): end linodego and k8s spans when disabled mid-operation
items.body:
## Description

Two more instrumentations had the span-lifecycle bug #1094 fixed for net/http: an after hook re-checked `Enable()` and returned before ending a span the before hook already created. Because `Instrumented()` reads `OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` fresh on every call, a span created while enabled leaked if instrumentation was disabled before the operation completed.

- **linodego**: `AfterDoRequest` (`hook.go`) and `afterAPICall` (`public_method.go`).
- **k8s.io/client-go**: `afterProcessDeltas` and `afterProcessDeltasInBatch` (`hook.go`).

In every case the `!ok || span == nil` guard sat after the `Enable()` re-check, so the guard already covered the disabled-at-before case (no span stored). This removes the redundant re-check from the after hooks, keeping it in the before hooks where span creation is gated. A disabled before hook stores nothing, so the after path is a safe no-op; a span that was created is always ended.

This mirrors the net/http fix in #1094 and the sibling database/sql fix in #1209.

## Tests

Both packages build and test standalone, so this adds mid-operation-disable regression tests:

- linodego: `TestAfterDoRequest_DisabledAfterStart_Regression`, `TestPublicMethodHooks_DisabledAfterStart_Regression`.
- k8s.io/client-go: the `TestAfterProcessDeltas` and `TestAfterProcessDeltasInBatch` "disabled after span started" cases now assert the span is ended (they previously asserted the leak).

Verified each regression test fails on the pre-fix code and passes with the fix.

items.title: bug(tool): separated-value flags without values pass setup parsing
items.body:
### Description

`splitBuildTargets` skips the argument following recognized separated-value flags such as `-exec`, `-run`, and `-o`, but it does not verify that a value is present before advancing the argument index.

As a result, malformed commands such as:

```text
otelc go test ./pkg -exec
otelc go test ./pkg -run
otelc go build ./pkg -o
```

pass setup argument parsing. Setup may then perform unnecessary package-loading and instrumentation work before the underlying Go command rejects the missing value.

For example, the Go tool reports:

```text
flag needs an argument: -run
```

### Expected behavior

`splitBuildTargets` should return an early, focused error when a recognized separated-value flag is the final argument.

### Proposed fix

* Verify that a following argument exists before incrementing the parser index.
* Return a clear missing-value error when no value is present.
* Add table-driven regression cases to `TestSplitBuildTargets` for trailing `-exec`, `-run`, and `-o`.

items.title: bug(tool/internal/setup): extractGZip calls ex.Fatal inside defer causing abrupt process termination
items.body:
### Describe the bug

In `tool/internal/setup/extract.go` (lines 90-95), `extractGZip()` invokes `ex.Fatal(err0)` within a deferred cleanup function when closing `gzip.Reader`:

```
```go
defer func() {
    err0 = gzReader.Close()
    if err0 != nil {
        ex.Fatal(err0) // Calls os.Exit(1)
    }
}()
```

ex.Fatal executes os.Exit(1), killing the process immediately rather than returning the error up the call stack to the CLI handler or unit test runner.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS / Linux / Windows
- Go Version: 1.22+
- Version: main (latest)

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Call extractGZip() with a reader where gzip.Reader.Close() encounters a stream/close error.
2. The deferred anonymous function catches err0 != nil and executes ex.Fatal(err0).
3. The entire process exits abruptly via os.Exit(1) without returning the error to the caller.

**Expected behavior**
extractGZip() should return the gzip.Reader.Close() error gracefully (e.g. using errors.Join / named error return) so caller functions in setup can handle or report the error properly without unexpected process termination.

**Additional context**
We have prepared a fix for this issue on local branch fix/extract-gzip-fatal-defer by returning a named error parameter and combining gzip.Reader.Close() errors via errors.Join.

items.title: Compile-time performance: several redundant subprocess spawns and re-parsing in the setup/toolexec pipeline
items.body:
I went through the `otelc` setup and toolexec pipeline (`tool/internal/{setup,instrument,pkgload,ast}`) looking for compile-time performance issues, and found a handful of spots where we're doing more subprocess spawning and re-parsing than we need to. None of these are correctness bugs, the tool works fine, but they add real wall-clock time, especially on larger projects and in CI. Opening this to get feedback on priority before I send PRs, since a couple of these touch performance-sensitive code.


1. `pkgload.ResolvePackageName` (`tool/internal/pkgload/pkgload.go`) spawns an uncached `go list` subprocess for every unaliased import, and `imports.FindNew` → `AddToFile` (`tool/internal/imports/imports.go`) end up parsing the same file's imports twice, plus another subprocess per newly-added import in `createSpec`. A file with 15 imports can trigger 30-50 subprocess spawns. Fix: cache by import path and build flags, and pass the already-parsed import mapping from `FindNew` into `AddToFile` instead of re-parsing.

2. `ast.ParseFileFast` (`tool/internal/ast/parser.go`) still runs full `dst.DecorateFile` even though the setup-phase rule matching (`tool/internal/setup/match.go`) only reads the AST and never writes it back. Fix: a read-only matcher over plain `go/ast` for the matching path, saving `dst` decoration for where code actually gets rewritten.

3. `findHookFile` and `getHookFunc` (`tool/internal/instrument/trampoline.go`) re-list and re-parse the hook package directory with zero caching, called once per trampoline and again during `optimizeTJumps`. `materializeTemplate` also re-parses the static `impl.tmpl` string from scratch for every single func rule instead of once.

4. Every `otelc toolexec compile` subprocess (one per package in the build) fully reads and JSON-unmarshals `matched.json` before checking if it even applies, even though most packages in a typical build aren't instrumented. There's already a `// TODO: shared memory across sub-processes is possible` comment acknowledging this.

5. On a project's first `otelc setup`, `findDeps` (a `go build -a -x -n` dry run) runs twice back to back because of how `generatePinnedProjects` intentionally returns an empty result after `syncDeps`. Cold-start only, not per-build, but it adds up in CI without cached state.

6. `resolveRulePaths` (`tool/internal/setup/store.go`) already caches by import path, but still spawns one `go list` subprocess per unique path instead of batching them into one `packages.Load` call per module dir.

7. `generateRuntimePerPackage` regenerates identical import and var AST declarations for every package in the build, even though they only depend on the matched rule set, which stays constant across packages.

8. `findFuncDecl` allocates two throwaway slices per lookup just to return the first match.

9. Bundle extraction re-extracts the embedded tarball on every initial pin with no version check.

10. `applyCallRule` (`tool/internal/instrument/apply_call.go`) walks a file's AST 2-3 times per call rule, and `compileExpression` (`tool/internal/instrument/call_template.go`) re-parses and re-decorates a synthetic wrapper file for every matched call site, even when the replacement template has no dynamic content and would produce identical output each time. Fix: pre-compile static templates into a prototype AST once and `dst.Clone` with node substitution per site.

These are all internal-only changes with no user-facing behavior difference.

items.title: bug(instrumentation/net/http): url.full and url.query export sensitive query parameters unredacted
items.body:
## Describe the bug

The net/http instrumentation exports sensitive query-parameter values verbatim, which the OpenTelemetry URL semantic conventions say should be redacted by default.

- Client spans set `url.full` from `req.URL.String()` (`instrumentation/net/http/semconv/client.go`). The code already strips userinfo (`req.URL.User`), but the query string is included unredacted, so signing keys and tokens in the query survive.
- Server spans set `url.query` directly from `req.URL.RawQuery` (`instrumentation/net/http/semconv/server.go`), with no redaction at all.

The [URL semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/url/) state that query string values for a known set of keys "SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the value `REDACTED`", that key matching "SHOULD be case-sensitive", and that "when a query string value is redacted, the query string key SHOULD still be preserved". The default set is:

- `X-Amz-Signature`
- `X-Amz-Credential`
- `X-Amz-Security-Token`
- `sig`
- `X-Goog-Signature`

These appear in presigned URLs (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage) and OAuth-style flows, so an application that calls a presigned URL through an instrumented `http.Client`, or a server that receives one, ships the signing credential straight to its trace backend today.

## Evidence

`client.go`, url.full construction:
```go
userinfo := req.URL.User
req.URL.User = nil
u = req.URL.String()   // query string still raw, e.g. ...&X-Amz-Signature=<real signature>
req.URL.User = userinfo
```

`server.go`:
```go
if req.URL != nil && req.URL.RawQuery != "" {
    attrs = append(attrs, semconv.URLQuery(req.URL.RawQuery))  // raw, unredacted
}
```

A grep of the package for `redact`/`sensitive`/`scrub` finds only the userinfo handling above; there is no query-parameter redaction anywhere.

## Expected behavior

`url.full` and `url.query` should have the values of the sensitive keys above replaced with `REDACTED`, case-sensitive, with the keys and all other parameters preserved, matching the URL semantic conventions and the behavior of opentelemetry-go-contrib`s otelhttp. For example `?color=blue&sig=abc123` becomes `?color=blue&sig=REDACTED`.

This is net/http only and self-contained; it does not change any other instrumentation. Happy to send the fix, with tests for both the client and server paths.

items.title: bug(instrumentation/openai): streaming spans report gen_ai.usage.* = 0 when the response carries no usage object
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`finalize` in the shared streaming reader always sets `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.total_tokens` on the span. The fields behind them only get assigned in `processChatChunk` and `processCompletionChunk`, and only when a chunk actually carries a `usage` object. When none does, all three sit at zero and get published anyway:

```go
r.span.SetAttributes(
	genAIResponseFinishReasonsKey.StringSlice(r.reasons),
	genAIUsageInputTokensKey.Int64(r.inputTokens),
	genAIUsageOutputTokensKey.Int64(r.outputTokens),
	genAIUsageTotalTokensKey.Int64(r.totalTokens),
)
if r.id != "" {
	r.span.SetAttributes(genAIResponseIDKey.String(r.id))
}
```

The same function already knows how to leave an attribute off when it has no value for it. `gen_ai.response.id` and `gen_ai.response.model` are both guarded that way, a few lines down. The token counts aren't, and those are the ones people add up on a cost dashboard.

v1, v2 and v3 all share this reader, so it affects all three.

### To Reproduce

Worth saying up front that this is the default path, not an edge case. OpenAI doesn't put `usage` in streaming chunks unless the request sets `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`, and nothing in this repo sets it. `grep -rn "include_usage\|stream_options" .` comes back empty, and `parseChatRequest` never looks at either field.

1. Call `client.Chat.Completions.NewStreaming(...)` with default options.
2. The response comes back as `text/event-stream`, so `OtelMiddleware` wraps the body in a `StreamingReader`.
3. None of the chunks carry `usage`.
4. The span ends with all three token counts at 0.

Any OpenAI-compatible gateway that doesn't echo `usage` back hits the same thing.

`TestStreamingReader_EmptyStream` and `TestStreamingReader_CloseBeforeRead` already exercise this path, but they only assert that one span was recorded and never look at its attributes.

### Expected behavior

The three attributes should be left off when no usage object showed up. A zero gets averaged into cost-per-request panels without anyone noticing. A missing attribute is obvious.

The semconv version this repo pins (v1.37.0) has these at `requirement_level: recommended` and describes `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` as the number of prompt tokens *as reported in the usage `prompt_tokens` property of the response*. With no usage property there's nothing to report.

One thing worth being careful about: the check needs to be whether a usage object arrived, not `if tokens > 0`. A response that genuinely reports `completion_tokens: 0` is still a measurement and should be recorded. Guarding on `> 0` just swaps one version of the absent-vs-zero mixup for another.

`gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` has a smaller version of the same problem, since an empty stream publishes an empty slice. Probably worth fixing in the same change.

## Description

`finalize` set `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `total_tokens` on every streaming span, but those fields only get assigned when a chunk carries a `usage` object. When none did, all three were published as zero.

They're now only set when usage actually arrived. `processChatChunk` and `processCompletionChunk` take `usage` as a pointer so an absent object stays distinguishable from one reporting real zeros, and both go through a small `recordUsage` helper. The guard is "did usage arrive" rather than `if tokens > 0`, so a response genuinely reporting `completion_tokens: 0` is still recorded.

Two small things in the same function: `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` is skipped when there are no reasons, and the attributes are built into one slice so the span is touched once instead of four times.

Tests cover a stream with no `usage` field, `"usage":null`, the completion variant, a usage object reporting a real zero, and a partial usage object not erasing earlier counts. The bundle is regenerated because it embeds `instrumentation/`.

OpenAI doesn't send `usage` on a streaming response unless the request sets `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`, and nothing here sets it. So on the default streaming path every span reported zero tokens. A zero gets quietly averaged into cost-per-request dashboards; a missing attribute is visible.

items.title: bug(pkg/runtime): parsed-empty OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS disables all instrumentation
items.body:
## Description:

`pkg/runtime.Instrumented` checks `OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` with a raw `!= ""` test before parsing it. Values that parse to an empty allowlist after trimming and dropping empty entries still activate allowlist mode, so every instrumentation returns `false`.

## Environment:

- OS: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Go Version: go1.26.4 linux/amd64
- Version: `main` at `4873b48`

## Steps to Reproduce:

1. Check out `main` at `4873b48`.
2. From WSL in the repository root, run:
   ```bash
   cat >/tmp/repro-empty-allowlist.go <<'"'"'EOGO'"'"'
   package main

   import (
       "fmt"
       "os"

       runtime "go.opentelemetry.io/otelc/pkg/runtime"
   )

   func main() {
       cases := []struct {
           name string
           val  *string
       }{
           {name: "unset", val: nil},
           {name: "spaces", val: strPtr("   ")},
           {name: "commas", val: strPtr(",, ,")},
           {name: "normal allowlist", val: strPtr("nethttp")},
       }

       for _, tc := range cases {
           os.Unsetenv("OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS")
           os.Unsetenv("OTEL_GO_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS")
           if tc.val != nil {
               _ = os.Setenv("OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS", *tc.val)
           }
           fmt.Printf("%s: env=%q nethttp=%v grpc=%v\n", tc.name, os.Getenv("OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS"), runtime.Instrumented("nethttp"), runtime.Instrumented("grpc"))
       }
   }

   func strPtr(s string) *string { return &s }
   EOGO

   cd pkg/runtime
   go run /tmp/repro-empty-allowlist.go
   ```

## Actual Behavior:

Whitespace-only or commas-only values disable every instrumentation instead of behaving like an empty allowlist input.

Example output:
```text
unset: env="" nethttp=true grpc=true
spaces: env="   " nethttp=false grpc=false
commas: env=",, ," nethttp=false grpc=false
normal allowlist: env="nethttp" nethttp=true grpc=false
```

## Expected Behavior:

Values that parse to an empty allowlist should behave like unset, so whitespace-only or commas-only `OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` should not disable all instrumentations.

## Notes:

This comes from `Instrumented` checking the raw env var before calling `parseInstrumentationList`:

- `enabledList := os.Getenv("OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS")`
- `if enabledList != "" { ... }`

`parseInstrumentationList` already trims whitespace and drops empty elements, so inputs like `"   "` and `",, ,"` become an empty slice after parsing, but allowlist mode stays active.

The current docs describe `OTEL_GO_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS` as a comma-separated allowlist in `docs/configuration.md`, and the existing `pkg/runtime` tests cover case-insensitive names and spaces around valid entries but not parsed-empty inputs.

items.title: fix(instrumentation/net/http): redact sensitive query parameters from url.full and url.query
items.body:
## Description

The net/http instrumentation exported sensitive query-parameter values verbatim. Client spans set `url.full` from `req.URL.String()` and server spans set `url.query` from `req.URL.RawQuery`, both with the query string unredacted. The client path already stripped userinfo, but not the query string, so signing credentials and tokens carried in query parameters survived.

The [URL semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/url/) name a default set of query parameter keys whose values SHOULD be redacted and replaced with `REDACTED`, with case-sensitive key matching and the key preserved. These appear in presigned URLs (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage) and similar flows, so an application calling a presigned URL through an instrumented client, or a server receiving one, shipped the signing credential to its trace backend today.

This change adds a `redactQuery` helper in the shared semconv `util.go` that replaces the values of the sensitive keys with `REDACTED` while preserving key order and every other parameter, and applies it to both `url.full` (client) and `url.query` (server). A query string with no sensitive keys is returned unchanged, so the common path allocates nothing.

Redacted keys, matching the conventions: `X-Amz-Signature`, `X-Amz-Credential`, `X-Amz-Security-Token`, `sig`, `X-Goog-Signature`.

Example: `?color=blue&sig=abc123` becomes `?color=blue&sig=REDACTED`.

## Motivation

Credentials and tokens in query strings should not be copied into spans and shipped to trace backends by default. This aligns net/http with the URL semantic conventions and with opentelemetry-go-contrib's otelhttp, and it is self-contained to net/http (no other instrumentation changes).

## Tests

- `TestRedactQuery` covers each sensitive key, non-sensitive preservation, key-order preservation, case-sensitivity, bare keys, empty values, and repeated keys.
- `TestHTTPClientRequestTraceAttrs` and `TestHTTPServerRequestTraceAttrs` gain cases asserting `url.full` and `url.query` are redacted end to end.

Fixes #1243

items.title: fix(tool/internal/ast): match parenthesized receivers and stop aborting on unrecognized ones
items.body:
## Description

This is the consolidated fix for #766 discussed on the issue: instead of handling one receiver shape at a time, it recognizes the reachable parenthesized forms and makes the matcher degrade to no match on anything still unrecognized, in one place.

`stripGenericTypes` recognized plain, pointer, and generic receivers, but returned `""` for parenthesized forms like `(r (T))`, `(r (*T))`, and `*(T)`. These compile (verified on go1.25) and appear in unformatted dependency source, which is what otelc parses out of the module cache. `findFuncDecl` then treated an empty result as `util.Unimplemented`, an `ex.Fatalf` that ended the user's whole build over a receiver an unrelated rule was not even targeting.

Two changes in `tool/internal/ast/shared.go`:

1. `stripGenericTypes` now recurses through `StarExpr` and has a `ParenExpr` case, so `(r (T))`, `(r (*T))`, `(r (G[P]))`, and `*(T)` resolve to the same base type name as their unparenthesized equivalents. Existing behavior for plain, pointer, and generic receivers is unchanged (pinned by `TestStripGenericTypes`).
2. `findFuncDecl` returns no match instead of calling `util.Unimplemented` when a shape is still unrecognized. A receiver the matcher does not understand is one the rule is not selecting, so it should not end the build.

Together this covers the parenthesized forms (the reachable gap), the qualified receiver named in #766 (which does not compile and so only ever comes from non-building source), and any future shape, without a branch per shape. It supersedes the shape-specific approaches in #786 and #1230.

## Tests

- `TestStripGenericTypes` gains the parenthesized value, pointer, generic, and pointer-to-parenthesized cases, plus pointer-to-unrecognized yielding empty.
- `TestFindFuncDeclParenthesizedReceiver` asserts `(r (T))` and `(r (*T))` now match their base type end to end.
- `TestFindFuncDeclUnrecognizedReceiverNoMatch` asserts an unrecognized receiver is a no match rather than a build abort.

Fixes #766

## Summary

Per [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md), E2E tests spin up **multiple instrumented processes** and assert one coherent trace.

HTTP→OpenAI non-streaming e2e already landed (#1107 / #1120):

- Combo app: `test/apps/httpserveropenaiclient`
- File: `test/e2e/httpserver_openaiclient_test.go`
- Asserts HTTP client → HTTP server → GenAI client (`gen_ai.system=openai`) for a non-streaming chat completion

OpenAI **streaming** is only covered beside the instrumentation package today (e.g. `TestOtelMiddleware_StreamingResponse` / `internal/streaming` unit tests). It is **not** exercised by:

- `test/integration/openai_client_test.go` (non-streaming only)
- `test/e2e/httpserver_openaiclient_test.go` (non-streaming only)
- `test/apps/openaiclient` / `httpserveropenaiclient` (no streaming path)

So we never verify that a streaming GenAI span (`gen_ai.request.is_stream=true`, usage/finish_reason after SSE finalize) stays correctly parented under an upstream instrumented HTTP server in a multi-process build.

## Proposed work

Extend the existing HTTP→OpenAI e2e path for streaming (prefer reusing apps over new ones):

1. Add a `-stream` (or similar) flag to `test/apps/httpserveropenaiclient` so `/hello` can call streaming chat completion and fully consume the SSE body
2. Extend the mock OpenAI server used by the e2e test to serve `text/event-stream` with a minimal chat completion stream (including a final usage chunk + `[DONE]`, matching the middleware unit-test shape)
3. Add `test/e2e/httpserver_openaiclient_stream_test.go` (or a streaming subtest) that:
   - `BuildAndStart("httpserveropenaiclient", ..., "-stream")`
   - `BuildAndRun("httpclient", ...)`
   - `f.WaitForSpans(3)`
   - Asserts **one** trace with **3** spans: HTTP client → HTTP server → GenAI client
   - Pins `http.response.status_code=200`, `gen_ai.system=openai`, and `gen_ai.request.is_stream=true`
   - Keeps full `gen_ai.*` detail in existing package/unit coverage
4. No new instrumentation — OpenAI streaming middleware already exists

### Out of scope
- Shared GenAI adapter / new providers (orthogonal to #709 mentorship design work)
- Anthropic streaming instrumentation (#679 follow-up; Anthropic middleware still pass-through for streams)
- Opt-in message content capture

items.title: feat: Support top-level `version` (min otelc version) field in `otelc.yaml` and define multi-file behavior
items.body:
## Description
As brought up during the migration to the contrib repo (see open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-contrib#5), we need a way to specify the required `otelc` version in our `otelc.yaml` rule files. Adding a top-level `version` field (representing the **minimum `otelc` version** required) will allow us to evolve the compiler capabilities and schemas safely without breaking older environments.

Currently, the `otelc.yaml` file structure defines rules directly at the root level (where keys are rule names). Adding a `version` field will require updating the schema parser (either by reserving the `version` key or wrapping rules under a `rules:` block).

Additionally, since an instrumentation package is allowed to have multiple rule files (e.g., `otelc.yaml`, `http.otelc.yaml`, `client.otelc.yaml`), we need to define the semantics of this version requirement across these files.

## Open Questions / Design Decisions
1. **Schema Structure:** Should we reserve `version` as a special top-level key (meaning no rule can be named `version`), or should we change the schema to require a `rules:` block?
   ```yaml
   # Option A (Reserved key)
   version: "v1.1.0"
   my_rule_1:
     target: ...
   
   # Option B (Nested block)
   version: "v1.1.0"
   rules:
     my_rule_1:
       target: ...
   ```
2. **Multi-file versioning:** If a package contains multiple `*.otelc.yaml` files, how is the minimum version evaluated?
   - Is the version parsed **per-file**?
   - Or must all files in a package share the same version? If so, must they all declare it, or can a primary `otelc.yaml` declare the version for the entire package?
3. **Default behavior:** If a rule file does not contain a `version` field, what is the fallback behavior? (e.g., assume an older version, or throw a validation error?)

## Tasks
- [ ] Agree on the schema structure for the `version` field.
- [ ] Define and document the behavior for multiple `*.otelc.yaml` files in a single package.
- [ ] Update the `otelc.yaml` schema parser and validation logic to support the new field and check it against the running compiler version.
- [ ] Update all existing `otelc.yaml` files in the repository to include the version field.

items.title: refactor(tool/internal/setup): batch resolveRulePaths into one call per module dir
items.body:
Item 6 from #1242.

resolveRulePaths was calling packages.Load once per import path referenced by matched rules, in a loop. Now it collects all the unique paths up front and does one batched packages.Load call per module dir instead.

Benchmarked with 15 distinct hook paths in one module dir: 3.08s before, 246ms after, about 12.5x. Added a test with two distinct paths to cover the batching (the old test only had one path used by two rules, so it never actually exercised more than one path at a time).
items.author: darkraider01

items.title: refactor(tool/internal/instrument): stop re-parsing hook files and the trampoline template
items.body:
Item 3 from #1242.

Two things were getting re-parsed for no reason:

getHookFunc re-scanned and re-parsed the whole hook directory for every rule, with no caching at all. First pass at this cached by {resolved path, hook name}, but that only helped when the exact same rule got looked up twice (it's called once building the trampoline, once in optimizeTJumps). Real instrumentation packages don't work that way, database/sql alone has ~18 rules that all point at the same hook file with different hook names, so that cache barely did anything. Switched to caching the parsed file itself, keyed by path, so any rule sharing a file only pays for the parse once.

materializeTemplate re-parsed the same static impl.tmpl string from scratch on every func rule. Now it's parsed once per process and cloned per use (has to be cloned, not shared directly, since the caller mutates names on the clone to make each trampoline unique). Checked first whether cloning is actually cheaper than reparsing since that wasn't obvious, it is, about 14x (82µs vs 1.18ms in a quick benchmark).

Added a test that corrupts the hook file after the first lookup and confirms a second lookup for a different rule sharing that file still works, which only passes if it's served from the cache.

items.title: Optimization: Remove unused HookContextImpl methods when After hook is absent
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
During the instrumentation optimization phase in `optimizeTJumps()`, the `otelc` tool removes the generated calls to the `After` trampoline if a rule doesn't define an `After` hook (`rule.After == ""`). However, there is an unresolved `TODO` to also remove the corresponding `HookContextImpl` methods (such as `SetReturnVal` and `GetReturnVal`) that are only relevant when an `After` hook is executed. By leaving these methods in the generated `HookContextImpl` type for every instrumented function that lacks an `After` hook, we increase the size of the injected AST, which leads to unnecessary compilation overhead and slightly larger final binaries.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Extend `optimizeTJumps()` to locate the `HookContextImpl` type declaration associated with the trampoline. When `rule.After == ""` is true, the tool should actively remove the AST nodes for methods like `SetReturnVal` and `GetReturnVal`. This will keep the generated hook context as lean as possible and resolve the pending technical debt.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative is leaving it as-is (the current behavior), which doesn't break functionality but leaves technical debt and incurs a slight performance penalty during compilation due to serializing/compiling unused AST nodes.

**Additional context**
Code pointer: `tool/internal/instrument/optimize.go` inside `func (ip *instrumentPhase) optimizeTJumps() error` (around line 367)

```go
// TODO: Remove corresponding HookContextImpl methods
removedOnExit := false
rule := tjump.rule
if rule.After == "" {
```

items.title: chore(ci): keep golangci-lint version in sync with .tools/go.mod
items.body:
### Describe the bug
CI and local golangci-lint versions have drifted. Local `make lint/go` builds golangci-lint from `.tools/go.mod` (v2.12.2). CI pins a separate, hardcoded version in `.github/workflows/lint-golang.yaml` (v2.11.3) via a `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION` env var, with an existing TODO:

```yaml
# lint-golang.yaml — Lines 11-12
# TODO: Configure dependabot or renovate to update this version.
GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION: v2.11.3
```

Renovate already bumps `.tools/go.mod`, but `.github/**` is disabled in `.github/renovate.json5` (actions are ratchet-pinned), so the workflow env var never tracks the tools module. The path filter also omits `.tools/go.mod` / `.tools/go.sum`, so a tools-only bump doesn't even re-run lint. Net result: CI and local lint can disagree.

### Environment
- OS: N/A (CI/tooling issue, not platform-specific)
- Go Version: N/A
- Version: `.tools/go.mod` golangci-lint v2.12.2 vs CI-pinned v2.11.3

### To Reproduce
1. Bump `.tools/go.mod` to a newer golangci-lint version (Renovate does this automatically)
2. Run `make lint/go` locally — it builds/uses the new version
3. Push and let `.github/workflows/lint-golang.yaml` run — it still uses the stale `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION` pin
4. See version mismatch between local and CI lint results

### Expected behavior
CI should read the golangci-lint version from `.tools/go.mod` (the same source of truth local builds use) instead of a separately hardcoded env var, so the two never drift. A tools-only version bump should also trigger the lint workflow via the path filter.

### Additional context
Proposed fix:
1. Drop `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION`.
2. After `setup-go`, read the version from `.tools/go.mod` and pass it to `golangci-lint-action`.
3. Include `.tools/go.mod` / `.tools/go.sum` in the workflow path filter.
4. Remove the TODO.

Suggested workflow change:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-go@4dc6199c7b1a012772edbd06daecab0f50c9053c  # v6.1.0
  with:
    go-version-file: go.mod

- name: Read golangci-lint version
  id: golangci
  run: |
    ver=$(awk '/github\.com\/golangci\/golangci-lint\/v2[[:space:]]+v/ {print $2; exit}' .tools/go.mod)
    if [ -z "$ver" ]; then
      echo "failed to read golangci-lint version from .tools/go.mod" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "version=${ver}"
    echo "version=${ver}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

- name: Generate embedded bundle
  run: make package

- uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@<pinned-sha>  # verify latest release/SHA before use
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.golangci.outputs.version }}
    args: --config .tools/golangci.yml
```

And add these to the `code:` path filter:

```yaml
- '.tools/go.mod'
- '.tools/go.sum'
```

`.tools/golangci.yml` still says "Golden config for golangci-lint v2.11.3" — that can stay as-is; it refers to the upstream golden-config origin, not the installed version.

No CHANGELOG entry needed; this is not user-facing.
